Rationale ARCHIVE_BATCH_010
Problem: Active Docs/AgentLogs and Docs/Tasks contain Batch010 transient evidence mixed by agent and artifact type.
Solution: Move active evidence into Docs/Archive/Batch010 and generate slim grouped collections by first filename token.
Rejected Alternatives: single combined file repeats Batch008/Batch009 bloat and makes LOG/Rationale/Status retrieval slow. Keeping POLISH and instruction text active conflicts with user's explicit 'except CURRENT_BATCH.md' rule.
Scalability potential: Low = active folders stay minimal for weak devices/tools; Middle = prefix grouped retrieval; High = parallel human review of LOG/Rationale/Status groups; Ultra = split parts keep giant signal dumps searchable without loading one monolith.
Hardware Impact: Runtime game impact 0 microseconds. Tooling impact is reduced editor/CLI scan surface in active folders; no profiler claim.
Problem: Combined evidence files can exceed 3MB, especially SignalBus contract audit groups.
Solution: Emit part files with 40-line overlap when slim output crosses threshold.
Rejected Alternatives: Hard truncation loses forensic data; unsplit full files violate user threshold.
Scalability potential: Low = smaller chunks open on cheap machines; Middle/High/Ultra = review can target prefixes and parts.
Hardware Impact: Runtime game impact 0 microseconds. Workstation memory pressure reduced during document review; no measured benchmark.
Problem: Previous combined format wrote file size and write timestamps into every section.
Solution: Section separator only records filename and end filename.
Rejected Alternatives: Batch009 metadata format rejected by current user order.
Scalability potential: Less noisy corpus for search and summarization across all tiers.
Hardware Impact: Runtime game impact 0 microseconds; static document bytes reduced only.
Problem: Concurrent agents recreated SHINOBU files while archive build was running.
Solution: Late-sweep active folders into Batch010 using collision-safe __late suffixes, then rebuild combined manifests.
Rejected Alternatives: overwrite original archived files; leave active clutter.
Scalability potential: preserves forensic sequence without blocking other writers.
Hardware Impact: Runtime game impact 0 microseconds.
Problem: Second concurrent write wave appeared during combined rebuild.
Solution: Moved wave 2 and rebuilt affected LOG/Rationale/Route/Status groups only.
Rejected Alternatives: keep rebuilding full SignalBus dump; block other agents by permissions.
Scalability potential: bounded archive pass under concurrent workspace churn.
Hardware Impact: Runtime game impact 0 microseconds.

Decision 03 - Kinetic Presentation Decoupling
Problem: `PlayerSwimPresentationController` referenced concrete Animation runtime type, forcing Gameplay to know Animation implementation details and risking sibling-domain compile coupling.
Solution: Added `IKineticCharacterPresentationSink` to Core contracts and changed Gameplay to cache that interface. Animation runtime implements interface. Hot publish uses cached interface calls; cold resolution uses `TryGetComponent` only outside hot path.
Rejected Alternatives: direct Animation assembly reference was rejected because it violates compile-wall rule. Reflection and string event routing were rejected because they add runtime fragility and allocation risk.
Scalability potential: Low-tier devices avoid hot-path component lookup. High/Ultra tiers can receive richer presentation data through same interface without gameplay truth coupling.
Hardware Impact: Exact profiler saving not measured. Expected saving is removal of repeated concrete dependency resolution from swim presentation publication; 0 microseconds are claimed as measured.

Decision 04 - Equipment Signal Ambiguity
Problem: Including equipment thermal battery contracts introduced `ToolDepletedSignal` name collision between Gameplay and Tools namespaces.
Solution: Qualified HUD explicit interface and handler signatures with `Hecton8.Gameplay.ToolDepletedSignal`.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing Tools contract from Core would hide real contract identity problem. Renaming either signal would be wider API change outside this pass.
Scalability potential: No runtime performance change. Compile identity is explicit and deterministic.
Hardware Impact: 0 measured microseconds.
Evidence: `Assets/_Project/Scripts/UI/SuitHUDV4CanvasOverlay.cs`.
Decision 05 - GlobalSignals Compile Defects
Problem: `GlobalSignals` passed `NativeArray` indexer result as `in`, which is illegal because indexer returns value copy. Weather compatibility path also referenced missing quality byte encoder.
Solution: Copied snapshot entry to local before comparison and added local `EncodeSignalQualityWeightByte(float)` helper.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing compatibility path would break stale generated consumers. Boxing or managed comparer paths were rejected because this is signal infrastructure.
Scalability potential: Keeps deterministic snapshot logic allocation-free. Low-tier devices preserve cheap byte signal compatibility; high-tier systems can still consume normalized float quality where available.
Hardware Impact: Exact microseconds not measured. Expected gain is compile recovery and no GC introduction; 0 measured microseconds claimed.

Problem: generated-project build graph still referenced older `IJobAdmissionController` and `ISimulationBucketer` method shapes that consumed byte quality, while current standards require continuous `GlobalQualityWeight`.
Solution: Encoded continuous quality once in `SystemDispatcher` only at stale boundary. Added byte overload in `SimulationBucketingContracts` and `ModuloSimulationBucketer` that immediately normalizes back to 0..1 before policy math.
Rejected Alternatives: Changing all domain consumers in one pass was rejected because it would expand outside SHINOBU_02 and risk wider compile wall. Leaving callsite broken would block Core compile diagnostics.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra policy still flows through continuous normalized float inside bucketer. byte bridge is compatibility debt at generated-contract boundary and should be removed when stale binary references are eliminated.
Hardware Impact: One byte encode per dispatch frame; exact cost not measured and expected to be below profiler noise. 0 measured microseconds claimed.

===== FILE: Rationale_SHINOBU_100.md =====
SHINOBU_100 Rationale
Date: 2026-05-19
Agent: SHINOBU_100
Evidence class: STATIC_SOURCE until Unity compile/import/profiler proof exists.
Decision 00 - Scope Gate
Problem: Batch target requests global elimination of owner-blocked native arrays, but project architecture forbids converting local scratch into global heap without real cross-domain/save/replay/telemetry ownership.
Solution: Apply GlobalDataVault only to persistent AI/Physics state that crosses rollback/save/telemetry/job-owner boundaries. Keep cold local scratch local unless source proves it survives across frames as authority.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected blind replacement of every `NativeArray` token because `GLOBAL_AUTHORITY_SETUP_PLAYBOOK.md` explicitly rejects DataVault buffers for local scratch. Rejected new global surface for absent systems because `GLOBAL_AUTHORITY_BOUNDARIES.md` marks it as merge blocker.
Scalability potential: Low tier avoids DataVault bloat from scratch buffers; Middle tier gets stable generation-checked authoritative buffers; High tier can add denser telemetry and presentation consumers; Ultra tier spends saved simulation cost in `VISUAL_SYNC` without changing gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: Estimated gain on i3/MX350 is avoiding allocator churn and rollback snapshot misses; expected per-frame saving cannot be claimed without profiler/GCMonitor. Static target is sub-100 microseconds per migrated buffer family by removing stale local ownership and generation misses.
Decision 01 - Mandate Selection
Problem: SHINOBU_100 touches memory topology, DTO layout, rollback determinism, execution phases, signals, and crash telemetry.
Solution: Read eight mandates before code: native memory/job protocol, ARM64 layout, zero-GC, AUP determinism, deterministic RNG, execution phases, signal lane segregation, and post-mortem telemetry.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected reading only AGENTS.md because task-specific registry files define current runtime DTO/Vault rules. Rejected broad documentation crawl before source scan because batch requires evidence-based implementation, not report inflation.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior must be continuous through `GlobalQualityWeight`, with authority invariant across tiers.
Hardware Impact: No runtime gain yet. Prevents compile/runtime regressions caused by Pack=1 DTOs, unmanaged lane drift, or hidden hot-path allocations.
Decision 02 - VehicleMotor Vault Migration
Problem: `VehicleMotor` held three local persistent `NativeArray` allocations for headless submarine state and deferred capsule sweep commands/results. This state participates in physics, presentation, and rollback-adjacent movement, but Vault could not snapshot or relocate it.
Solution: Added `BufferID.VehicleMotorSubmarineStates`, `VehicleMotorSweepCommands`, and `VehicleMotorSweepResults`; replaced local allocations with `VaultBufferHandle ` resolution and DataVault buffer locks while scheduled sweep job owns pointers. Teardown now tombstones local handles and clears motor slot instead of freeing owner-local native memory.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected one shared single-element Vault buffer because multiple registered motors would alias same state. Rejected retaining `Dispose(JobHandle)` because DataVault owns lifecycle after migration. Rejected creating per-instance enum IDs because BufferID is global ABI and per-instance enum growth is unbounded.
Scalability potential: Low uses same authority buffer with one command/result slice per registered motor; Middle/High/Ultra can increase visual interpolation and telemetry consumers without adding new authority arrays.
Hardware Impact: Removes three owner-local persistent arrays per active vehicle. On i3/MX350 direct allocation saving is scene-lifetime, not per-frame; expected hot-path gain is stale-handle/rollback safety, not measurable CPU until profiler proof. Estimated avoided allocator/registration overhead per vehicle boot: 80-150 microseconds static estimate.
Decision 03 - DTO Layout And NoAlias
Problem: `VehicleMotor.SubmarineState` used `Pack=1`, and fauna parasite attach DTOs had implicit layout. Burst job arrays in fauna/submarine jobs lacked explicit NoAlias metadata after consolidation into Vault-backed memory.
Solution: Rebuilt `VehicleMotor.SubmarineState` as explicit 112-byte layout, rebuilt `ScheduledSweepState` as explicit 48-byte non-native helper, rebuilt fauna parasite input/result as explicit 80/64-byte DTOs, and added `[NoAlias]` to migrated NativeArray job fields.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected `Pack=1` because ARM64 runtime structs must not trade bytes for misaligned loads. Rejected property wrappers because CS1612 risks stack-copy mutations. Rejected relying on Burst alias analysis because Vault memory co-location makes conservative alias assumptions plausible.
Scalability potential: Low gains predictable aligned loads; Middle/High get SIMD-friendly job fields; Ultra can add richer presentation data outside these authoritative DTOs.
Hardware Impact: Expected gain is reduced copy/alias penalty in Burst jobs. No profiler proof yet. Static estimate: 5-25 microseconds per 5k fauna job batch depending on vectorization and cache pressure.
Decision 04 - Continuous Quality Striding
Problem: `Submarine6DIntegratorJob` used thermal binary low-LOD branch and hard `Frame & 3` cadence. Batch requires continuous `GlobalQualityWeight` consumption.
Solution: Added `GlobalQualityWeight` to job and mapped it to stride 1-4 continuously. Skipped frames run deterministic dead reckoning from last velocity/rotation, keeping presentation motion coherent while reducing expensive solver passes.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected `if (isLowEndHardware)` because binary quality switches are prohibited. Rejected skipping writes completely because renderer/audio would observe frozen truth. Rejected Unity random or wall-clock staggering; phase uses deterministic `Frame + index`.
Scalability potential: Low quality weight approaches stride 4; Middle operates around stride 2-3 under pressure; High/Ultra converge to stride 1 and can spend saved budget in VISUAL_SYNC effects.
Hardware Impact: At quality 0.1, heavy submarine solve cadence drops toward 25% for affected vehicles while dead reckoning remains cheap. Static estimate: saves 10-40 microseconds per 16-vehicle batch depending on active forces; measured proof absent.
Decision 05 - Signal Bridges Without Owner-Local Queues
Problem: SubmarineDynamics owned three persistent `NativeQueue` bridges and AcousticEcho owned one persistent tap queue. These allocations were outside Vault/signal authority and were invisible to rollback/state audit.
Solution: Moved submarine mock flood, mock impact, and cavitation payloads to typed `SignalBus ` lanes. Moved AcousticEcho pending taps into `BufferID.AcousticEchoPendingTaps` as Vault buffer because frame tap buffer is read asynchronously by `EchoTrackingJob` and cannot be reused as producer staging area.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected writing AcousticEcho producers directly into `AcousticEchoFrameTaps` because it races scheduled tracking job. Rejected keeping owner-local queues because they are not snapshot-owned. Rejected introducing new managed list or event because it violates Zero-GC.
Scalability potential: Low tier sheds through SignalBus low-tier capacity and uses one Vault pending tap buffer; Middle tier preserves normal echo density; High/Ultra can raise signal lane limits or add richer acoustic presentation without changing authoritative AI state ownership.
Hardware Impact: Removes four owner-local persistent queues from AI/vehicle physics source. Static runtime gain is allocator/lifecycle safety, not measured frame time. Expected i3/MX350 gain is reduced session memory fragmentation and no per-owner queue drain overhead beyond fixed SignalBus flush.
Decision 06 - Rollback Layout Fence
Problem: Sequential submarine/acoustic DTO layouts left netcode memcpy offsets implicit and platform-dependent enough to fail ARM64 layout mandate.
Solution: Converted changed hot DTOs to `[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit, Size = ...)]` with exact `[FieldOffset]` declarations. Submarine state/control/mass/PID/force/config/telemetry and acoustic tap/hunt/trail/blackbox rows now have stable byte contracts. Submarine and acoustic jobs use deterministic Burst float mode.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected relying on current C# sequential order because future field insertion would silently break rollback snapshots. Rejected `Pack=1` because ARM64 unaligned reads are forbidden.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all share identical authoritative state bytes; only cadence/math changes with `GlobalQualityWeight`, so scalability cannot alter rollback truth.
Hardware Impact: Runtime speedup is not claimed without Burst disassembly/profiler. concrete gain is lower desync risk and aligned, explicit DTO surfaces for blind `UnsafeUtility.MemCpy`.
Decision 07 - Vault Sovereignty Telemetry Ring
Problem: `VaultSovereigntyTelemetryRing` BufferID existed after migration, but no 300-frame SHINOBU_100 ring or dump path wrote evidence for Vault bytes/stride/faults.
Solution: Added explicit 64-byte `VaultSovereigntyTelemetryEntry` and static `VaultSovereigntyTelemetry` writer. `SubmarineDynamicsRuntime` records Vault allocated bytes, arena bytes, block count, stride multiplier, quality weight, frame, source hash, and fault flag. Fatal submarine state also triggers `Docs/AgentLogs/Dump_SHINOBU_100.bin`.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected reporting profiler timings without profiler data. `GenerationMisses` and `MaxMemoryJobUs` are present in ABI but currently written as zero until dispatcher/Vault miss counters are routed.
Scalability potential: Low tier records stride inflation and capacity pressure; Middle/High/Ultra can correlate richer memory jobs and visual overkill with same ring without changing file format.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate under 2 microseconds per record due one Vault array write. Fault dump is cold-path IO only.
Decision 08 - Culling Allocation Boundary (Superseded By Decision 17)
Problem: Static scan still finds `GlobalPhysicsStateManager.Shinobu37PhysicsCulling.cs` owning one `NativeParallelMultiHashMap` spatial hash and two `NativeQueue` lanes.
Solution: Do not rewrite SHINOBU_37 culling spatial hash inside this pass without replacing its query contract and parallel changed-index writer. Mark as remaining dependency boundary for Task 15 instead of pretending global scan is clean.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected blind replacement with `SignalBus` for changed indices because Burst jobs require parallel writer and downstream culling dispatch currently drains queue semantics. Rejected O(n) linear spatial scan as it would buy memory purity by burning frame time.
Scalability potential: Low tier needs cheaper spatial representation, likely Vault bucket arrays plus fixed head/next-index SoA. High/Ultra can keep denser wake candidates, but it still needs one owner and one compaction route.
Hardware Impact: Superseded. Loop 4 migrated three culling containers into Vault-backed SoA/counter buffers; see Decision 17.
Decision 09 - UI Toolkit Vault Facade
Problem: existing Vault X-Ray was IMGUI-only and did not expose `GlobalQualityWeight` stride relationship requested by Task 18.
Solution: Rebuilt `VaultXRayWindow` on UI Toolkit with fixed 256-bar heatmap, allocation/arena/generation labels, fragmentation ratio, and continuous quality-derived stride display. It reuses existing window/menu route instead of adding duplicate editor tool.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected second `VaultSovereigntyWindow` because it would split debugging authority. Rejected per-refresh child allocation by pre-creating heatmap bars once in `CreateGUI`.
Scalability potential: Low tier pressure is visible through stride/fragmentation; Middle/High/Ultra can inspect larger active block maps without changing runtime systems.
Hardware Impact: Editor-only. Runtime impact is 0 microseconds.
Decision 10 - AUP Sector Local32 Compaction
Problem: Vault AUP rows preserved 64-bit sector/local truth, but hot physics and debug consumers still needed stable 32-bit local row so they do not perform broad-world double math in every tight loop.
Solution: Added explicit 64-byte `VaultAupSectorLocal32` and deterministic `VaultAupPrecisionDeltaCompactionJob`. job wraps local offsets across 5000m sector boundary, increments/decrements 64-bit sector IDs, writes local `float3` into hot rows, and keeps rollback truth blit-safe.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected using absolute world floats because 100km coordinates amplify jitter. Rejected running physics directly on `double3` every frame because it burns bandwidth and ALU for data that should be localized once.
Scalability potential: Low tier gets one compact sector-local row per entity with minimal math; Middle/High/Ultra can use same row for denser rendering/debug overlays without changing authoritative AUP storage.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate 6-18 microseconds per 1k active rows on i3/MX350 depending on cache residency. No profiler proof; build blocked by CPU gate.
Decision 11 - Frost Swap-Pop Sweep And 64B Mutation Signal
Problem: Destroyed/despawned Vault hot rows can leave authoritative holes. Presentation systems also need to know when compaction relocates entity index without querying memory manager.
Solution: Added `VaultSovereigntyActiveEntityCount` and `VaultOrphanedPointerSweepJob`. job scans `GlobalQualityWeight`/`stride_aggressiveness` budget, treats zero EntityId or non-finite vectors as tombstones, performs O(1) swap-pop, and emits expanded 64-byte `MemoryAddressShiftSignal` records with old index, new index, entity id, frame, source hash, and compacted count.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected O(n) render-side remaps because presentation must react to signals, not inspect Vault internals. Rejected rewriting SHINOBU_37 culling containers in this pass because that would alter another agent's spatial query contract.
Scalability potential: Low tier collapses toward 64-row minimum Frost budget; Middle scans larger fraction; High/Ultra approaches full active-row sweep. curve is continuous, not low-end boolean.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate 8-35 microseconds per Frost sweep window on i3/MX350 for common active counts; one queue enqueue per moved entity.
Decision 12 - Dispatcher Telemetry Heartbeat
Problem: telemetry ABI existed, but generation-handle misses and memory job cost were not routed from dispatcher, and batch requires 300-frame black box that can survive post-mortem analysis.
Solution: Added `IDataVault.GenerationHandleMissCount`, incremented refresh misses inside `GlobalDataVault.ResolveBuffer`, and routed dispatcher POST_SIMULATION heartbeats into `VaultSovereigntyTelemetry.TryRecord`. Frost memory maintenance updates last measured memory-job microseconds and flags; post-sim heartbeat writes those values every frame. Fatal submarine state still dumps `Docs/AgentLogs/Dump_SHINOBU_100.bin`.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected writing fake profiler numbers. Rejected only recording from subsystem runtimes because generation misses belong to Vault/dispatcher boundary.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all write same 64-byte row. Stride values make thermal memory shedding visible without altering authoritative bytes.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate under 2 microseconds per heartbeat. Dump path is cold IO only.
Decision 13 - Native Scratch CSV Memory Profile
Problem: Designers need to tune Vault budgets and stride curves in Play Mode, but managed full-file reads and `string.Split` would violate Zero-GC hot-path policy.
Solution: Reworked `VaultLegacyBinaryArchaeology.TryApplyMemoryOverridesCsv` to request `VaultMemoryProfileCsvScratch` from DataVault, stream file into native byte spans, hash lower-case ASCII keys with FNV-1a, and mutate `VaultMemoryLayoutConfig` fields including `StrideAggressiveness`. `SystemDispatcher` polls `memory_overrides.csv` on Frost cadence in editor/development builds.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected `File.ReadAllBytes`, regex, `string.Split`, and managed `List<>` staging. Rejected OSHINO-only regeneration because task explicitly asks for live human tuning.
Scalability potential: Low can raise `stride_aggressiveness` to shrink maintenance budgets aggressively; Middle/High can use moderate values; Ultra can hold it low and scan more rows while preserving same data route.
Hardware Impact: Runtime hot path impact is 0 microseconds. Frost/editor polling is bounded by 4096-byte Vault scratch buffer and only parses on changed file ticks.
Decision 14 - Deterministic Editor Visualization
Problem: Memory compaction is invisible unless developer can see contiguous rows and recent swap-pop moves without attaching profiler or mutating simulation state.
Solution: Added editor-only `VaultMemoryGizmoVisualizer`. It reads Vault AUP/hot buffers, reconstructs runtime positions from sector/local coordinates minus floating origin, draws active rows green, and flashes rows yellow when matching `MemoryAddressShiftSignal` snapshot reports swap-pop relocation. `VaultXRayWindow` also moved from managed `List<>` snapshots to fixed 256-row array.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected debug GameObject probes because they create scene state and managed churn. Rejected console logging because it is not spatial and can allocate.
Scalability potential: Low-tier runtime pays nothing because this is `#if UNITY_EDITOR`; High/Ultra developers can raise draw counts for denser inspection without touching runtime systems.
Hardware Impact: Player runtime impact is 0 microseconds. Editor gizmo cost is proportional to drawn rows, capped by serialized `maxDrawn`.
Decision 15 - Cached Vault Dependency Boundary
Problem: DataVault migration that still resolves services from `GlobalRegistry` inside Tick/FixedTick would trade native-memory purity for service-locator stalls and hot-path branch noise.
Solution: Kept migrated runtime files on cached `IDataVault` fields for hot access and verified target Fauna, VehicleMotor, SubmarineDynamics, and AcousticEcho files have no `GlobalRegistry.DataVault/Get/TryGet` calls. Cold fallback now uses `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated`, matching Vault-owned dependency boundary.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected passing `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` through every ref helper because it hides unbounded service lookup behind memory access. Rejected broad service rewrites outside SHINOBU_100 files.
Scalability potential: Low tier avoids repeated dependency lookup overhead; Middle/High/Ultra gain same stable memory route and can layer denser telemetry without changing service ownership.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate 1-2 microseconds avoided per dense hot ref-access burst. No profiler proof due CPU-gated build.
Decision 16 - Core.Memory Compile Wall And BufferID Collision Fix
Problem: Frost sweep initially wrote `MemoryAddressShiftSignal` directly through `SignalBus` from `Hecton8.Core.Memory`. `SignalBus` and `MemoryAddressShiftSignal` are compiled in `Hecton8.Core`, while `Hecton8.Core` already references `Hecton8.Core.Memory`; adding reverse reference would create compile-wall violation. same pass also placed late SHINOBU BufferIDs on 560-565, colliding with existing WristHud IDs.
Solution: Replaced direct SignalBus writer with 64-byte `VaultMemoryAddressShiftRecord` plus Vault-owned count buffer. `VaultOrphanedPointerSweepJob` writes records only; `SystemDispatcher` maps those records into `MemoryAddressShiftSignal` and publishes from Core boundary where dependency is legal. Moved `VaultXRayWindow` to Editor asmdef and `VaultMemoryGizmoVisualizer` to Core diagnostics so editor/debug code can legally use Core-only types. Relocated late SHINOBU BufferIDs to 636-641 and changed `VaultBufferContract.OwnsBufferId` from range math to explicit owner switch.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected adding `Hecton8.Core` as asmdef reference to `Hecton8.Core.Memory`; that would create circular architectural dependency. Rejected leaving duplicate BufferID values because it corrupts one-fact ownership. Rejected moving WristHud IDs because that is another domain's authority.
Scalability potential: Low tier still writes bounded record buffer sized by same continuous Frost sweep budget; Middle/High/Ultra publish denser relocation records without changing data route. Editor visuals remain zero runtime cost.
Hardware Impact: Removes compile-wall risk rather than direct frame-time cost. per-move path is one 64-byte Vault record write and one main-thread signal publish; static cost remains below previous queue enqueue class, with deterministic ownership and no reverse assembly edge.
Decision 17 - SHINOBU_37 Physics Culling Vault Closure
Problem: Static audit still found three persistent owner-local native containers in `GlobalPhysicsStateManager.Shinobu37PhysicsCulling.cs`: `NativeParallelMultiHashMap ` for spatial culling, `NativeQueue ` for changed-state indices, and `NativeQueue ` for targeted wake requests. Keeping them as session allocations violated GlobalDataVault sovereignty target and left rollback-adjacent culling state outside Vault handle generation.
Solution: Replaced multi-hash map with Vault SoA buffers: `ShinobuPhysicsCullingSpatialBucketHeads` (4096 bucket heads), `ShinobuPhysicsCullingSpatialNext` (per-body chain next), and `ShinobuPhysicsCullingSpatialCellHashes` (exact full cell hash, so bucket collisions do not become false spatial hits). Replaced changed-index queue with `ShinobuPhysicsCullingChangedIndices` plus 64-byte `PhysicsCullingCounter64` at `ShinobuPhysicsCullingChangedCount`; Burst writers use `Interlocked.Increment` through `NativeArray ` pointer. Replaced targeted wake queue with existing `ShinobuPhysicsCullingWakeRequestMirror` plus `ShinobuPhysicsCullingWakeRequestCount`. local `VaultBufferBinding ` now caches `IDataVault` and uses `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated` as cold fallback, removing hot `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` service lookup from physics culling buffer access.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected keeping queues under `NativeMemorySentinel` because that preserves owner-local persistent native allocations. Rejected `SignalBus` for changed indices because culling jobs need parallel write target and dispatcher drains indexed body mutations, not fire-and-forget event semantics. Rejected bucket-only hash because it would wake/sleep bodies from unrelated cells on collisions. Rejected reusing 70609-70614 after source scan showed those IDs are reserved by `ShinobuApexBrainVault` constants; physics extension moved to 70630-70635.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same fixed SoA memory and benefit from continuous quality radius shrinkage via `HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight`; Middle uses moderate radii and same O(N + C) candidate path; High/Ultra expand activation radius smoothly and spend saved CPU on denser visual systems. route has no binary tier branch for culling radius.
Hardware Impact: Removes three owner-local persistent native allocations from physics culling partial. Rebuild remains O(N) over active bodies and query is O(C) over nine neighbor buckets plus exact hash checks. Static i3/MX350 gain is reduced allocator fragmentation and queue container overhead; frame-time gain is not claimed without profiler proof. Counter false sharing is addressed by 64-byte explicit layout.
Decision 18 - Boot Prewarm And Test Contract Repair
Problem: SHINOBU_100 maintenance buffers were created lazily when Frost maintenance first ran, and `VaultSurgeryEditTests` still asserted pre-expansion VaultBufferContract values. That created boot/runtime ownership ambiguity and stale CI contract.
Solution: Added `VaultSovereigntyMaintenance.PrewarmBuffers(IDataVault, int)` and called it from `GameBootstrapper.PreallocateDataVaultPrimaryBuffers` using `VaultMemoryLayoutConfig.HotEntityCapacity` with 1024 fallback. prewarm path requests active count, address shift count/records, CSV scratch, telemetry ring, and AUP local32 from DataVault before gameplay maintenance. Editor tests now assert expanded BufferID contract and 8-byte alignment of `VaultAupSectorLocal32`, `VaultSovereigntyTelemetryEntry`, and `VaultMemoryAddressShiftRecord`.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected relying on first Frost tick allocation because it violates boot-phase DataVault request rule. Rejected broad bootstrap refactor because existing preallocation method is narrow owner route. Rejected leaving tests stale because future agents would receive false-negative ABI failures unrelated to their changes.
Scalability potential: Low devices receive bounded default capacities and avoid first-frame allocation spike; Middle/High/Ultra can increase `HotEntityCapacity` through layout config without new C# code.
Hardware Impact: Boot-only allocation route. Expected runtime gain is avoiding first-maintenance allocator stalls; exact microseconds are not claimed without Unity Profiler proof.
Decision 19 - Core Memory Explicit ABI Closure
Problem: post-polish ABI scan still found `LayoutKind.Sequential` on non-generic Core.Memory records and dispatcher black-box DTOs in files touched by Vault route. Even when current sequential order happened to produce aligned sizes, it left future field insertion able to silently alter rollback/black-box byte offsets.
Solution: Converted non-generic Core.Memory records to explicit layouts with unchanged sizes: `BlockDescriptor` 40B, `H8AllocationRecord` 48B, `H8MemoryTelemetryEntry` 64B, `VaultRelocationRecord` 32B, `VaultBufferMeta` 48B, `VaultMemoryBlockSnapshot` 48B, `VaultArenaBlock` 32B, and `MemoryDefragTelemetryEntry` 128B. Also converted touched dispatcher DTOs `CriticalMemoryPressureEvent` 32B and `DispatcherBlackBoxEntry` 64B. Kept `VaultBufferHandle ` and `VaultBufferSlice ` sequential because generic explicit-layout value types are CLR/IL2CPP compile-wall risk; both retain exact `UnsafeUtility.SizeOf` assertions and are handle/view metadata rather than hot authoritative DTO rows.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected forcing explicit layout onto generic handle/view structs because compile-risk in core memory API would be worse than documented handle-layout exception. Rejected expanding field sizes or changing enum underlying types because goal is ABI freezing, not public contract change. Rejected touching AI pathfinding `Pack=1` DTOs inside this decision because those are separate AI ownership lanes with their own binary contracts.
Scalability potential: Low tier gets deterministic, cache-aligned crash/relocation metadata without extra bytes; Middle/High/Ultra can add richer telemetry only by explicit versioned fields, not accidental sequential drift.
Hardware Impact: Runtime microseconds are not claimed. direct value is ARM64-safe documented offsets for memory authority records and prevention of future unaligned insertions. Existing size assertions remain compile/import guard.
Decision 20 - Dispatcher Vault Dependency Cache Closure
Problem: `SystemDispatcher` still had two `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` fallbacks in its memory heartbeat/cache path. They were cold fallbacks, but their presence made static hot-path audits unable to prove that SHINOBU-touched Vault route uses cached dependencies only.
Solution: Replaced both direct fallbacks with cached `_dataVault` plus `GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated`. This keeps route inside Vault ownership boundary and matches migrated VehicleMotor/Physics/Acoustic/Fauna cold fallback pattern.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected retaining registry fallback with comments because audit target is objective source proof, not intent. Rejected broad dispatcher dependency-injection refactor because that would alter unrelated service bootstrap contracts.
Scalability potential: Low tier avoids service-locator branch noise during memory heartbeat; Middle/High/Ultra keep same route while increasing telemetry density or Vault capacities.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate is small, under 1-2 microseconds in cache-miss recovery paths. larger value is compile-wall and audit determinism; no profiler measurement was taken.
Decision 21 - Physics Culling Scratch Vault Closure
Problem: After native container migration, `GlobalPhysicsStateManager.Shinobu37PhysicsCulling.cs` still held two managed byte scratch arrays for CSV and legacy binary hydration plus one managed `int3[]` neighbor-cell scratch. They were cold paths, but they weakened DataVault sovereignty proof and kept configuration IO outside same Vault scratch model used by SHINOBU memory ingestion.
Solution: Added BufferIDs `ShinobuPhysicsCullingCsvScratch` (70636) and `ShinobuPhysicsCullingLegacyRadiiScratch` (70637). CSV and legacy `.h8bin` readers now stream directly into Vault-backed `NativeArray ` spans and parse via `ReadOnlySpan `. 3x3 neighbor scratch array was deleted; spatial candidate gathering now computes nine neighbor cell hashes directly in nested loops.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected leaving managed byte arrays with comments because source proof matters more than intent. Rejected storing neighbor cells in another Vault buffer because fixed nine-element loop is cheaper and has no persistent authority. Rejected replacing `Plane[6]` frustum scratch because Unity's `GeometryUtility.CalculateFrustumPlanes(Camera, Plane[])` requires managed array and this scratch is pre-existing API interop, not rollback state.
Scalability potential: Low tier keeps same fixed 4096B/64B scratch route with no managed array staging; Middle/High can reload tuning without heap churn; Ultra can raise culling richness through existing continuous quality radii without changing scratch ABI.
Hardware Impact: Measured frame savings are not claimed. Static gain is removal of two managed scratch arrays and one candidate-cell array from culling partial, plus direct native-span file hydration. Expected i3/MX350 value is lower GC-audit risk and less cold-path copy pressure; hot-path gain from deleting 9-cell array is negligible but removes persistent managed field.
Decision 22 - Ecosystem Migration Field Vault Closure
Problem: `MigrationDirector` still carried persistent migration vector-field storage outside Vault route. field crosses AI/ecosystem state, scheduled Burst jobs, black-box debugging, and rollback-adjacent sampling, so owner-local H8Memory allocation left DataVault unable to relocate or snapshot authoritative rows.
Solution: Moved front/back migration grids, blood-cloud POI rows, and swarm states into Vault handles `70653..70656`. runtime keeps only non-owning `NativeArray ` views resolved from generation-checked handles, refreshes those views before reads/jobs, locks write-grid and POI buffers while field job owns pointers, and tombstones handles/views on teardown without freeing memory.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected retaining H8Memory owner allocation because it remains outside Vault generation and compaction. Rejected managed list/array bridge because field is read by hot simulation code. Rejected pushing vector field into global service because DataVault buffer IDs already give one owner and one route.
Scalability potential: Low devices use longer cold tick interval, POI stride up to 4, and nearest-cell sampling below low-quality curve; Middle blends toward trilinear reads; High/Ultra use stride 1 and trilinear sampling while preserving same authoritative buffers.
Hardware Impact: Measured frame savings are not claimed. Static low-end gain is fewer POI reads and 7 fewer neighbor cell reads when nearest-cell mode is selected; memory gain is removal of four persistent ecosystem owner allocations. Expected i3/MX350 value is lower allocator pressure and bounded ALU under thermal throttling.
Decision 23 - AI ABI/Burst Cleanup
Problem: Broad AI scans still found ARM64-hostile `Pack=1` DTO declarations and non-synchronous Burst attributes in pathfinding/ambient AI files. Those are outside Core.Memory, but they sit inside user-requested AI target directory and violate same rollback/ARM64 mandates.
Solution: Removed `Pack=1` from touched explicit structs, expanded `NavPortal` from 36B to 40B with explicit tail padding, and changed touched Ambient Biota Burst jobs to synchronous deterministic Burst with `[NoAlias]` NativeArray fields. No sibling assembly reference was added.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected preserving 36B portal stride because it is not 8/16-byte aligned. Rejected Burst `FloatPrecision.Low`/async compile for rollback-sensitive AI state because mandate prioritizes deterministic cross-platform state over speculative speed. Rejected larger pathfinding refactor because this pass only needed ABI/Burst closure.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra share identical path/ambient byte contracts; runtime quality can vary cadence and visual density without changing DTO stride or rollback bytes.
Hardware Impact: Static value is aligned ARM64 loads and safer Burst vectorization metadata. No profiler proof; public `NavPortal` stride change must be validated by Unity import or owning AI agent.
Decision 24 - Buoyancy Force Packet Vault Window
Problem: last broad AI/Physics/Ecosystem native-ownership scan found `PhysicsApplySystem.BuoyancyQueue.cs` owning `NativeQueue (Allocator.Persistent)`. code already reserved force-packet Vault route, but Burst producer still wrote into owner-local queue, and architecture ledger documented that queue as intentional.
Solution: Replaced queue with Vault-backed force-packet window `(BufferID)71621` and reused existing 64-byte `BuoyancyCounterDTO` row at `71630` as atomic packet count. `EvaluateBuoyancyJob` writes packets by `Interlocked.Increment`, `ReduceBuoyancyTelemetryJob` preserves overflow flags, and `PhysicsApplySystem` drains Vault window only after combined solver handle completes. stale ledger and route card were updated to document Vault route.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected keeping `NativeQueue` under sentinel because it preserves owner-local persistent native memory. Rejected `SignalBus` for force packets because this is high-volume single-consumer fixed-step transfer, not fan-out notification. Rejected adding new enum member in `H8Memory` after concurrent buffer ownership churn; `(BufferID)71621` is narrow route constant documented in route card, matching existing casted private buffer patterns.
Scalability potential: Low quality already reduces evaluated buoyancy objects through continuous stride curve; force packet window remains fixed and bounded. Middle/High/Ultra can use more stride-1 evaluations and richer debug force readback without adding another transfer container.
Hardware Impact: Removes one persistent native queue and prewarm loop from physics force transfer. Static cost shifts to one atomic increment per emitted force packet and one sequential main-thread drain over valid packet window. Measured microseconds are not claimed; build is blocked by unrelated external Core missing DTO/namespace errors.
Decision 25 - Target Tree ABI And Burst Law Closure
Problem: After native ownership scans were clean, target-tree ABI/Burst scans still found sequential runtime DTOs and async Burst attributes in AI/Physics/Ecosystem files. `VerletCableDTOs.cs` was largest risk cluster because cable physics DTOs enter NativeArray/job/telemetry/GPU lanes and were still layout-stable only by convention, not by explicit field offsets.
Solution: Converted remaining target-tree runtime DTOs to explicit layout while preserving their existing byte sizes and public field names. largest patch covers `VerletNodeDTO`, `VerletConstraintDTO`, `GpuCableSplinePointDTO`, `GpuCableDrawParamsDTO`, `CableSystemDTO`, `VerletCableTuningDTO`, `CableMaterialDTO`, `SdfSampleDTO`, `MockSDFSampler`, `MockWorldSampler`, `MockWinchSignal`, `MockSubmarineAnchor`, `CableSnappedSignal`, `CableTensionForceDTO`, `CableAabbDTO`, and `VerletCableBlackBoxEntry`. Also converted `TetherVerletTelemetryEntry`, `MockCrushDepthSignal`, and editor-only `HydrodynamicKccLayoutReport`. Updated remaining async Burst attributes in `VerletCableDTOs`, `FaunaGenome64`, `FunnelSmoothingJob`, `MacroSwarmTravelJob`, `EcosystemBalancerJob`, and `FluidMathCore` to synchronous compile; rollback-adjacent simulation jobs use deterministic float mode. Added `[NoAlias]` to changed NativeArray job fields.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected leaving sequential layout because exact size assertions do not freeze offsets under future field insertion. Rejected broad ownership rewrite in tether/cable systems because allocator scan showed no remaining persistent native owner allocation in target trees. Rejected deleting safety-restriction attributes because Apex and Vault write-window jobs already carry justification or require controlled parallel write windows.
Scalability potential: Low devices get stable aligned DTO strides and deterministic kernels without changing visual fidelity. Middle/High/Ultra can increase cable/path/ecosystem density without changing ABI or Burst aliasing assumptions.
Hardware Impact: Measured microseconds are not claimed. Static gains are safer ARM64 loads, prevention of future offset drift, and better Burst alias/devirtualization metadata. Build was not rerun because CPU measured 71.9%, above AGENTS/user build gate.
Decision 26 - Deterministic Frame Source Closure
Problem: After ABI and Burst scans were clean, direct `Time.frameCount` reads remained in target AI/Physics/Ecosystem runtime files. Some were telemetry-only, but `PathFunnelActivePath.LastTouchedFrame`, ecosystem free-ring slots, ecosystem cull events, and physics mock shockwaves are rollback-adjacent state labels. Leaving them tied to Unity wall-frame numbering weakens deterministic replay and makes static audit unable to prove target tree is free of Unity time dependency.
Solution: Added `SignalBus .SnapshotGeneration`, per-lane deterministic generation advanced by dispatcher pre-simulation flush, and moved `FluidFeedbackEvents` snapshot dedupe onto it. Moved path-funnel frame stamping into Vault-resident `PathFunnelRuntimeState.FrameCounter` at explicit offset 48 without changing 64B runtime-state stride. Moved `EcosystemPopulationBalancer` onto local `_simulationFrameCounter` advanced once per `ColdTick`. Moved SHINOBU_37 physics culling telemetry and mock seismic frame stamping onto `_physicsCullingSimulationFrame`.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected exposing new global `SystemDispatcher.CurrentFrame` because that adds wider core surface and currently mirrors Unity frame count internally. Rejected using `Time.frameCount` with comments because source proof matters. Rejected resetting `FluidFeedbackEvents` every flush call because same-snapshot retry paths can duplicate dispatch; `SignalBus .SnapshotGeneration` gives exact snapshot identity with no managed allocation.
Scalability potential: Low devices still get same signal load shedding and snapshot caps; Middle/High/Ultra can raise signal density without changing frame identity. Path-funnel and ecosystem counters advance with simulation cadence, so thermal cadence changes remain deterministic instead of wall-frame dependent.
Hardware Impact: Runtime microseconds are not claimed. Static cost is one integer increment per typed signal-lane pre-simulation flush, one uint increment per path/ecosystem/physics simulation frame, and removal of Unity time reads from target state paths. Build was not run because CPU measured 100%, above AGENTS/user build gate.
Decision 27 - Target Tree Job Fence Closure
Problem: After native ownership, ABI, Burst, and deterministic frame scans were clean, broad AI/Physics/Ecosystem job scans still found direct `.Complete()` and `.Run()` sites. Several were cold bootstrap or shutdown paths, but others were runtime readback/finalization points. Local completion calls weaken dispatcher phase proof and can hide mid-tick stalls behind "small" helper jobs.
Solution: Routed target-tree job reclamation through `DispatcherJobSwap`. Live readbacks use `TryFinalizeCompleted(ref handle)` and keep previous stable snapshot when worker is still running. Shutdown, explicit state mutation, cold boot initialization, mapped GPU upload copy, and deterministic mock hydration use `TryComplete(ref handle, forceComplete: true)` because those paths own blocking boundary and must not leak handles past teardown or unlock mapped buffer before copy job has finished. SHINOBU_37 mock seismic wake no longer schedules and completes immediately; it marks pending wake and schedules Burst wake job into existing physics culling chain, which is later finalized by established culling drain.
Rejected Alternatives: Rejected leaving direct `.Complete()` in "only cold" paths because static enforcement cannot distinguish cold and hot call stacks reliably. Rejected replacing all waits with no-op deferral because mapped buffer uploads and teardown require completed producer before unlock/disposal. Rejected adding new dispatcher API surface because `DispatcherJobSwap` already supplies exact forced/non-blocking split needed for this pass.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep stale-but-valid snapshots when jobs do not finish inside current frame instead of blocking simulation. Middle keeps normal finalization latency. High/Ultra can run denser exosuit, ecosystem, culling, and acoustic jobs without adding local stall points; presentation remains responsible for smoothing through existing dead-reckoning/visual fake routes.
Hardware Impact: Static expected gain is removal of hidden local waits in target runtime paths and better preservation of dispatcher phase budget on i3/MX350-class hardware. Exact microseconds are not claimed without profiler proof. Forced completion remains only at explicit cold/shutdown/mapped-buffer ownership boundaries. Build was not run because CPU measured 100%, above AGENTS/user build gate.

Rejected moving `DispatcherJobSwap` itself because that would create broad churn across World/root systems and increase merge risk.

Rationale_SHINOBU_101
Status: PENDING VERIFICATION
Initial Boundary Decision
Problem: Addressables streaming handle ownership is Echelon 1 memory infrastructure; unmanaged DTOs and release cadence can create global authority routes.
Solution: Limit edits to Addressables/memory infrastructure, native DTO contracts, editor-only tuner surface, and concise docs/logs. Any cross-domain dependency must be through existing registry/interface/vault/signal seams discovered in source.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct references to narrative, VRAM, or homeostasis concrete classes before source proof. That creates compile walls with 20+ concurrent agents.
Scalability potential: Low uses shortest TTL and conservative capacity pressure; Middle keeps normal TTL; High extends residency for backtracking; Ultra uses saved CPU to keep more visual assets resident and reduce visible swaps.
Hardware Impact: Target is avoiding managed dictionary rehash/GC spikes on i3/MX350. Static estimate before source proof: 50-500 us avoided on biome-boundary lookup storms; runtime proof absent.
Mandate Selection
Problem: Task spans Addressables, native memory, Burst jobs, AUP, telemetry, editor tuning.
Solution: Apply selected mandates: STRM asset lifecycle, OPT native jobs, DATA ARM64 layout, OPT zero-GC, MATH AUP, DBG telemetry, ARCH phases, TOOL CSV/editor bridge.
Rejected Alternatives: Reading only AGENTS.md. registry contains task-specific laws for runtime DTO layout, Burst, and designer data bridges that AGENTS.md only summarizes.
Scalability potential: Mandates force continuous quality weight, not binary tiers; release windows and TTL curves must scale from weak devices to Ultra.
Hardware Impact: Mandate compliance prevents hidden GC and unaligned native layout penalties on ARM64/Steam Deck/Quest-class devices. Exact gain pending profiler evidence.
Runtime Storage Rewrite
Problem: Addressables residency used managed hash containers for hot lookup/release bookkeeping. Managed dictionary rehash and queue growth are unacceptable during biome-boundary asset churn.
Solution: Replace hot `Dictionary`/`Queue`/`List` layer in `AssetLifecycleGovernor` with fixed managed arrays for non-blittable `AsyncOperationHandle` storage plus Vault-owned `AddressableHeapHandleMap` open-address table. `AssetHandleMapEntryDTO` is explicit 64-byte layout and mutation goes through `GetEntryAsRef` over Vault memory.
Rejected Alternatives: `NativeHashMap` auto-growth and managed `Dictionary ` were rejected. former can still reallocate; latter keeps GC/rehash risk and pointer-chasing in streaming hot path.
Scalability potential: Low keeps bounded slots and aggressive eviction; Middle retains stable TTL; High/Ultra can raise TTL without changing table shape, preserving no-resize behavior.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate only: avoiding managed dictionary probes/rehash during streaming storms targets roughly 50-500 us jitter reduction on i3/MX350-class CPUs. Profiler proof absent.
Core Buffer ID Boundary
Problem: CSV tuning needed Vault-owned scratch buffer, and SHINOBU_101 had to prove it was not inventing private parser buffer or hijacking another domain's ID.
Solution: Verify existing Core Memory `BufferID.AddressableHeapCsvScratch = 70329` authority and route CSV parsing through that Vault buffer. No SHINOBU_101 edit to `H8Memory.cs` is required for this ID; other dirty `H8Memory.cs` differences in worktree are neighboring-lane changes and were not reverted.
Rejected Alternatives: private `byte[]` or local `NativeArray ` parser buffer was rejected because it violates H-PHI/DataVault ownership. Reusing unrelated buffer ID was rejected because one fact needs one owner.
Scalability potential: Low devices parse designer TTL overrides without managed text allocations; High/Ultra keep same hot-reload route with larger residency windows.
Hardware Impact: Cold/editor parse path only; no steady-frame claim.
TTL, VRAM Panic, and AUP Eviction
Problem: TTL decay must run outside main thread, while panic eviction must avoid unloading assets that were reacquired between evaluation and release.
Solution: `AssetTtlEvaluationJob` is `IJobParallelFor` with Burst synchronous compile flags and `[NoAlias]` fields. It mirrors refcount/TTL into Vault map, subtracts player AUP from asset AUP before casting to `float3`, and applies required continuous TTL curve. VRAM panic now selects furthest 10% of unreferenced, unpinned assets via atomic zero-ref verification before queuing release.
Rejected Alternatives: Marking every unreferenced handle under VRAM panic was rejected because it over-evicts and creates avoidable visible churn. Absolute `Transform.position` scoring was rejected because it violates AUP precision rules.
Scalability potential: Low/thermal quality collapses TTL to 10%; Middle keeps default residency; High/Ultra stretch TTL to 300% and spend saved reload stalls on richer visual residency.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate only: Burst TTL pass moves O(n) decay off main thread; panic selection is O(n*10%) but runs only under OOM-risk pressure where stutter is acceptable. Measured frame cost pending.
Human Control and CSV Bridge
Problem: editor facade used IMGUI/OnGUI and CSV ingest used `File.ReadAllText`, creating avoidable managed strings and failing native scratch requirement.
Solution: Replaced tuner with UI Toolkit, fixed graph element arrays, direct telemetry reads, sliders for TTL/VRAM thresholds, and leak banner display. CSV loading now uses `FileStream.Read(Span )` into Vault buffer `AddressableHeapCsvScratch`, then parses `ReadOnlySpan ` with manual ASCII FNV-1a/float/uint parsing.
Rejected Alternatives: `string.Split`, `Regex`, `File.ReadAllText`, and IMGUI row generation were rejected. They allocate and obscure runtime/editor boundary.
Scalability potential: Low devices consume compact binary/Vault records only; editor cost is isolated. High/Ultra users get live tuning without recompilation or runtime parser allocations.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate only: CSV parser is cold/editor path; runtime benefit is zero hot-path managed allocation from profile reload plumbing. Measured GC proof absent.
Polish Pass: Release Gate and Unsafe Mock Removal
Problem: Static self-review found two architectural defects after first report. `MockChunkLoadSpamJob` wrote same tracker slots from different parallel indices through unsafe pointer, and raw `AsyncOperationHandle` helper overloads called `Addressables.Release` immediately despite being named as blind-frame gate.
Solution: Delete unused mock spam job and its signal DTO; it was not referenced outside `AssetRecord.cs` and did not satisfy SPSC or partitioned-write proof required for unsafe pointer jobs. Add fixed 64-slot detached Addressables release bridge for non-registered handles. only direct `Addressables.Release` source line now sits inside `TryExecuteOrDeferBlindFrameRelease`, which releases only during `IsBlindReleaseFrame()` or VRAM panic; otherwise it stores handle for later gated drain.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `NativeDisableUnsafePtrRestriction` with comment was rejected because job had actual slot aliasing race, not just safety-system false positive. Directly releasing failed-registration handles was rejected because it violated Task 08 under visible frames.
Scalability potential: Low/thermal devices avoid visible-frame release stalls; Middle keeps ordinary release deferral; High/Ultra retain larger cache windows while still honoring same hard release gate.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate only. detached bridge is fixed cold array, so it adds bounded memory and avoids unmanaged dictionary growth or visible-frame release spikes. Measured proof absent.
Polish Pass: Compile-Wall AUP Boundary
Problem: `AssetLifecycleGovernor` used `Hecton8.World` only to call floating-origin helpers for fallback AUP. That created direct source-level sibling-domain smell in Optimization runtime code.
Solution: Remove direct `using Hecton8.World` from governor. Player fallback AUP is reconstructed from `PlayerRuntimePoseSnapshot.Aup` using contract-owned `HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble`. Exact chunk-center AUP stamping remains in `WorldChunkResidencyManager`, which is owner that already knows chunk AUP.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping direct world namespace import was rejected because required fallback can be computed from Core player snapshot contract. Moving chunk-center ownership into Optimization was rejected because it would invert ownership; world domain owns chunk coordinates.
Scalability potential: No visual tier change. This preserves same TTL/eviction math while reducing compile-wall coupling.
Hardware Impact: Static architecture impact only. No frame-time saving claimed; compile graph risk is reduced.
Polish Pass: TTL False-Sharing Boundary
Problem: `AssetTtlEvaluationJob` wrote release bits into `NativeArray trackerFlags` from parallel worker indices. Even with one index per worker, byte lanes colocate many handles on one 64-byte cache line, so adjacent workers can invalidate each other while flipping TTL bits.
Solution: Remove byte flag array from Burst TTL job. Before scheduling, mirror byte flags into already 64-byte `AssetTrackerDTO.Flags` lane while preserving future high `uint` bits. job reads/writes `AssetTrackerDTO.Flags`; completion mirrors low byte back into existing main-thread/editor flag mirror. `_ttlEvaluationFlagsMirrored` guard prevents stale DTO flags from overwriting main-thread mutations when `TryPrepareTrackerMutation()` completes job early. Remove byte flag writes from parallel sanitizer clear job as well; cold byte mirror is cleared sequentially after 64-byte DTO/map clear.
Rejected Alternatives: Padding existing byte buffer was rejected because it would require new Vault DTO and broad API migration. Documenting write as "small" was rejected because mandate is explicit about false sharing. Leaving byte writes in Burst was too fragile for Quest-class cores.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid cache-line ping-pong during TTL collapse. Middle/High/Ultra keep same TTL math and can stretch residency without adding managed state.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate only. Expected gain is removal of worker cache invalidations in 1 Hz TTL pass; exact microseconds require Burst profiler/Unity runtime proof, currently blocked by external Visor/Somatic compile ownership.
Polish Pass: Editor Facade Text Churn
Problem: UI Toolkit tuner had fixed graph elements, but metric labels and tracker rows formatted strings every 250 ms refresh even when values were unchanged. This is editor-only, yet it violated intent of zero-churn facade requirement.
Solution: Add fixed numeric caches for metric labels, leak banner identity, row hashes/refcounts/slots/TTL/flags, and visible-row count. Labels now assign text only on value change; graph bars still use preallocated `VisualElement` arrays.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing UI Toolkit labels with custom text rendering was rejected as unnecessary editor scope. Leaving repeated string concatenation was rejected because change-gating is cheap and keeps facade predictable.
Scalability potential: Low-end editor machines avoid avoidable UI refresh churn; High/Ultra machines get same live telemetry without rebuilding runtime assemblies.
Hardware Impact: Editor-only static estimate. Runtime frame cost unchanged; editor GC churn is reduced to value-change events rather than every scheduled refresh.
Compile Attempt 1 and Import Correction
Problem: first allowed build attempt exposed `AssetRecord.cs` missing `using Unity.Mathematics;` after DTO/job moved `double3`, `float3`, and `math` into that file. same build also failed in unrelated `Visor/HectonVisorUberPostFeature.cs` references to missing reconstruction DTOs.
Solution: Add required `Unity.Mathematics` import to `AssetRecord.cs`. Remove stale unused `Hecton8.SaveSystem` import from `AssetLifecycleGovernor` during compile-wall scan.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating build as purely external was rejected because two errors were in SHINOBU file and had direct import fix. Editing Visor reconstruction feature was rejected as outside Addressables heap defragmenter domain.
Scalability potential: No runtime tier change. This is compile hygiene only.
Hardware Impact: No frame-time claim. Build attempt 2 ran after CPU dropped again and reported no SHINOBU/Optimization errors; remaining compile wall is external Visor/Somatic DTO ownership.
Compile Attempt 2 Boundary

Solution: Treat this as dependency block rather than editing another domain. Remaining errors are missing reconstruction DTOs in `Assets/_Project/Scripts/Visor/HectonVisorUberPostFeature.cs` and missing comfort DTOs in `Assets/_Project/Scripts/Editor/SomaticTunerWindow.cs`.
Rejected Alternatives: Touching Visor or Somatic editor DTO ownership was rejected. It is outside Addressables heap defragmentation and would violate domain boundary without direct cross-domain interface need.

Polish Pass: TTL Map-Entry Iteration
Problem: TTL Burst job was structurally still doing tracker-slot iteration and then probing open-address map to mirror refcount/TTL per tracker. That reintroduced avoidable O(tracker slots * map probe length) pattern inside kernel and contradicted requirement that Vault hash table be bounded lookup surface.
Solution: Reorient `AssetTtlEvaluationJob.Execute` to iterate `AddressableHeapHandleMap` entries directly. Each occupied 64-byte map entry carries pool slot, so job updates `TimeToLiveSeconds[slot]`, `AssetTrackerDTO.Flags`, and map entry itself without inner probe. job now validates `tracker.AssetHash == entry.AssetHash` before touching slot, preventing stale occupied map entries from mutating wrong tracker.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping mirror probe was rejected because it burns probe work inside hot kernel. Iterating only dense tracker array was rejected because map pressure and tombstone state live in map, not in tracker order.
Scalability potential: Low devices reduce TTL kernel ALU/memory traffic under asset churn; Middle/High/Ultra keep same residency curve while spending less CPU on bookkeeping.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate only. Worst-case kernel work drops from tracker count times probe walk to one pass over fixed map. Measured microseconds still blocked by external compile errors.
Polish Pass: Release Queue Idempotence
Problem: fixed pending-release ring and detached raw Addressables handle bridge were bounded, but they accepted duplicate entries. Under repeated callbacks or repeated blocked drains, duplicate entries could consume ring capacity and risk duplicate release attempt.
Solution: Add fixed-ring `Contains(uint)` scan before pending-release enqueue and compare existing detached handles before storing raw handle. No managed dictionary/list is introduced; scans are bounded by fixed capacity and occur only on release staging.
Rejected Alternatives: managed `HashSet` was rejected because it reintroduces heap allocation and resize risk. Ignoring duplicates was rejected because idempotent release ownership must be explicit.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid release queue churn during visible-frame blocks; High/Ultra keep same larger residency behavior without duplicate release risk.
Hardware Impact: Cold-path bounded O(n) scan trades tiny staging cost for preventing queue overflow and duplicate `Addressables.Release` pressure. No measured microseconds claimed.
Polish Pass: Pending Release Ownership
Problem: Several paths set `AssetRecord.PendingRelease = true` before proving fixed release ring accepted key. If ring was full, or if queue-drained release hit scheduled TTL job and could not clear its native slot, record could remain pending without queue owner.
Solution: Tie `PendingRelease` to successful `EnqueuePendingRelease(key)`. If enqueue fails, record stays non-pending and telemetry dumps fault. If native slot clear is blocked after dequeue, key is immediately re-enqueued and only then kept pending.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving pending bit as intent flag was rejected because one fact must have one owner; pending release must be owned by either native flags or release ring, not silent boolean. Growing queue was rejected because fixed capacity is hard memory contract.
Scalability potential: Low devices under visible-frame release blocking avoid silent pending leaks; High/Ultra larger residency windows remain bounded and deterministic.
Hardware Impact: No measured frame claim. This prevents leak accumulation and queue owner loss under pressure.

Polish Pass: Tombstone Defragmentation
Problem: `AddressableHeapHandleMap` pressure counted occupied and tombstone entries, but handler only forced eviction. tombstone-heavy table could remain above 85% pressure threshold and keep triggering eviction without recovering probe length.
Solution: Add `CompactAddressableHandleMap`, no-allocation in-place rebuild. When used+tombstone pressure is high but live occupancy is below threshold, map is cleared and rebuilt from active tracker slots, existing handle-pool bundle prefix hashes, and current native refcounts. Shared-bundle flags are reset during rebuild and re-applied only when multiple active entries share prefix.
Rejected Alternatives: Resizing was rejected because assignment forbids resize under pressure. Allocating temporary NativeList/Dictionary was rejected because persistent memory must remain Vault-owned and fixed. Ignoring tombstones was rejected because it lets linear probing rot over long sessions.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid accumulating probe debt after repeated biome-boundary load/unload churn. High/Ultra keep longer residency without turning tombstones into permanent lookup cost.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate only. Compaction is cold pressure-path O(map + active slots), replacing repeated future probe penalties. Runtime profiler proof remains blocked by external compile failures.

Problem: compaction rebuild re-applied `BundleShared` to map entries, but current slot's byte mirror and 64-byte `AssetTrackerDTO.Flags` could lag until later mirror pass. Existing shared-prefix entries also needed immediate DTO sync when `MarkBundlePrefixShared` mutated their byte flags.
Solution: Make bundle-sharing propagation update all three owners at once: `AssetHandleMapEntryDTO.Flags`, `AddressableHeapTrackerFlags`, and low byte of `AssetTrackerDTO.Flags`. Registration, recompute, and tombstone compaction now pass tracker DTO buffer into `MarkBundlePrefixShared`. Compaction also preserves current TTL value when rebuilding each map entry.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying on next TTL schedule to mirror byte flags was rejected because compaction is state-repair path and must leave map internally consistent before returning. Adding temporary dictionary/list of bundle groups was rejected because rebuild must stay fixed-capacity and Vault-owned.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid repeated reload churn from missed shared-bundle TTL inflation after compaction. Middle/High/Ultra keep longer residency windows while map pressure recovery remains no-allocation.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate only. This prevents state skew that could shorten shared bundle TTL after tombstone cleanup; no measured microseconds claimed. Compile attempt 4 reports no SHINOBU/Optimization errors and remains blocked by external Visor/Somatic DTO ownership.

Problem: Addressables heap telemetry dump still used stale prior-agent filename, which mislabels crash evidence for this agent and breaks owner-local forensic routing.

Compile Attempt 4 Boundary
Problem: compaction signature, bundle-shared mirror propagation, and dump identity changes required fresh compile probe once CPU/dotnet gate opened.
Solution: Ran `dotnet build Hecton8.Core.csproj --no-restore -m:2 /nr:false -v:minimal` only after CPU dropped below 50 and no `dotnet/csc` process was present. Polish Pass: Release Ownership Preflight
Problem: `ExecuteReleaseFlow` cleared native slot ownership and removed managed record after calling `TryExecuteOrDeferBlindFrameRelease(record.AddressableHandle)`, but it ignored `false` return. If visible frame was not blind and fixed detached-release bridge was full, last valid `AsyncOperationHandle` reference could be dropped while actual `Addressables.Release` never executed.
Solution: Add `CanAcceptAddressableRelease(AsyncOperationHandle)` as bounded preflight. release flow now proves handle can either execute immediately in blind/panic frame or fit in detached fixed bridge before clearing native map slot. If bridge cannot accept it, record is preserved and re-owned by fixed pending-release queue. release counter now increments only when handle is released in current blind/panic frame, not when merely staged.
Rejected Alternatives: Growing detached bridge was rejected because capacity contract must stay fixed. Dropping record and relying on telemetry was rejected because that converts full queue into silent Addressables leak.
Scalability potential: Low devices that spend longer outside blind frames keep release ownership without leaking handles. High/Ultra larger residency windows keep same bounded bridge and do not add managed collections.
Hardware Impact: Cold release-path bounded scan over 64 detached slots before native ownership is cleared. No measured frame cost; it prevents lost-handle leaks under release pressure.
Polish Pass: Hard-Reaper Addressables Handle Retry
Problem: hard-reaper `Addressables.CleanBundleCache()` handle used same release helper but also ignored failed defer path. If completed cache-clean handle could not fit in detached bridge, code could clear field and lose handle. first preflight patch preserved handle, but active hard-reaper window had no retry pump.
Solution: Gate completed cache-clean handle release with `CanAcceptAddressableRelease()`. When it cannot be accepted, keep `_hardReaperBundleCacheCleanComplete=false` and leave handle live. While `_hardReaperAsyncWindowActive` is true, `EvaluateHardMemoryReaper` now retries `PurgeAddressableCachesAsync()` and `TryCompleteHardReaperAsyncWindow()` every slow tick. Releasing already completed clean handle now returns immediately instead of starting second cache-clean operation.
Rejected Alternatives: Dropping clean handle on bridge overflow was rejected for same reason as asset handles: one release fact needs one owner. Starting another `CleanBundleCache` after releasing completed handle was rejected because it can create unbounded hard-reaper loop.
Scalability potential: Low devices that have fewer blind frames avoid losing cleanup handles under pressure; higher tiers retain same hard-reaper cadence without extra allocations.
Hardware Impact: Cold hard-reaper path only. Adds one bounded 64-slot preflight scan and retry pump during active cleanup window; no steady-frame cost claimed.
Polish Pass: No-Owner Registration Failure Release
Problem: failed `RegisterAddressableHandleSlot` can happen after `Addressables.LoadAssetAsync` has already returned valid local handle. That handle is not yet owned by Vault map or managed record. Calling normal defer helper and then dropping local variable can leak handle if visible-frame detached bridge is full.
Solution: Add `TryExecuteOrForceAddressableReleaseFault`. It first uses normal blind-frame/deferred helper. If handle has no durable owner and detached bridge refuses it, path raises short external VRAM panic window and releases through same helper under panic semantics. This is restricted to no-owner registration-failure cleanup; normal tracked records still preserve ownership and requeue instead of forcing visible release.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding second overflow bridge was rejected because it creates another owner for same release fact. Dropping handle after telemetry was rejected because it leaks Unity Addressables state. Forcing all tracked release failures was rejected because tracked records can preserve ownership safely.
Scalability potential: Low-memory devices get deterministic leak-prevention escape hatch when fixed release staging is saturated. High/Ultra systems keep normal blind-frame release behavior.
Hardware Impact: Fault path only. cost is one failed bounded bridge scan plus forced release under panic semantics; no normal-frame cost claimed.

Sidecar Audit R7: Release Storage Reset Ownership

Solution: Before Vault cold-clear or handle-array rebind, `EnsureNativeHandleStorage` now proves existing Addressables handles were released through blind-frame/panic gate under forced explicit blind window. `DisposeNativeHandleStorage` returns `bool` and refuses to clear `_assetRecords` if release ownership cannot be discharged. Pool and detached handles are released before records are cleared.
Rejected Alternatives: Clearing native state first was rejected because it destroys only route from asset hash to Unity handle. Growing second overflow owner was rejected because one release fact must have one owner.

Sidecar Audit R7: AUP Metadata and TTL Authority
Problem: Cache-hit and registration paths treated unknown asset AUP as player AUP. That makes unlocalized assets appear artificially close and defeats furthest-first eviction. Burst TTL job also wrote per-slot float TTL mirror, creating adjacent 4-byte writes across worker threads.
Solution: `AssetTrackerDTO` now stores AUP as sector-local fields: three `long` sector coordinates, three `float` local offsets, `MaxResidencyRadiusSq`, `Flags`, and `AupShiftGeneration`, still exactly 64 bytes. New registrations set `AssetTrackerMetaFlags.UnknownAup`; `MarkAddressableAssetAup` converts `double3` into sector/local storage and clears flag. Distance scoring ignores unknown AUP for ordinary TTL decay and treats non-finite known AUP as far for panic selection. `AssetTtlEvaluationJob` now owns TTL in `AssetHandleMapEntryDTO.TimeToLive`; float TTL Vault buffer is mirrored only after job completion for editor/cold readers.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `double3 AssetAup` was rejected after sidecar review because assignment's AUP requirement is better served by explicit sector/local storage without changing 64B cache-line stride. Leaving `TimeToLiveSeconds` as parallel job output was rejected because it creates 4-byte false-sharing risk.
Scalability potential: Low quality uses same smooth TTL collapse but without fake-near AUP protection; high/ultra retain assets longer only when their owner provides truthful AUP metadata.
Hardware Impact: Static estimate only. job removes per-slot float writes from Burst worker path and keeps 64B map-entry stride as TTL authority. Profiler proof is still pending.
Static Verification R7 Boundary
Problem: R7 code changed DTO layout, helper methods, and TTL ownership after compile attempt 5, so verification status had to be reset instead of relying on stale compile evidence.
Solution: Ran static scans for managed collections, forbidden unsafe attributes, `Pack=1`, direct World/SaveSystem using, `OnGUI`, raw `Addressables.Release`, stale `ResolveAssetAup`, and `AssetTtlEvaluationJob` ownership of `TimeToLiveSeconds`. Results: target files contain no forbidden managed collection patterns, no direct World/SaveSystem using, no `Pack=1`, no `OnGUI`, and TTL job section has no `TimeToLiveSeconds`. only `Addressables.Release` source line remains inside gated helper.

Read-Side Dependency Discipline R10
Problem: After TTL authority moved into 64-byte handle map, several read-side paths still resolved tracker/map/TTL views without proving that `_ttlEvaluationHandle` was complete. `WriteHeapTelemetrySample`, `TryGetHeapSanitizerTrackerAt`, and `TryGetHeapSanitizerLeakSuspectAt` could read `AssetTrackerDTO` or `AssetHandleMapEntryDTO` while TTL job was still scheduled.
Solution: Gate those read-side paths through `TryPrepareTrackerMutation()`. If job is still running, they return or skip without blocking. If job has completed, `TryPrepareTrackerMutation()` completes it, mirrors DTO flags and map TTL into editor/cold buffers, releases Vault locks, and only then allows read.
Rejected Alternatives: Calling `JobHandle.Complete()` unconditionally from editor/telemetry paths was rejected because it can stall visible frames. Reading "just for telemetry" during scheduled job was rejected because it violates dependency graph and can observe torn tracker/map state.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid telemetry/editor reads forcing job wait under thermal pressure; high/ultra keep same telemetry visibility after dependency is naturally complete.
Hardware Impact: No measured frame-time claim. change trades skipped stale telemetry/editor rows for no main-thread block and no concurrent read of job-owned buffers.

Result: no `Assets/_Project/Scripts/Optimization/*` errors. build still fails in external owner domains: Gameplay `KineticCharacter`, Visor reconstruction/decal DTOs, Equipment DTOs, Somatic comfort DTOs, World Ecosystem DTOs, plus duplicate `SaveStateMerkleTree.cs`.
