Hardware Impact: At q near 0.1, scheduled solver calls collapse toward 5Hz and one pass. On i3/MX350 this can remove most idle fixed-frame solver dispatches; exact profiler proof pending because CPU gate blocked build.
Telemetry Facade Repair
Problem: Editor bars originally read active compartment DTOs directly, which could alias job-owned buffers and made editor facade less isolated than requested.
Solution: Added Vault buffer `ShinobuFluidCompartmentTelemetry` with 32-byte `FluidCompartmentTelemetryDTO`; summary job writes read-oriented snapshot. Editor reads and tuning writes now return false while `ActiveBurstLockMask` is nonzero.
Rejected Alternatives: Reading live front/back buffers from UI Toolkit, or allocating managed snapshots for editor charts.
Scalability potential: Low tier still writes compact telemetry; high/ultra can draw denser editor diagnostics without touching solver authority.
Hardware Impact: Adds one 32-byte write per active compartment per solved frame. Avoids editor/job data races and keeps runtime hot path allocation-free.
GPU Upload Double Buffer
Problem: single GraphicsBuffer upload path could rewrite buffer still bound as global shader resource and uploaded every render pass even without new solved frame.
Solution: Added /B GraphicsBuffers, dirty flag, and `ResolveNextWaterlineWriteBuffer`. Render upload is skipped while jobs are scheduled or no new waterline DTOs exist.
Rejected Alternatives: Per-material instance edits, per-room mesh planes, or unconditional SetData-style uploads.
Scalability potential: Low tier gets sparse dirty uploads; high/ultra can consume same scalar buffer for more expensive shader waterline noise.
Hardware Impact: Eliminates redundant upload work on frames without solved flood changes. Estimated savings depend on room count; static proof only until profiler is allowed.
Global Authority Route Cards
Problem: domain had real bridges but no route-card proof tying owner, producer phase, consumer phase, payload layout, and failure modes.
Solution: Added route cards for `SHINOBU_119_FLUID_VAULT_STATE`, `SHINOBU_119_FLUID_MASS_SHIFT`, and `SHINOBU_119_FLUID_ACOUSTIC_MUFFLE` in `Docs/ARCHITECTURE/HABITAT_FLUID_INCURSION.md`. They are marked `YELLOW / STATIC PROOF ONLY`.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating chat report as proof or claiming profiler/import verification without running it.
Scalability potential: Cards document low/middle/high/ultra behavior and identify required profiler/GC/runtime proof.

Build Wall Handling
Problem: CPU-gated `dotnet build Hecton8.Core.csproj` ran once when CPU reported 36. build failed on cross-agent/pre-existing missing symbols and one generated-project visibility error for new flood muffle payload.

Decision 001 - Implementation Boundary
Problem: assignment targets volumetric particulate fog, but repository already contains separate noir depth fog, half-res volumetric light, abyssal flow, and GPU marine snow systems.
Solution: Add dedicated RenderGraph compute facade for volumetric particulate fog that consumes existing abyssal flow globals and MarineSnow fog-density texture instead of rewriting those owners. This matches presentation-layer mandate and keeps system in VISUAL_SYNC.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing HectonMarineSnowRenderer or VolumetricLightFeature would couple unrelated domains and risk breaking existing GPU particle/wake work. CPU fluid simulation is rejected by Dear Lie and frame-time mandates.
Scalability potential: Low uses dithered analytic fog with minimal steps; middle uses reduced-resolution short raymarch; high uses more steps and flow/noise; ultra allows up to 64 steps and extra scattering samples.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids CPU particle truth and per-frame RT allocation; expected gain is avoiding Shuriken/CPU-fluid path, exact microseconds PENDING VERIFICATION.
Decision 002 - Registry and Evidence
Problem: AGENTS.md requires status and rationale files before recording completion, and repo has no prior SHINOBU_120 state.
Solution: Create explicit status and rationale files and keep task checkboxes tied to verifiable implementation evidence. Unknown metrics remain PENDING VERIFICATION.
Rejected Alternatives: Marking tasks complete from source inspection alone would create fake reports.
Scalability potential: Evidence-first status allows low/middle/high/ultra claims to remain tied to source or profiler proof.
Hardware Impact: No runtime impact. Process guard only.
Decision 003 - 64B Fog DTO
Problem: Fog state must cross C#/shader/vault boundaries without hidden managed properties or layout drift.
Solution: Use VolumetricFogParamsDTO with explicit 64B layout: FogColorAndDensity at 0, ScatteringParams at 16, FlowAdvection at 32, QualityAndLimits at 48. Validate with UnsafeUtility.SizeOf and Marshal.OffsetOf, matching established project layout checks.
Rejected Alternatives: Auto-layout structs, ScriptableObject runtime state, or properties were rejected because they hide layout and invite GC/property graph work.
Scalability potential: same DTO drives low, middle, high, and ultra paths through continuous floats instead of tier enums.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 receives one 64B constant upload instead of managed parameter fan-out. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 004 - RenderGraph Persistent Targets
Problem: feature needs half/quarter raymarch and full-res composite without per-frame temporary texture allocation.
Solution: Allocate persistent RTHandles quantized to 64-pixel buckets, import them into RenderGraph, and execute raymarch/composite as compute passes.
Rejected Alternatives: RenderTexture.GetTemporary, CommandBuffer.Blit, and material full-screen passes were rejected because they conflict with no-temp/no-blit mandate and existing RenderGraph patterns.
Scalability potential: Low uses quarter-ish internal scale; middle increases scale; high/ultra increase scale while preserving same pass topology.
Hardware Impact: Avoids temp RT churn on weak GPUs; exact allocation and GPU savings PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 005 - Dithered Proxy Through 64 Steps
Problem: binary low/ultra switch would violate GlobalQualityWeight and waste weak hardware on token loop.
Solution: Resolve ray steps continuously from 4 to 64 and proxyBlend continuously from analytic dithered fog to full raymarch. At proxyBlend >= 0.999, shader bypasses loop.
Rejected Alternatives: Fixed 16/32/64 presets and simulating real suspended-fluid physics were rejected. Fog is cinematic cheat, not fluid solver.
Scalability potential: Low = analytic dithered opacity; middle = short reduced-res march; high = longer flow/noise march; ultra = 64-step scattering with more point lights.
Hardware Impact: Toaster path skips march loop; RTX path spends saved budget on visual density and shafts. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 006 - Flow and Silt Ownership
Problem: Wake-reactive fog needs propeller turbulence, but fog feature must not invent direct dependencies on another agent's submarine code.
Solution: Consume existing shader globals from HectonMarineSnowRenderer and abyssal flow. Marine snow fog density becomes wake/silt input; abyssal flow advection warps volumetric noise.
Rejected Alternatives: New 3D SiltBuffer owner, CPU fluid grids, or submarine component lookup were rejected as cross-domain coupling and frame-time risk.
Scalability potential: Low can ignore inactive globals with 1x1 fallback textures; middle/high/ultra progressively reveal flow and wake density when producers are present.
Hardware Impact: Uses already-produced GPU fields; exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 007 - Biome and CSV Bridge
Problem: Extinction must react to biome/water profile without black-box fog stack or managed parsing in hot path.
Solution: Remove direct BiomeMatrix reads from render domain, seed default extinction DTOs, expose ReadOnlySpan CSV parser for water_extinction_profiles.csv, and blend vault-loaded profiles by local depth band until biome owner publishes unmanaged DTO/signal. editor path now streams file bytes into vault-owned CsvScratch and parses directly into vault profile array.
Rejected Alternatives: FindObjectOfType, GlobalRegistry.BiomeMatrix concrete polling, string.Split, per-frame CSV parsing, editor File.ReadAllBytes staging, and temp NativeHashMap/GetValueArray copying were rejected.
Scalability potential: Weak devices still use one selected extinction profile; middle/high/ultra spend same DTO profile data on smoother depth-band blending and denser scattering.
Hardware Impact: No hot-path managed parser; exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 008 - Telemetry Honesty
Problem: prompt requests GPU timing and black-box ring, but current implementation could not be compiled/profiled because CPU guard blocked build execution.
Solution: Implement 300-entry NativeArray telemetry ring, source-state hash, flags, estimated GPU usec, and binary dump on NaN or estimated >2ms. dump now writes NativeArray memory through `ReadOnlySpan ` and `FileStream` instead of copying into managed `byte[]`. Mark GPU query/profiler numbers as pending instead of fabricating results.
Rejected Alternatives: Reporting fake exact GPU query values, omitting black box, or allocating managed dump staging array were rejected.
Scalability potential: Same ring records low/middle/high/ultra behavior and can be swapped to real GPU query values after compile/profiler access.
Hardware Impact: Ring write is fixed-size NativeArray state; exact measured cost PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 009 - Compile-Wall Boundary Repair
Problem: first pass directly referenced Hecton8.Environment types from render feature, crossing sibling domain without contracts route.
Solution: Remove concrete BiomeMatrix/AtmosphereProfile read. Current fog uses owner-local settings, vault DTO overrides, and vault-loaded extinction profiles. biome hash blend requires future unmanaged contract or signal from biome owner.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `using Hecton8.Environment`, polling `GlobalRegistry.BiomeMatrix`, or adding new one-off global route without route card were rejected.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra still blend through same DTO; future biome data can be fed by single owner route without rewriting shader.
Hardware Impact: Removes per-frame concrete registry dependency and compile-wall risk. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 010 - Scheduled Mock Light Job and Double Buffer
Problem: Per-frame `IJob.Run()` and single point-light GraphicsBuffer violated dependency-chain and GPU upload discipline.
Solution: Schedule `BuildMockVolumetricLightsJob` with exact Burst flags and `[NoAlias]`, upload completed prior-frame data into inactive GraphicsBuffer via `UnsafeUtility.MemCpy`, then flip active buffers.
Rejected Alternatives: Same-frame `.Run()`, `Complete()` before checking `IsCompleted`, `SetData`, and single-buffer CPU/GPU contention were rejected.
Scalability potential: Low uploads zero/one cheap light after first completed job; high/ultra feed up to eight synthetic lights without changing topology.
Hardware Impact: Reduces main-thread stall and PCIe contention risk. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 011 - Explicit Dear Lie Dither
Problem: prior proxy path used stochastic noise but did not prove requested ordered dither fallback.
Solution: Add 4x4 Bayer matrix generated arithmetically, blend it with temporal screen noise, and keep low-quality branch outside raymarch loop.
Rejected Alternatives: Full raymarch on weak hardware and stochastic-only dirt were rejected.
Scalability potential: Below low-quality threshold shader collapses to one exponential fog evaluation; higher weights smoothly re-enter reduced-resolution raymarching and 64-step overkill.
Hardware Impact: Low path bypasses loop and avoids 3D noise octaves. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 012 - Silt Ownership
Problem: literal task asks for new persistent 3D SiltBuffer, but project already has MarineSnow wake/fog-density ownership.
Solution: Consume existing MarineSnow fog-density/wake texture as authoritative silt signal. Do not create duplicate wake/SiltBuffer owner in this render facade.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct WakeGeneratedSignal dependency, Submarine kinematic DTO polling, and second 3D density owner were rejected by one-owner authority and compile-wall rules.
Scalability potential: Low ignores absent texture through 1x1 fallback; high/ultra amplify existing wake density in raymarch.
Hardware Impact: Avoids duplicate compute injection and memory surface. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 013 - RenderGraph Buffer Ownership
Problem: compute pass imported textures into RenderGraph but bound fog constant buffer through `Shader.SetGlobalConstantBuffer` before graph passes, leaving hidden resource edge outside RenderGraph validation.
Solution: Import `_paramsBuffer` and active point-light GraphicsBuffer as BufferHandles, declare read access with `builder.UseBuffer`, bind constant buffer inside each compute render function, and pass point-light buffer through graph handle route.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping process-wide shader state was rejected because it can race graph scheduling and hides proof required by zero-temp RenderGraph mandate.
Scalability potential: Low, middle, high, and ultra all use same declared buffer route; quality changes remain scalar fields in 64B DTO instead of variant-specific globals.
Hardware Impact: Avoids implicit global-state hazards and improves RenderGraph scheduling visibility. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 014 - Noir Luminance Floor
Problem: shader allowed `_HectonVolumetricFogColorAndDensity.rgb` to resolve to pure black through `max(color, 0)`, which can erase particulate depth cues and violates Deep Sea Noir mandate against flat black voids.
Solution: Add `ResolveNoirFloorColor` with tiny blue-green luminance floor and use it in both proxy and raymarched branches.
Rejected Alternatives: Clamping in C# settings only was rejected because editor/CSV/runtime overrides can still feed zero into shader. shader floor is final visual authority.
Scalability potential: Low proxy fog remains legible under Bayer dithering; high/ultra raymarching preserves color energy for scattering without adding samples.
Hardware Impact: One `max(float3)` per affected path; expected cost is below measurable threshold. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 015 - Proxy Curve and Texture Edges
Problem: Static subagent audit found two resource/math defects: `Mathf.SmoothStep(0.12, 0.42, q)` was incorrectly treated like HLSL `smoothstep(edge0, edge1, x)`, preventing proxyBlend from reaching 1.0, and external MarineSnow/AbyssalFlow textures were raw global reads without RenderGraph texture edges.
Solution: Replace proxy math with explicit cubic smoothstep polynomial over 0.12..0.42 quality interval. Wrap external texture sources in cached RTHandles, import them into RenderGraph, declare read access, and bind TextureHandles inside compute pass.
Rejected Alternatives: boolean low-end branch was rejected by GlobalQualityWeight continuum. Per-frame texture wrappers were rejected by zero-temp policy. Direct producer dependencies were rejected by compile-wall rules.
Scalability potential: Low now truly executes analytic Bayer proxy branch; middle smoothly blends back into reduced raymarching; high/ultra keep declared graph inputs for flow/wake sampling.
Hardware Impact: Low-end path can finally bypass loop as designed. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 016 - Shader NaN Write Barrier
Problem: shader guarded many denominators but still wrote final raymarch and composite values to UAVs without finite check, allowing one bad upstream texture/depth value to poison frame.
Solution: Add `SafeFiniteScalar`, `SafeFiniteColor`, and `ResolveSafeFogWrite`; sanitize proxy/raymarch writes and composite color/alpha before UAV output.
Rejected Alternatives: C# telemetry-only NaN detection was rejected because it catches symptoms after GPU write. shader must prevent propagation at write barrier.
Scalability potential: Same barrier applies from proxy mode through 64-step mode without variants or branches on hardware tiers.
Hardware Impact: few finite checks at write-out only; expected cost is below measurable threshold. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 017 - Vault CSV Scratch
Problem: editor CSV load still used managed `File.ReadAllBytes`, temp `NativeHashMap`, and `GetValueArray(Allocator.Temp)`. It was cold-only, but it weakened human-control facade proof and left reserved CsvScratch buffer unused.
Solution: Add `ExtinctionCsvScratchBytes`, stream file into `ShinobuVolumetricFogCsvScratch`, and parse scratch `ReadOnlySpan ` directly into `ShinobuVolumetricFogExtinctionProfiles` with duplicate hash upsert inside fixed-capacity array.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping temp native containers was rejected because fixed 16-profile table does not need hash map. runtime binary reader was rejected because this task is editor/human-tuning CSV facade, not production payload route.
Scalability potential: Low, middle, high, and ultra all read same compact profile DTOs; designers can tune depth/biome-style water clarity without C# recompilation.
Hardware Impact: Removes cold editor native temp allocations and one copy. Runtime hot-path impact remains unchanged. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 018 - Span-Based Telemetry Dump
Problem: surge dump path still allocated managed `byte[]` and used `Marshal.Copy` before writing 300-frame telemetry ring. It was failure-only, but black-box path should be deterministic and allocation-minimal.
Solution: Wrap telemetry NativeArray pointer in `ReadOnlySpan ` and stream directly to dump file with `FileStream.Write`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping managed staging array was rejected because dump size is fixed and source memory is already contiguous/blittable.
Scalability potential: Same dump path works for low/middle/high/ultra; no gameplay or shader quality behavior changes.
Hardware Impact: Removes one managed allocation and one memory copy on surge/NaN dump. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 019 - Explicit Visual Phase
Problem: Shader drift used Unity's implicit `_Time.y`, making low-quality update shedding undocumented and hiding global dependency in shader.
Solution: Compute presentation-only visual phase in C# from `Time.frameCount`, quantized by polynomial `GlobalQualityWeight` curve from about 5Hz to 60Hz, pass it in `_HectonVolumetricFogCompositeParams.w`, and use that scalar for dither temporal noise, flow advection, and mock light phase.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `_Time.y` was rejected because it bypassed SHINOBU DTO/frame-param route. gameplay simulation tick route was rejected because this fog remains rollback-excluded presentation.
Scalability potential: Low quality advances visual drift less frequently while proxy fog bypasses raymarching; high/ultra update every frame with 64-step overkill available.
Hardware Impact: Low-end shader temporal work now naturally freezes between quantized phase updates instead of changing every frame. Exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 020 - Compile-Wall Honesty
Problem: legal narrow Core build was finally attempted after CPU/process guard cleared, but compilation failed before SHINOBU code could be validated because `Hecton8.Core.csproj` references missing `Assets/_Project/Scripts/World/HectonMapMagicVegetationBridgeFloraCollisionProxies.cs`.
Solution: Record failure as compile-wall strike 1 and leave World/csproj dependency untouched. SHINOBU_120 does not own World bridge file or project-file inclusion route, so changing it here would violate domain boundary and could hide another agent's dependency problem.
Rejected Alternatives: Restoring guessed World source file, deleting compile include, or editing project file from VFX fog domain were rejected. Those would be cross-domain repairs without owner proof.
Scalability potential: No runtime scalability change. decision preserves compile wall so SHINOBU remains RenderGraph/VFX facade instead of absorbing World integration authority.
Hardware Impact: No runtime impact. Build validation is blocked by dependency; profiler microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 021 - CBuffer Dirty Gate and Dead Variant Removal
Problem: render path still repeated native-layout reflection through `Marshal.OffsetOf`, uploaded 64B fog constant buffer every frame even when DTO page was bit-identical, and carried `_MATH_LOD_LOW/_MATH_LOD_HIGH` compute variants that SHINOBU shader never actually branched on.
Solution: Cache layout proof after static initialization, add hash/equality dirty gate around `LockBufferForWrite `, and remove unused compute `multi_compile` line. shader still scales through continuous `GlobalQualityWeight` DTO fields: ray step count, proxy blend, dither weight, internal scale, and point-light count.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping reflection in `RecordRenderGraph`, uploading constants blindly because payload is only 64B, or adding fake `_MATH_LOD_LOW` shader branches were rejected. project mandate is page-level dirtiness and continuous quality, not dead keyword surface.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep analytic dither proxy and avoid redundant CPU/GPU buffer map work on static cameras/settings; middle/high/ultra keep 64-step overkill available without shader variant stalls from SHINOBU-specific unused keywords.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 gain is small but deterministic: zero repeated layout reflection and skipped 64B CBuffer map/unmap on unchanged frames. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER because current Core compile is blocked by missing World file.
Decision 022 - Point-Light Page Dirty Hash
Problem: scheduled mock light job can produce identical `PointLightDTO` pages while low quality quantizes visual phase to about 5Hz, but prior path uploaded inactive structured GraphicsBuffer every time job completed.
Solution: Hash completed point-light page from active count plus up to eight `PositionRadius`/`ColorIntensity` float4 lanes, skip `LockBufferForWrite` and active-buffer flip when page hash/count matches last uploaded page, and reset dirty state on resource recreation and teardown.
Rejected Alternatives: Storing point lights in managed arrays for equality, uploading blindly because buffer is small, or stopping scheduled job entirely were rejected. job remains deterministic producer; upload path now respects page-level dirtiness.
Scalability potential: Low quality benefits most because visual phase cadence can hold steady for multiple frames; middle/high/ultra still upload when generated light page actually changes.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 gain is avoiding redundant structured-buffer map/unmap and GPU upload on unchanged frames. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 023 - AUP-Local Camera Route Without World Dependency
Problem: render facade used `camera.transform.position` and `camera.transform.forward` directly for fog depth-band selection, wrapped noise offset, telemetry, and mock-light generation. `AbsoluteUniversePosition` is in World namespace, so importing it into Visor would violate compile-wall routing even though AUP mandate is real.
Solution: Use Core-owned `HectonFloatingOrigin.CurrentTotalOffsetDouble` as authority snapshot, derive camera AUP double3, subtract same offset immediately, and narrow only local result to float3 for presentation math. Camera forward is finite-normalized before it enters Burst job. This preserves AUP/localization discipline without taking direct World dependency.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct `using Hecton8.World` from Visor render feature, continuing raw transform reads, or sending absolute double coordinates into shader were rejected. render facade may consume Core origin authority but cannot own World AUP truth.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra all use same local camera DTO route; quality still only changes scalar cost, not coordinate truth.
Hardware Impact: One double3 add/subtract and one forward normalization per rendered camera frame. Expected cost is below profiler noise; benefit is avoiding large-world coordinate drift and NaN propagation. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 024 - Unity.Mathematics Quality Continuum
Problem: SHINOBU's quality response was continuous, but C# control surface still mixed `Mathf.Clamp01`, `Mathf.Lerp`, and implicit clamps for same scalar that architecture documents define as `GlobalQualityWeight`. That weakens auditability and made low-end survival floor less explicit than mandate requires.
Solution: Add one `ResolveQualityCurve` cubic polynomial helper and route ray steps, internal render scale, proxy blend, point-light count, visual phase cadence, setup clamping, and estimate scaling through `math.saturate`, `math.lerp`, and `math.step`. proxy path now has explicit `math.step(0.12, quality)` survival floor before smooth polynomial fade releases toward raymarching.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping mixed `Mathf` quality code, adding binary low/high quality branches, or reintroducing shader keywords for SHINOBU-specific variants were rejected. Continuous math is owner route; variants are not needed for this fog facade.
Scalability potential: Low stays analytic/dithered with slow visual phase cadence and minimum ray cost; middle smoothly increases internal scale, light count, and ray count; high/ultra spend scalar on 64-step scattering without changing gameplay truth or adding variant churn.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 benefit is not raw ALU reduction from this patch alone; gain is deterministic load-shed correctness and easier audit of low-quality collapse. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 025 - Finite-Saturated Quality Gate
Problem: `math.saturate` clamps finite values but is not complete NaN vaccination strategy. If `HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight` or editor-injected render scale became NaN/infinite, SHINOBU could feed invalid values into ray-step rounding, visual cadence, estimate math, or RTHandle dimension calculation.
Solution: Add `ResolveFiniteSaturated`: finite values clamp to 0..1, invalid values collapse to `0.0`. Apply it to public quality scalar, quality curve, proxy blend, point-light count, visual phase cadence, and estimate scale. Add explicit finite fallback endpoints for `minimumInternalScale` and `maximumInternalScale` before interpolation.
Rejected Alternatives: Assuming upstream systems never publish NaN, relying on `math.saturate` alone, or clamping after render-target dimensions are computed were rejected. render facade must fail toward minimum survival cost before values reach GPU/resource sizing.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged for valid scalars. Invalid scalar state now degrades to low-cost dithered proxy rather than allocating invalid targets or producing undefined shader parameters.
Hardware Impact: Two finite checks on settings and finite guards around scalar curves; expected cost is below profiler noise. Benefit is preventing catastrophic NaN propagation. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 026 - Shader FBM Detail Gate
Problem: shader exposed continuous octave count, but after proxy mode released it always evaluated both coarse and fine FBM paths. That meant low/middle quality paid extra noise work even when quality scalar was supposed to shed ALU smoothly.
Solution: Make `ResolveFogDensity` compute coarse FBM first, then derive continuous `fineBlend` from quality above 0.35. fine FBM is only evaluated when blend is non-zero, and its contribution is lerped into coarse density without visual pop.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping unconditional second FBM, adding hardware-tier shader keywords, or removing fine detail entirely were rejected. scalar must buy extra particulate richness only when device has budget.
Scalability potential: Low stays proxy or single-FBM reduced raymarch; middle gradually introduces fine suspended silt; high/ultra pay fine-detail branch while still capped by 64 steps and opacity early-out.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 gain is avoiding one FBM call per ray step in low/middle raymarch band. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 027 - External Shader-Global Snapshot Consolidation
Problem: `RecordTelemetry` repeated global shader queries for MarineSnow density and AbyssalFlow activity even though `RecordRenderGraph` already needs same producer globals for RenderGraph texture import and compute binding.
Solution: Read MarineSnow/AbyssalFlow producer globals once per RenderGraph record, before vault/GPU state update, and pass immutable booleans into telemetry. Telemetry now records flags from same snapshot used for resource binding instead of touching global shader state again.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving duplicate `Shader.GetGlobalTexture`/`Shader.GetGlobalFloat` reads in telemetry or adding direct MarineSnow owner reference were rejected. route remains shader/global-producer bridge, but render feature samples it once.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged. change reduces hot-path bookkeeping and keeps external resource truth consistent for both graph binding and black-box flags.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 gain is tiny but deterministic: two global shader queries removed from telemetry per camera frame. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 028 - Editor Facade NaN Quarantine
Problem: UI Toolkit tuner writes directly into vault-backed `VolumetricFogParamsDTO`, but its slider paths used raw `math.clamp` or `math.saturate`. Invalid editor input could therefore write NaN into same DTO read by runtime RenderGraph feature.
Solution: Add `ClampFinite` in editor facade and route default quality seeding, slider display, and all slider-to-DTO writes through finite fallback clamps. Invalid density/scattering/extinction/anisotropy/flow/quality values collapse to conservative SHINOBU defaults.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving editor facade unsanitized because it is cold-only, or duplicating runtime repair after every editor mutation, were rejected. human-control surface must not be able to poison runtime DTO.
Scalability potential: Valid low/middle/high/ultra tuning remains unchanged. Invalid tuner state now fails toward low-cost, visible defaults rather than breaking quality curves or shader parameters.
Hardware Impact: Editor-only finite checks; no player hot-path cost. Runtime benefit is preventing invalid DTO state before Play Mode profiling. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 029 - Runtime DTO Boundary Sanitization And Local Noise Coordinates
Problem: Runtime serialized settings, vault overrides, and CSV extinction profiles still had path to feed NaN/infinity into `VolumetricFogParamsDTO` through raw `Mathf` clamps or unchecked color/profile lanes. compute shader also derived FBM coordinates from `samplePositionWS`, which weakens AUP-local noise guarantee if Unity world floats ever become large before origin shift.
Solution: Add finite fallback clamps at runtime DTO boundary for fog color, density, scattering, extinction, anisotropy, opacity break, flow strength, ray distance, silt strength, bilateral scale, profile depth ranges, profile absorption/scatter, and telemetry debug values. Invalid estimated GPU time is flagged in telemetry and stored as finite `0` before dump. In `Hecton_VolumetricFog.compute`, derive volumetric FBM coordinates from `samplePositionLocal + wrappedCameraNoiseOffset`, while still sampling owner-provided AbyssalFlow field with world/sample coordinate.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting inspector ranges, assuming CSV/editor paths are harmless, or relying only on shader write-barrier sanitization were rejected. shader output clamp stops visible NaN propagation too late; DTO and black-box records must be finite before they become frame evidence.
Scalability potential: Low stays on dithered analytic proxy when upstream values are invalid; middle/high/ultra keep same visual paths for valid data, with camera-relative noise precision preserved across large-world motion.
Hardware Impact: Adds bounded scalar finite checks on CPU presentation path and removes no GPU features. Expected cost is below profiler noise. Precision benefit is preventing large-coordinate FBM shimmer and invalid DTO poisoning. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 030 - Proxy Composite Bypass And Shader Inner-Path Sanitation
Problem: previous shader still had three local costs/risks after main polish: MarineSnow wake density was sampled inside every ray step even though it is screen-space constant for pixel, pure proxy mode still paid 3x3 bilateral composite path, and several flow/light/phase inputs could become NaN before final UAV write barrier caught them. runtime full-res composite target was also quantized, which is valid for reduced raymarch targets but not for final camera replacement.
Solution: Move MarineSnow density sampling to once per raymarched pixel and pass it into `ResolveFogDensity`. Add proxy fast path in `CompositeVolumetricFog` that samples half fog texture once when `proxyBlend >= 0.999`, bypassing 9-tap depth bilateral. Bound compute dispatches by UAV `GetDimensions`, not float uniform casts. Add `SafeFiniteSaturate`, finite-safe normalize, HG phase clamps, flow texture param sanitation, point-light attenuation/color sanitation, and finite editor telemetry plotting. Runtime full-res composite dimensions now match camera target exactly; only reduced internal targets are quantized.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving sample-in-loop because texture read is "small", quantizing final camera output for allocator convenience, or relying only on end-of-pixel finite clamps were rejected. low-end proxy must collapse real work, not merely hide raymarch loop.
Scalability potential: Low quality now executes analytic fog plus ordered/temporal dither, one half-texture composite sample, and no raymarch/9-tap bilateral. Middle uses reduced raymarch with one MarineSnow read per pixel and coarse FBM until quality buys fine detail. High/ultra keep 64-step scattering, flow advection, point-light pages, directional HG scattering, and bilateral composite.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 benefit is avoiding up to 64 redundant MarineSnow texture loads per fog pixel and avoiding 8 extra fog/depth samples in pure proxy composite. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER because Core compile/import/profiler proof is blocked by missing non-SHINOBU World source.
Decision 031 - Black-Box Dump Owner Identity
Problem: live runtime still used original task-literal dump name `Dump_VOLUMETRIC_SURGEON.bin`, while active AGENTS Black Box rule requires crash/NaN dumps to land at `Docs/AgentLogs/Dump_[YourID].bin`. That mismatch weakens owner-local forensic routing.
Solution: Change cold failure-path dump target to `Docs/AgentLogs/Dump_SHINOBU_120.bin` and record protocol override in status/logs. Historical log lines remain historical evidence; runtime path is now owner-ID aligned.
Rejected Alternatives: Dual-writing both dump files was rejected because failure handling should avoid extra I/O and ambiguity. Keeping legacy name was rejected because current AGENTS.md owner-ID rule is higher-priority session authority.
Scalability potential: Low, middle, high, and ultra rendering behavior is unchanged. black-box file name now maps directly to agent/domain when multiple systems dump during endurance testing.
Hardware Impact: No hot-path frame cost. only runtime change is file path used after NaN or estimated surge triggers fixed-size telemetry dump.
Decision 032 - UnsafeUtility Offset Proof
Problem: Task 04 explicitly requested layout validation through UnsafeUtility, but SHINOBU's cached verifier still used `Marshal.OffsetOf` for field offsets. sizes were already checked with `UnsafeUtility.SizeOf`, yet offset proof was weaker than assignment wording.
Solution: Route `VolumetricFogNativeLayout.OffsetOf ` through `UnsafeUtility.GetFieldOffset` using field metadata, returning -1 on missing fields so validation fails closed. validation remains cached at static initialization and still checks every SHINOBU DTO offset.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Marshal-only offsets was rejected because it did not match Task 04 precisely. Adding per-frame offset assertions was rejected because layout is static and already cached.
Scalability potential: Low, middle, high, and ultra rendering behavior is unchanged. layout proof now better protects all tiers from silent C#/GPU constant-buffer drift.
Hardware Impact: No frame hot-path cost. Cold static validation performs same number of field checks but uses Unity's unsafe layout authority.
Decision 033 - Setup Timing Cadence Gate
Problem: `AddRenderPasses` measured setup cost with `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp` every camera frame, but result was only allowed to publish performance warning once every 30 frames. That paid timing and division overhead on frames that could not emit telemetry.
Solution: Sample setup timing only when `Time.frameCount >= _nextPerformanceWarningFrame`. After each sample, advance next sample frame by 30 whether or not warning is emitted. render pass still enqueues every frame; only diagnostic timing is cadence-gated.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing setup warning entirely was rejected because black-box/performance telemetry remains useful. Keeping per-frame measurement was rejected because it violates frame-time dictatorship for rate-limited diagnostic path.
Scalability potential: Low, middle, high, and ultra visuals are unchanged. Weak devices stop paying redundant CPU timing work on 29 of 30 frames; high-end devices retain periodic setup telemetry.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 gain is tiny but deterministic: removes two timestamp reads and one floating division on non-sampled frames. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 034 - BiomeTransition Shader-Global Bridge
Problem: Task 12 wanted BiomeTransitionManager output, but earlier safe implementation only used SHINOBU vault extinction profiles because direct World DTO or BiomeMatrix reads would cross compile wall. repository now exposes World-owned shader-global atmosphere payload.
Solution: Read `_H8BiomeTransitionFogColor`, `_H8BiomeTransitionAbsorption`, and `_H8BiomeTransitionWeights` once during RenderGraph recording and finite-blend those values into fog DTO before upload. This keeps one fact owned by biome system while SHINOBU consumes only published visual payload.
Rejected Alternatives: Importing `Hecton8.World`, calling `BiomeTransitionManagerRuntime.TryReadSnapshot`, polling `GlobalRegistry.BiomeMatrix`, or duplicating biome blending inside SHINOBU were rejected. Those would couple VFX facade to World runtime ownership.
Scalability potential: Low still uses dithered proxy but with biome-correct tint/extinction when available; middle/high/ultra spend same owner-published atmosphere values across richer raymarching and scattering.
Hardware Impact: Adds three static-ID shader-global reads and finite scalar clamps per RenderGraph record. No new allocations, no new jobs, and no sibling assembly reference.
Decision 035 - Authored DTO Versus External Override Fence
Problem: runtime writes its final, profile/biome-blended `VolumetricFogParamsDTO` back into Vault every frame. Treating any valid Vault DTO as external override can cause SHINOBU's own previous output to be re-used as designer input on next frame, risking repeated extinction/biome compounding or stale override authority.
Solution: Track `_lastAuthoredParams` separately from `_externalOverrideParams`. valid Vault DTO becomes external override only when it differs from last SHINOBU-authored DTO. Runtime-authored DTOs are recognized and ignored as override input; external editor/vault writes persist as base tuning snapshot until explicitly replaced or cleared. validity gate now requires finite lanes and sane ranges for all four 16B lanes so uninitialized Vault memory cannot plausibly be captured as designer override.
Rejected Alternatives: Clearing all Vault overrides after every render write would break Abyssal Atmosphere Tuner. Trusting every valid Vault DTO was rejected because it confuses owner-authored output with human/external input. Adding direct World/Biome route was rejected by compile-wall rule.
Scalability potential: Low, middle, high, and ultra now consume stable external tuning before applying current extinction profiles and BiomeTransition globals once per frame. visual curve remains continuous and avoids accumulating density/extinction drift over long sessions.
Hardware Impact: Adds two 64B DTO fields and one fixed four-lane equality check per RenderGraph record. No managed allocation, no new job, no GraphicsBuffer traffic, and no sibling assembly dependency. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 036 - Shared DTO Validity And Editor Seed Fence
Problem: After external override fence became strict, UI Toolkit tuner still seeded full `VolumetricFogParamsDTO` only when `QualityAndLimits.y <= 0`. partially invalid vault page could therefore receive one edited slider value, remain invalid under runtime fence, and silently fail to become usable human-authored override.
Solution: Move full DTO default creation and validity checks into `VolumetricFogParamsAccess`. editor now calls `EnsureUsableParams` before refresh display and before every slider mutation, seeding complete 64B DTO with finite color, scattering, flow, quality, ray-step, distance, and proxy fields. Runtime override validation now calls same shared gate.
Rejected Alternatives: Relaxing runtime validity gate was rejected because it would re-open uninitialized Vault capture. Keeping duplicated editor/runtime range checks was rejected because next strictness change could diverge again. Clearing buffer on every editor refresh was rejected because it would destroy designer-authored values.
Scalability potential: Low seeds to analytic proxy/ray-step minimum through continuous `GlobalQualityWeight`; middle, high, and ultra retain same DTO shape while quality and ray steps scale continuously. Human edits now survive runtime override fence instead of disappearing when non-edited lane was invalid.
Hardware Impact: Editor seeding is cold-path. Runtime work is unchanged in shape because prior validity check already read same four 16B lanes; shared method reduces drift, not frame cost. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 037 - Single Quality-Curve Authority For SHINOBU DTOs
Problem: editor default path, editor quality slider, and runtime render feature had separate quality math after seed-fence work. That allowed valid DTO to carry linear ray steps or stale proxy blend while runtime used cubic `GlobalQualityWeight` curve and 0.12..0.42 proxy release.
Solution: Promote SHINOBU quality helpers into `VolumetricFogParamsAccess`: `ResolveQualityCurve`, `ResolveRayStepsForQuality`, and `ResolveProxyBlendForQuality`. Runtime `FeatureSettings`, editor `ApplyQuality`, and `CreateDefaultParams` now consume same scalar law.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping duplicate formulas was rejected because quality drift is hidden binary-tier failure mode. Creating new `Visor` asmdef was rejected in this loop because folder contains many unrelated renderer features and moving serialized `ScriptableRendererFeature` class would change its assembly identity.
Scalability potential: Low remains analytic proxy with minimum ray steps; middle releases smoothly into reduced raymarching; high and ultra reach 64-step overkill through same cubic curve. Designers no longer author DTO that disagrees with runtime cost math.
Hardware Impact: No new per-frame allocation or job. Runtime delegates to shared static helper instead of local duplicate math; expected frame impact is neutral. Exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.

===== FILE: Rationale_SHINOBU_121.md =====
Rationale_SHINOBU_121
Date: 2026-05-19
Status: ACTIVE / PENDING VERIFICATION
Decision 01 - Stop Before Source Mutation
Problem: user assigned `SHINOBU_121`, but `Docs/Tasks/CURRENT_BATCH.md` contains no ` ` block. batch protocol requires exact extraction from current batch before architectural decisions or code changes.
Solution: Halt source mutation and record prompt absence in disk-backed status/rationale/log files. This preserves anti-amnesia protocol and prevents cross-contamination from adjacent agent prompts.
Rejected Alternatives: Inferring tasks from chat text was rejected because XML block is mandated primary directive. Reading archived batches was rejected because current-batch authority explicitly forbids stale prompt leakage. Borrowing `SHINOBU_105` or `SHINOBU_120` GPU tasks was rejected as domain contamination.
Scalability potential: No runtime path changed. Low, middle, high, and ultra device behavior remains untouched until authoritative task block defines exact WFC/GPU scope.
Hardware Impact: 0 us runtime change on i3/MX350. No GPU, CPU, VRAM, GC, or PCIe behavior changed.
Decision 02 - Mandate Readiness Without Implementation
Problem: Procedural wreckage work would touch WFC, AUP, deterministic RNG, native memory, GPU buffers, and `DrawProceduralIndirect`; coding without mandate context would violate pre-code analysis rules.
Solution: Read relevant registry entries only: `TOOL_Procedural_Wreckage_Generator`, `MATH_AUP_Determinism_Sync`, `MATH_Deterministic_RNG_SlotMachine`, `REND_GPU_Sovereignty`, `GPU_Compute_Kernels_Kernels_Optimization_MX350`, `OPT_Zero_GC_Policy_AllocFree_Mandate`, `OPT_Native_Memory_Collections_JobSystem_Protocol`, and `ARCH_Global_Registry_ServiceLocator_DI_Init`.
Rejected Alternatives: Skipping mandate review was rejected. Creating generic WFC implementation was rejected because batch may demand specific DataVault, shader, or renderer ownership route.
Scalability potential: selected mandates define required Low/Middle/High/Ultra continuum: MX350 uses bounded WFC and minimal upload cadence; high and ultra tiers spend saved CPU/GPU budget on denser wreck matrices and richer presentation after real task block is restored.
Hardware Impact: 0 us runtime change. expected implementation envelope, once authorized, must remain below suspicious 0.1 ms frame cost for steady-state orchestration and avoid `SetData()`/`Instantiate()` hot paths.
Decision 03 - Reject Chat-Inferred 20-Task Reconciliation
Problem: follow-up mandate assumes 20-task matrix and orders reconciliation, but current authoritative batch file still lacks `SHINOBU_121`. Regex inventory found exactly 20 agent prompts and 400 task rows, all assigned to other IDs ending at `SHINOBU_120`.
Solution: Preserve strict parsing. Do not copy neighboring tasks, do not infer hidden tasks, and do not mutate source. correct action is to report prompt absence and wait for current batch file to be repaired.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating prose goal as substitute XML directive was rejected because it has no task list, no exact DoD, no editor facade requirements, and no buffer IDs. Executing generic WFC/GPU architecture was rejected because it could create wrong Vault routes, wrong asmdef boundaries, and wrong shader ownership.
Scalability potential: No runtime behavior changed. Once real block exists, implementation must expose continuous `GlobalQualityWeight` controls rather than low/high switches: low weight collapses WFC breadth, matrix upload cadence, and decorative module count; high/ultra weight increases ghost hull density, rust/caustic scalar richness, and draw count through indirect args without GameObjects.
Hardware Impact: 0 us runtime change on i3/MX350. This prevents speculative source churn and avoids unnecessary C# rebuilds under parallel-agent load.
Decision 04 - Restore Active Implementation After Current Batch Repair
Problem: active `Docs/Tasks/CURRENT_BATCH.md` now contains authoritative `SHINOBU_121` XML block with 20 tasks. previous blocker status is stale and would now obstruct required work. Existing `ProceduralWreckGenerator.cs` is large legacy mixed-object path with local persistent native containers, `Pack=1` DTOs, mesh creation, object-pool collision proxies, and loot spawn queues. Directly deleting or rewriting it risks breaking current World references owned by other agents.
Solution: Keep legacy source untouched for compatibility in this pass and add new isolated `Hecton8.World.ProceduralWreckage` assembly under World domain. new path owns explicit 128-byte `WreckageNodeDTO`, Vault buffer handles, deterministic fallback rules, Burst WFC jobs, AUP-relative matrix extraction, collision/loot staging DTOs, editor validation, and debug facades. Buffer IDs are cast constants local to assembly to avoid editing `H8Memory.cs` while other agents are modifying Core.
Rejected Alternatives: Deleting `ProceduralWreckGenerator.cs` was rejected because it exports public contracts and is referenced by World systems; doing so would be architectural sabotage outside narrow replacement migration. Patching every `Pack=1` World DTO was rejected as cross-domain churn. Waiting for `wreckage_module_rules.h8bin` was rejected because Task 01 demands emergency deterministic mock.
Scalability potential: Low devices receive bounded WFC breadth, shorter visibility distance, lower debris scatter count, and reduced interior detail by continuous `GlobalQualityWeight`; middle devices keep macro silhouette and moderate debris; high devices increase wreck density, shear variety, and collision proxy fidelity; ultra devices push richer indirect matrix payloads and shader scalar data without changing gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: Expected hot-path gain on i3/MX350 comes from replacing legacy hierarchy/object-pool hydration and mesh work with Vault-native DTO writes and indirect arguments. Static estimate before profiling: tens to hundreds of microseconds saved during generation frames and 0 B managed allocation in new generation jobs. Measured proof remains pending.
Decision 05 - Data-Only WFC and GPU Upload Route
Problem: assignment requires WFC generation, AUP-safe render matrices, loot/collision staging, and `DrawProceduralIndirect` without allowing persistent private `NativeArray` ownership or GameObject hierarchies. Unity `GraphicsBuffer` cannot be directly owned by Burst jobs, so literal "job writes GraphicsBuffer" design would either be invalid Burst code or force main-thread stalls.
Solution: Jobs write all simulation/render payloads into Vault-owned unmanaged DTO arrays. `ExtractRenderMatricesJob` subtracts `CameraAUP` from each node `double3 SectorAUP` before casting to `float3`, culls by continuous quality and optional HZB tiles, and writes `WreckageIndirectArgsDTO`. `ProceduralWreckageGpuUploadDispatcher` then uses `GraphicsBuffer.LockBufferForWrite` and `UnsafeUtility.MemCpy` to move matrices/args into double-buffered GPU buffers before `Graphics.DrawProceduralIndirect`.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct `GraphicsBuffer` access inside Burst was rejected because `GraphicsBuffer` is managed Unity object and not legal Burst field. `GraphicsBuffer.SetData` was rejected because it adds driver-managed copy behavior and violates explicit lock/memcpy upload mandate. `DrawMeshInstancedIndirect` was rejected because task asks for `DrawProceduralIndirect`.
Scalability potential: Low quality writes fewer nodes and debris matrices, shorter cull distance, and lower detail probability. Middle quality keeps silhouette and controlled debris ring. High quality increases shear/debris variety. Ultra quality uses saved CPU cost for richer shader scalar lanes rather than gameplay-truth bloat.
Hardware Impact: Expected MX350 benefit is fewer submitted matrices and no scene hierarchy updates. Upload cost becomes linear in visible matrix count and uses single contiguous memcpy per buffer. Measured microseconds remain pending until Unity import/profiler.
Decision 06 - Legacy Generator Quarantine Instead of Deletion
Problem: `ProceduralWreckGenerator.cs` contains legacy object-pool collision and loot application, plus `Pack=1` DTOs and local persistent native containers. It also exports public World contracts and has references from existing systems, so deletion would be cross-domain migration rather than local SHINOBU_121 fix.
Solution: Do not call or extend legacy path. Implement separate asmdef and document legacy path as incompatible with new procedural wreckage route. new path has no `Instantiate`, no object-pool calls, no managed collections in jobs, and no local persistent native arrays.
Rejected Alternatives: Deleting legacy file was rejected because it can break existing scene/world references and violates simultaneous-agent compile-wall rule. Half-patching individual pool calls was rejected because it would leave old mesh/local allocation architecture intact and create false compliance report.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra behavior now exists in new route and can be integrated without inheriting legacy generator's mesh/hierarchy costs.
Hardware Impact: New path avoids old collision proxy GameObject and loot spawn queue during generation. Exact savings require Unity-side integration proof.
Decision 07 - Build Gate Obeyed
Problem: workflow asks for compilation verification after task loops, but active mandate forbids `dotnet build` while CPU load is above 50% or another compiler is running. Current CPU samples were `99.42%` and `100%`.
Solution: Do not launch `dotnet build` under prohibited system load. Run static scans and `git diff --check` only. Mark compile status as `PENDING VERIFICATION` instead of fabricating green build.
Rejected Alternatives: Running build anyway was rejected because it violates user's explicit hardware protection rule. Claiming compile success from static scans was rejected because Unity asmdef import and Burst compile are not proven by text inspection.
Scalability potential: No runtime behavior changed by this decision. It preserves developer hardware and avoids adding load during parallel-agent batch.
Hardware Impact: Prevented high-load C# compile on already saturated system. Runtime impact is 0 us; verification remains pending.
Decision 08 - Add Endian-Aware H8BIN Rule Ingestion
Problem: pipeline had deterministic mock rules and CSV ingestion, but no safe parser for optional `wreckage_module_rules.h8bin` payload. That left Phase 6 endianness compliance as documentation-only and would force future integrators either to raw-copy file bytes into runtime DTOs or to skip binary payload.
Solution: Add cold `TryLoadBinaryRules` path that reads file into Vault-owned scratch, validates 16-byte header (`H8WR` magic, endian marker, version, count), parses each 64-byte rule field-by-field, uses `math.reversebytes` for swapped 32-bit payloads, sanitizes non-finite extents/weights, and copies only aligned `WreckageRuleDTO` records into runtime rules array. fallback mock rule set remains active when binary is absent or invalid.
Rejected Alternatives: Raw `UnsafeUtility.MemCpy` from binary file into `NativeArray ` was rejected because it would silently corrupt big-endian or schema-drifted payloads. Defining `[StructLayout(Pack=1)]` file record was rejected because runtime packed DTOs are banned and unnecessary for 16-rule cold parser. Blocking boot until Agent 103 provides real payload was rejected by Task 01.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same bounded rule count and mock fallback. Middle/high/ultra can author richer rule payloads without changing C# or increasing hot-path allocations; parser only changes cold data hydration, while `GlobalQualityWeight` continues to control WFC breadth, debris density, visibility, and shader scalar richness.
Hardware Impact: 0 us hot path on i3/MX350 because parsing is cold/editor-only. Expected cold cost is one bounded file read into 32 KB Vault scratch buffer and at most 16 fixed-size row parses. It avoids future ARM64 endian/alignment traps and prevents startup crash when binary is missing.
Decision 09 - Route Card Over Self-Green
Problem: new procedural wreckage DataVault surface is global authority route. architecture mandate requires owner, phase, cadence, capacity, failure mode, telemetry, shutdown, stale-handle behavior, and proof fields. previous documentation described route but did not include full route-card/review shape.
Solution: Add `Docs/ARCHITECTURE/PROCEDURAL_WRECKAGE_GLOBAL_AUTHORITY_ROUTE_CARD_SHINOBU_121.md` and link it from domain architecture doc. route card is intentionally marked `YELLOW / PENDING VERIFICATION`, not `GREEN`, because static source is not Unity import, Burst compile, profiler, GCMonitor, Frame Debugger, or player proof.
Rejected Alternatives: Claiming `GREEN` from static source was rejected as false proof. Adding `GlobalRegistry` slot was rejected because current data route is native bulk state and should remain DataVault-only. Adding SignalBus lane for bulk matrices was rejected because payload is not event and would create managed/global traffic pressure.
Scalability potential: route card preserves low/middle/high/ultra continuum by keeping quality math inside generation jobs and keeping bulk payloads in contiguous Vault buffers. High/ultra visual overkill uses `GpuScalars` and larger indirect matrix counts without turning gameplay truth into monolith.
Hardware Impact: 0 us runtime. architectural value is compile-wall protection and reduced H-Phi ambiguity: no new sibling runtime dependency, no new global service slot, no hidden ownerless native heap.
Decision 10 - Explicit NaN Fallbacks in Debris and Audit Paths
Problem: debris scatter math is deterministic and bounded, but two writes still depended on that assumption rather than proving finite output at final Vault write boundary. `GenerateDebrisFieldJob` wrote debris matrices/AUP directly, and `WreckageSelfAuditJob` computed overlap distance from pair deltas without first rejecting non-finite AUP data.
Solution: Add final finite checks before debris node writes and pair-overlap math. Debris nodes with non-finite matrix/AUP now fall back to root AUP, identity rotation, 0.5m bounds, `NonFiniteFallback`, and `FaultNonFinite`. Self-audit pair comparisons now skip non-finite deltas and OR `FaultNonFinite` into audit result.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting deterministic hash/curl-noise math was rejected because project rule says every render/physics-feeding NativeArray write must be guarded. Adding managed logs was rejected because faults belong in telemetry ring and dump path. Throwing exceptions was rejected because gameplay code must fail closed, not crash.
Scalability potential: Low and middle tiers pay only one finite check per debris write and audited pair. High/ultra tiers retain richer debris counts and audit coverage while keeping corrupt state out of GPU matrices and collision staging.
Hardware Impact: Static cost is bounded and data-local. Worst-case audit guard is capped to existing 256-node pair probe. gain is survivability: one NaN no longer propagates into render matrices, collision proxies, or self-audit results.

===== FILE: Rationale_SHINOBU_122.md =====
SHINOBU_122 Rationale - Biome Transition Manager
Problem: `Docs/Tasks/CURRENT_BATCH.md` does not contain ` `.
Solution: Treat XML task count as 0, record batch defect, and constrain implementation to user-provided objective plus domain 18 from `Docs/Actual Domains of Project.txt`.
Rejected Alternatives: Do not borrow neighboring agent prompts; strict parsing forbids architectural leakage from adjacent XML blocks.
Scalability potential: Low, Middle, High, and Ultra all require same deterministic owner-local blend contract; quality changes only alter how many biome centers are interpolated and how much visual/audio richness is consumed.
Hardware Impact: Prevents wasted implementation against wrong prompt. Runtime impact unchanged.
Problem: later CLI extraction returned actual ` ` with 20 tasks after initial extraction failed.
Solution: Corrected working state from task count 0 to 20 and promoted XML block to primary directive.
Rejected Alternatives: Continuing from fallback user summary would miss mandatory DTO alignment, mock traversal, Vault publication, acoustic staging, and editor tooling tasks.
Scalability potential: Low blends 1 biome, Middle blends 2, High blends 3, Ultra blends 4 through continuous `GlobalQualityWeight` math.
Hardware Impact: Correct directive prevents rework; runtime target remains zero physics broadphase and 0 B/frame GC.
Problem: `biome_transition_matrix.h8bin` is not present in `Assets`, `Data`, or `StreamingAssets`, and binary payload ledger does not classify it as active runtime content.
Solution: Treat CSV plus deterministic mock biomes as current source lane. `BiomeAtmosphereCsvIngestJob` parses `Assets/_Project/Data/World/biome_atmosphere_rules.csv` from Vault byte scratchpad; `BuildEmergencyMockBiomesJob` writes four deterministic centers when CSV/payload data is absent.
Rejected Alternatives: Do not fabricate or hand-patch `.h8bin`; binary payloads with headers/checksums must come from their baker. Do not crash boot while waiting for future baker.
Scalability potential: Low reads same data but evaluates fewer centers and blends fewer weights; Middle/High/Ultra progressively allow larger scan/blend/cadence budgets.
Hardware Impact: Missing-payload path becomes cold scheduled job instead of repeated file probes or managed fallbacks. i3/MX350 avoids boot stalls and per-frame IO.
Problem: Legacy biome switching could regress into BoxCollider/OnTrigger routes.
Solution: Static scans found no `BiomeVolume.cs`, `AtmosphereChanger.cs`, or biome-transition `OnTrigger*` scripts. new owner route is `BiomeTransitionManagerRuntime` -> Vault DTOs -> `BiomeChangedSignal`/shader globals. Existing collision triggers in audio, hazards, construction, and nav proxies are outside biome-transition owner and were not deleted.
Rejected Alternatives: Deleting unrelated BoxColliders would break gameplay collision and violates owner-local boundaries.
Scalability potential: All hardware tiers use mathematical proximity; weak hardware reduces ALU work through quality curves, not physics broadphase.
Hardware Impact: Biome switching no longer depends on thousands of trigger AABB checks. Estimated saved cost: 20-200 us/frame in dense scenes depending trigger count.
Problem: Old biome transition fog DTOs used packed sequential layout and new task mandates explicit ARM64 layout.
Solution: Replaced hot DTOs with explicit layouts. Primary `BiomeStateDTO` is 64B: `BiomeHash` offset 0, `FogColor` offset 16, `AbsorptionParams` offset 32, `AmbientAudioVolume` offset 48, explicit pad through byte 63. Added `BiomeTransitionNativeLayout.Validate()` and editor guard.
Rejected Alternatives: `Pack=1`, auto-layout, or C# properties. Those create unaligned ARM64 reads and can trigger CS1612/defensive copies when NativeArray elements are mutated.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra share one DTO ABI; quality changes math volume only, not memory layout.
Hardware Impact: 64B stride maps to one L1 cache line for primary state DTO and avoids unaligned NEON fetch penalties on Quest-class ARM64.
Problem: first implementation completed CSV, mock, and traversal jobs synchronously.
Solution: Seed jobs are now scheduled and completed only after `IsCompleted`; mock traversal is chained as input dependency and read by `EvaluateBiomeProximityJob`/`RecordBiomeTransitionTelemetryJob` through Vault AUP buffer. Shutdown remains allowed to complete outstanding handles.
Rejected Alternatives: Blocking `Complete()` in `FastTick`; direct CPU mock position writes; Transform-only fallback.
Scalability potential: Low hardware can run solver at 5Hz without main-thread stalls; Ultra can schedule every frame.
Hardware Impact: Removes hot-path wait risk. Estimated saved latency spike: 50-500 us when Burst worker scheduling is busy.
Problem: `UninitializedMemory` buffers can contain arbitrary bits and cannot be read before deterministic initialization.
Solution: CSV and emergency mock seed jobs now write counters from `default` instead of reading previous garbage. Tuning is set to deterministic default before runtime reads. No private persistent `NativeArray`, `NativeList`, or `NativeHashMap` fields were added.
Rejected Alternatives: `ClearMemory` on every Vault buffer; local component-owned persistent NativeArrays.
Scalability potential: Same data sovereignty across tiers; low devices avoid OS zero-fill cost.
Hardware Impact: Avoids clearing roughly 11 KB on boot/reload and prevents random active-count reads from uninitialized memory.
Problem: Biome atmosphere must reach visual and audio consumers without cross-domain concrete calls.
Solution: Publish path is split: Burst writes `CurrentAtmosphereDTO`, `BiomeBlendMaskDTO`, `BiomeAcousticStageDTO`, and six-slot `float4` shader payload in Vault; runtime mirrors completed payload into global shader vectors and standard fog/extinction globals. Audio consumes staged DTO or existing `BiomeChangedSignal`, not direct `AudioSource` mutation.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct references to rendering/audio managers, managed delegates, or per-biome `AudioSource` fade scripts.
Scalability potential: Low uses one dominant biome and slower cadence; Ultra exposes four weights, dither parameters, and full atmospheric coefficients to shaders.
Hardware Impact: Presentation handoff is six `float4` copies and handful of shader globals after job completion; no physics or managed event fanout in solver.
Problem: Rollback/determinism mandates reject Unity time and random state in authoritative blend math.
Solution: Removed `Time.*` from new biome manager path. Frame comes from `SystemDispatcher` snapshot when available, with local monotonic fallback only when dispatcher is unavailable. Jobs use `FloatMode.Deterministic`; no UnityEngine.Random or managed RNG is used.
Rejected Alternatives: `Time.frameCount`, `Time.deltaTime`, or nondeterministic noise in solver. Shader-side dither remains presentation-only.
Scalability potential: All tiers use same deterministic state hash; only cadence and active weights vary by `GlobalQualityWeight`.
Hardware Impact: Deterministic float mode costs more than Fast mode but protects net sync; saved physics work pays for it.
Problem: Designers need control without recompilation.
Solution: Added `Biome Transition Tuner` UI Toolkit window with radius, hardware-quality override, cadence, dither strength, gizmo, mock traversal, layout validation, CSV reload, and black-box dump controls. CSV rules are human-readable and hot-reloadable through editor button.
Rejected Alternatives: Hardcoded constants only; runtime IMGUI/debug overlay.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra can be tuned live through continuous sliders rather than binary tier toggles.
Hardware Impact: Editor-only allocations do not enter gameplay hot path; runtime reads one 64B tuning DTO.
Problem: Build verification is required but CPU gate forbids compiling while machine is under load.
Solution: Checked CPU and compiler processes before build: CPU average `53.26%`, `dotnet/csc` count `0`. Build was deferred per AGENTS rule. Static scans and `git diff --check` were run instead; diff check reports only CRLF normalization warnings.
Rejected Alternatives: Launching `dotnet build` against explicit >50% CPU prohibition.
Scalability potential: No runtime impact.
Hardware Impact: Protects developer machine from compile contention; compile proof remains pending until CPU <=50%.
Problem: `NativeArrayOptions.UninitializedMemory` made tuning DTO unsafe if read before deterministic seed.
Solution: Added `_tuningInitialized` and `EnsureTuningDefaultNoRead()` so `BiomeTransitionTuningDTO` is written once after Vault handle creation without reading previous bytes. Editor writes mark runtime tuning initialized so user sliders are not overwritten by later seed pass.
Rejected Alternatives: Reading `tuning[0].LowCadenceHz` as validity test; that touches undefined Vault bytes. Switching tuning buffer back to `ClearMemory` would violate Task 15.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra now start from deterministic cadence, dither, radius, and scan-scale values; designers can still override continuously.
Hardware Impact: Keeps zero-init savings while removing undefined branch behavior on i3/MX350 and ARM64.
Problem: Signal lane and scalability-limit plumbing had cold/hot ambiguity.
Solution: Forced `BiomeChangedSignalWriter` creation during Vault preparation instead of first evaluator schedule, added `MaxCenterScanScale` to `EvaluateBiomeProximityJob`, and exposed it through editor tuner. evaluator chooses nearby sector start index before applying quality-scaled scan budget.
Rejected Alternatives: Lazy queue allocation in first FastTick; unused DTO field; always scanning from index zero on low quality.
Scalability potential: Low devices can collapse distance evaluation toward one center from sector-relevant start point; Ultra scans full authored budget and blends up to four weights.
Hardware Impact: Removes first-transition allocation spike and preserves deterministic low-tier ALU shedding.
Problem: first SHINOBU_122 signal producer used `GlobalSignals.BiomeChangedSignalWriter`, but static source shows current consumers read `SignalBus .GetFrameSnapshot()` and no owner drains `_biomeChangedSignals` direct queue into that snapshot.
Solution: Changed cold lane warmup and evaluator writer to `SignalBus .ParallelWriter`. job still writes 64-byte unmanaged `BiomeChangedSignal` from Burst, but now it enters typed lane that consumers already observe.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding new bridge drain in `GlobalSignals.cs` would modify core global infrastructure from biome domain. Keeping direct queue output would silently drop signal for most modern consumers. Managed C# events remain rejected.
Scalability potential: Low emits at same dirty-only cadence as solver, while middle/high/ultra consumers can read existing typed snapshot without polling biome runtime.
Hardware Impact: No additional per-frame allocation; typed lane already owns bounded capacity/load shedding. This fixes correctness without adding new global route or broad core edit.
Problem: biome transition route added and consumed global surfaces without formal route-card artifact.
Solution: Added `SHINOBU_122_BIOME_TRANSITION_STATE` route-card and self-review result `YELLOW / PENDING VERIFICATION` to `Docs/Tasks/Status_SHINOBU_122.md`. It names existing `SignalBus ` lane, Vault BufferIDs `71220..71231`, capacities, failure modes, telemetry fields, shutdown behavior, stale-handle behavior, and runtime proof still missing.
Rejected Alternatives: Reporting route as `GREEN` from static scans only; hiding route-card evidence in chat; adding new registry slot.
Scalability potential: Same continuous quality curve; route-card prevents later low/high binary forks or catch-all signal misuse.
Hardware Impact: Documentation/static governance only; no gameplay cost.
Problem: Task 20 required embedded self-audit, not just chat/log claim.
Solution: Added `TryRunSelfAudit(out faultFlags, out weightSumError)` to validate native layout, snapshot readiness, normalized weight error, and blend-count bounds. UI Toolkit validator now runs this routine after layout validation.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying only on final markdown. report cannot catch later bad CSV reload or uninitialized payload.
Scalability potential: Same audit applies across low, middle, high, and ultra because expected invariant is weight sum = 1.0 regardless of active blend count.

Rejected Alternatives: Ignoring AGENTS >50% CPU rule to force proof artifact.
Scalability potential: No runtime impact.

Problem: `BiomeTransitionManagerRuntime` still had `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` and `GlobalRegistry.Player` lookup paths reachable from ordinary `FastTick` through `EnsureVaultBuffers`, `TryResolveRuntimeBuffers`, and `TryResolvePlayerAup`.
Solution: Added cached `_vault` and `_playerContext` dependencies, bound them during cold lifecycle calls, and subscribed to `IGlobalRegistryHotSwapRefListener` so DataVault/Player replacement rebinds without polling. `TryResolveRuntimeBuffers` now resolves only against cached `_vault`; `TryResolvePlayerAup` reads cached `IPlayerRuntimeContext` or serialized/cold-resolved transform. `OnDrawGizmos` now uses cached Vault tuning instead of static editor facade.
