Hardware Impact: Removes two to three static service reads from every eligible biome solver tick and prevents service-locator drift from becoming live player/Vault state bus. Estimated direct saving is sub-microsecond per tick, but important gain is architectural: no hidden registry coupling inside solver loop.
Problem: registry fix still left cold-work leak into `FastTick`: tick could call `EnsureVaultBuffers()` and shared seed method could reach CSV path/file IO if initialization was delayed.
Solution: Removed `EnsureVaultBuffers()` from `FastTick` and split seed flow into `TrySeedBiomeData()` for cold scheduling and `TryFinalizeSeedBiomeData()` for hot completion. CSV file probes and file reads remain in Start/editor reload/hot-swap paths. tick path now only completes already-finished seed chain.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping one convenience seed method for both lifecycle and tick; lazy Vault handle creation inside `FastTick`; per-frame retries for missing DataVault.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra cadence behavior is unchanged after seed; weak hardware no longer risks cold file-system work during first gameplay tick.
Hardware Impact: Removes potential cold IO and Vault handle creation spikes from gameplay frame. Worst-case avoided hitch is file-system dependent; on i3/MX350 this is correctness requirement, not microsecond-only optimization.
Problem: previous seed split still allowed `FastTick` to schedule emergency mock fallback after completed CSV parse produced zero active biomes, and `BuildEmergencyMockBiomesJob` wrote tuning defaults that could overwrite editor-authored tuning.
Solution: Chained `BuildEmergencyMockBiomesJob` behind `BiomeAtmosphereCsvIngestJob` during cold scheduling with `OnlyWhenCounterEmpty`. conditional fallback reads CSV counter after dependency completes and writes deterministic mock biome states only when no CSV row was accepted. Tuning is now initialized solely by `EnsureTuningDefaultNoRead()` or editor facade, not by mock biome job.
Rejected Alternatives: Completing CSV in Start to branch synchronously; leaving fallback scheduling in `FastTick`; allowing mock biome writer to reset designer tuning.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra seed source is still same unmanaged state table; only runtime evaluation cadence and blend count scale through `GlobalQualityWeight`.
Hardware Impact: Removes last cold seed scheduling branch from solver tick and prevents accidental tuning reset. Direct steady-state saving is sub-microsecond; avoided hitch is first-run Burst/file-order dependent.
Problem: SHINOBU_122 scheduled Vault-writing seed/pipeline jobs but did not register those handles in global owner-job ledger, and local finalization still used direct `.Complete()` calls.
Solution: Added `OwnerSystem = SystemID.WorldStreaming`, registered seed and pipeline handles through `H8Memory.RegisterActiveJob`, and replaced direct completion with `DispatcherJobSwap.TryFinalizeCompleted` in ready-only finalize paths plus `DispatcherJobSwap.TryComplete(..., forceComplete: true)` in teardown/vault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving only private `_seedHandle`/`_pipelineHandle` ownership; adding new Core owner enum; blocking inside `FastTick`; editing H8Memory from biome domain.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra math is unchanged, but owner-job tracking now gives scene transition and DataVault release one authoritative fence path regardless of cadence.
Hardware Impact: Runtime ALU cost unchanged; teardown correctness improves. Static scan now reports no direct `.Complete()` calls in SHINOBU_122 files, removing class of accidental main-thread stall regressions.
Problem: Solver cadence used `FastTick` delta-time accumulation. It did not call Unity `Time.*`, but rollback-sensitive scheduling should be based on deterministic simulation frames rather than variable frame duration.
Solution: Replaced `_cadenceAccumulator`/seconds cadence with `_lastScheduledFrame` and `ResolveCadenceFrameStep()`. continuous quality curve still interpolates 5Hz to 60Hz, then maps to deterministic frame step from 12 frames to 1 frame using dispatcher frame snapshot.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping delta-time accumulator because it is "not Unity Time"; binary low/high tick-rate branches; scheduling every frame on all hardware.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra keep same continuous curve while cadence becomes rollback-friendly: weak hardware sheds updates by deterministic frame skip, high hardware approaches every-frame atmospheric solve.
Hardware Impact: ALU savings unchanged, but frame cadence is reproducible. Weak devices still reach 5Hz target without introducing nondeterministic accumulator drift.
Problem: Mock traversal still used mutable serialized float accumulator and was unreachable in forced mock mode when no player AUP/Transform existed, which breaks rollback repeatability and CI/editor fallback coverage.
Solution: Added `MockTraversalPeriodFrames = 600` and derive mock phase as `(simulationFrame % 600) / 600`. `FastTick` now resolves tuning first, permits forced/editor mock traversal without player Transform, and uses zero AUP placeholder only until `MockCameraTraversalJob` writes authoritative mock AUP into Vault buffer.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping float accumulation because it is "debug only"; requiring scene Player object for fallback path; using Unity `Time.time` or editor frame counters.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra keep same mathematical mock route. Weak hardware still runs at quality-cadenced frame steps; Ultra can sample same deterministic traversal every frame.
Hardware Impact: Removes accumulator drift and one hard dependency from fallback path. Direct runtime saving is sub-microsecond; correctness gain is deterministic replay and CI coverage without scene physics/Transform setup.
Problem: sparse center table or low-quality scan could produce zero positive weights after sector/radius gates, leaving `DominantBiomeHash = 0` and forcing visual/audio consumers into fallback constants instead of nearest biome.
Solution: `EvaluateBiomeProximityJob` now tracks nearest scanned biome center in AUP-local float space and inserts it at weight 1 when all radius/sector weights collapse to zero. event/counter flags mark `FlagNearestFallback`, while normal multi-biome interpolation is unchanged.
Rejected Alternatives: Full active-center scan on weak hardware; widening every biome radius to hide gap; returning hash 0 and depending on shader defaults.
Scalability potential: Low quality now collapses to explicit nearest-neighbor biome, Middle/High/Ultra still use 2-4 weighted lanes when valid weights exist. No binary tier switch was added.
Hardware Impact: Adds two scalar writes and one conditional per scanned center, plus one state lookup only on all-zero collapse. This is cheaper than increasing scan budget and keeps weak-device behavior valid.
Problem: deterministic cadence gate wrote `_lastScheduledFrame` before proving that real player AUP or forced mock AUP path existed. missing-player frame with mock disabled could consume cadence slot without scheduling solver.
Solution: Moved `_lastScheduledFrame = frame` after player/mock eligibility check and immediately before pipeline input blit/schedule path.
Rejected Alternatives: Accepting missed retries as harmless; scheduling with zero AUP when mock is disabled; reverting to seconds accumulation.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra cadence remains unchanged for valid schedules. Invalid frames no longer mask next eligible frame.
Hardware Impact: No extra ALU. Removes small starvation edge case during player service startup or scene transition.
Problem: `EvaluateBiomeProximityJob` could insert center candidate even when `FindStateIndex(center.BiomeHash)` returned `-1`. That allowed biome hash with no fog/audio state to become dominant and emit through `SignalBus `.
Solution: Require `stateIndex >= 0` before `InsertCandidate`; otherwise mark `FlagInvalidInput` and continue scanning. nearest fallback already performs same state validation.
Rejected Alternatives: Letting `BlendAtmosphereJob` silently fail to accumulate and rely on fallback colors; emitting state-less biome hashes and forcing consumers to guard them.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra are unchanged for valid data; malformed or partial Vault/CSV content now degrades to nearest valid state or explicit invalid flag.
Hardware Impact: Adds one branch after existing state lookup only for positive-weight candidates. It prevents downstream shader/audio churn caused by invalid dominant hashes.
Problem: shader payload Vault buffer was sized for eight `float4` slots, but `PublishAtmosphereDataJob` wrote only six. Because buffer is deliberately `UninitializedMemory`, slots 6-7 could contain stale data if future CBuffer consumer copied whole payload.
Solution: Require `ShaderPayloadFloat4Count` before publishing, write slots 0-5 as before, add slot 6 for dominant hash/frame/flags, and deterministically zero slot 7. Runtime shader-global mirroring also refuses partial payloads.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving slots 6-7 unwritten because current mirror reads only 0-5; switching buffer to `ClearMemory`; shrinking payload and breaking future CBuffer layout.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra are unchanged; all tiers now publish deterministic fixed-width payload.
Hardware Impact: Adds two `float4` `MemCpy` operations per solver publish. Cost is negligible compared to value of preserving zero-init and avoiding stale shader data.
Problem: Black-box dump serialization used `BinaryWriter`, hiding byte order and initially risking mismatch against explicit telemetry DTO offsets.
Solution: Replaced writer with stack `Span ` record and explicit little-endian integer/float encoders. record is exactly 64 bytes: AUP grid offsets 0/8/16, local floats 24/28/32, padding 36-47 zeroed, dominant hash 48, blend count 52, CPU microseconds 56, state hash 60.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `BinaryWriter` because dump is cold; memcpying raw struct bytes without endianness; writing variable-length records.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra dump format is identical, so QA crash forensics can parse every hardware tier with one decoder.
Hardware Impact: Cold crash/editor path only. It removes managed writer abstraction and makes 300-record dump deterministic at 19.2 KB.
Problem: `EvaluateBiomeProximityJob` still used hash scan over `BiomeStateDTO[]` for normal weighted candidates after sector/center scan. With 64 active centers this remains bounded, but it violates spirit of Task 12 because hot candidate path is O(scanCount * stateCount) instead of using center record as owner-local route to its state payload.
Solution: Added `BiomeCenterDTO.StateIndex` at byte offset 48 inside existing 64-byte center record. CSV and emergency mock seed jobs write this index. evaluator validates `States[StateIndex].BiomeHash == Center.BiomeHash` and only falls back to hash scan for stale or malformed buffers. Nearest fallback now tracks only nearest center whose state index has already validated.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding NativeHashMap from biome hash to state index would create another Vault surface and new init/failure path. Keeping hash scan was simpler but wasted ALU on every contributing center. Embedding managed dictionary is rejected outright.
Scalability potential: Low quality still scans quality-scaled center subset and collapses to one nearest biome; Middle/High/Ultra increase scan/blend lanes without multiplying by state-table length in normal path.
Hardware Impact: On i3/MX350, worst-case normal lookup drops from up to 64 state comparisons per candidate to one indexed load plus one hash compare. At Ultra with 64 centers, this removes hundreds of scalar compares per scheduled solve.
Problem: Raw `HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight` fed cadence, scan count, and blend gates directly. curve was continuous, but small thermal oscillations could still flip rounded frame-step/scan ceilings between adjacent values on consecutive eligible frames.
Solution: Added deterministic frame-based quality slew in `BiomeTransitionManagerRuntime`: 0.015 hysteresis band, downgrade ramp up to 1.0 over 60 simulation frames, and upgrade ramp up to 1.0 over 180 frames. It uses dispatcher frame identity and no `Time.deltaTime`; evaluator still receives continuous float. If dispatcher frame rewinds under rollback, filter resynchronizes to target quality instead of unsigned-underflow stepping.
Rejected Alternatives: Binary low/high tiers; seconds accumulator; raw quality pass-through; delaying all downgrades for three seconds, which protects visuals but risks thermal runaway.
Scalability potential: Low, Middle, High, and Ultra remain one continuum. Weak-device downgrades still shed cost quickly; high-end recovery is deliberately slower to avoid visual/cadence flicker.
Hardware Impact: Adds few scalar operations on scheduled frames only. It prevents cadence thrash and redundant job scheduling transitions under thermal noise.
Problem: Task 16 required 300-frame black box, but quality cadence intentionally skips solver frames at low `GlobalQualityWeight`. previous telemetry ring advanced only when full solver chain ran, leaving forensic gaps during exact weak-hardware mode where cadence drops toward 5Hz.
Solution: Added `RecordCadenceSkippedTelemetry()` in host tick. When frame is inside deterministic cadence gate, it writes one 64-byte telemetry record using current player AUP or cached mock AUP, cached dominant hash/blend count, frame-specific state hash, `CpuMicroseconds=0`, and `FlagCadenceReused`.
Rejected Alternatives: Scheduling full Burst solver just to fill telemetry; scheduling separate telemetry job every skipped frame without dependency owner; managed log lines; accepting 5Hz black-box coverage on weak devices.
Scalability potential: Low quality now keeps 60Hz forensic continuity while solver math remains 5Hz. Middle/High/Ultra naturally record either reused or newly solved frames as cadence approaches every frame.
Hardware Impact: Adds one fixed 64-byte NativeArray write on cadence-skipped frames. On i3/MX350 this is cheaper than waking evaluator/blend/publish job graph and preserves crash forensics.
Problem: `TryRunSelfAudit` used `max(maskSum, atmosphereSum)` before measuring weight-sum error. If one vector summed to 1.0 and other was malformed below 1.0, bad side could be hidden.
Solution: Compute `abs(maskSum - 1)` and `abs(atmosphereSum - 1)` independently, then report max error and fail if either sum or final error is non-finite or exceeds `0.001`.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting only atmosphere DTO; trusting only shader mask; keeping resolved max-sum shortcut because blender normally writes both together.
Scalability potential: All quality levels share same invariant: normalized weights sum to 1.0 whether one, two, three, or four biome lanes are active.
Hardware Impact: Editor/cold self-audit only. Runtime solver cost is unchanged.
Problem: Cadence-reused telemetry for forced/editor mock traversal could read last scheduled `MockCameraAup` Vault cell. At low quality solver intentionally skips up to 11 frames, so black-box AUP could lag behind deterministic mock phase even while ring cursor advanced every frame.
Solution: `RecordCadenceSkippedTelemetry()` now calls same endpoint/phase math used by `MockCameraTraversalJob`, derives AUP from `frame % 600`, and writes that blit back into mock AUP Vault cell when no SHINOBU pipeline job is active.
Rejected Alternatives: Scheduling full mock/evaluate/blend job graph just to refresh telemetry; accepting stale mock AUP in crash forensics; adding separate per-frame telemetry job with another dependency owner.
Scalability potential: Low quality keeps 60Hz black-box spatial truth while solver math remains near 5Hz. Middle, High, and Ultra converge toward every-frame solver updates but retain identical mock replay math.
Hardware Impact: Adds O(1) host scalar math and one 128-bit AUP Vault write only on cadence-skipped mock frames. It avoids waking Burst chain and prevents misleading QA dumps on weak devices.
Problem: Task 09 required shader Constant Buffer publication, but runtime visual-sync bridge still treated `Shader.SetGlobalVector` calls as final shader handoff. Vault payload was complete, yet GPU-facing route lacked prewarmed CBuffer upload lane.
Solution: Added explicit `BiomeTransitionShaderPayloadCBufferDTO` at 128 bytes (`float4[8]`) and validated its offsets in `BiomeTransitionNativeLayout`. `LateFrameTick` now uploads completed Vault shader payload through double-buffered `GraphicsBuffer.Target.Constant` named `H8BiomeTransitionPayload`, using `LockBufferForWrite` and `UnsafeUtility.MemCpy`; legacy scalar globals remain only as compatibility mirrors.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving vector globals as sole route; using `GraphicsBuffer.SetData`; creating per-frame managed arrays; moving upload into rendering sibling domain without owner-local contract; shrinking eight-slot payload.
Scalability potential: Low quality still uploads one 128B payload after 5Hz solver cadence while reusing presentation state between solves; Middle/High/Ultra can consume same fixed CBuffer with richer shader-side dither, caustic, and fog logic without changing CPU authority math.
Hardware Impact: Adds one 128B mapped GPU copy only after completed solver publishes and only on platforms supporting constant buffers. It removes architectural risk of per-vector global churn becoming only shader route; Quest-class devices pay bounded visual-sync bandwidth, RTX tier gets single packed payload for overkill shader work.
Problem: `RecordBiomeTransitionTelemetryJob` wrote estimated CPU microsecond value before scheduled pipeline actually completed. That was useful as model, but it was not black-box frame compute time required by Task 16.
Solution: Store `Stopwatch` timestamp when evaluate/blend/publish/acoustic/telemetry chain is scheduled. After `LateFrameTick` observes `_pipelineHandle.IsCompleted` and finalizes through `DispatcherJobSwap`, patch most recent 64B telemetry row and `BiomeTransitionCounterDTO.LastCpuMicroseconds` with measured schedule-to-finalize elapsed microseconds. Cadence-reused frames remain explicit zero-cost reuse records.
Rejected Alternatives: Calling `Complete()` to measure synchronously; trusting estimate as forensic truth; adding managed profiler samples inside Burst jobs; recording timing only in editor logs.
Scalability potential: Low quality still records 0 us reuse rows on skipped cadence frames and measured timings on actual 5Hz solver frames. Middle/High/Ultra get measured timings as cadence approaches every frame, so thermal tuning can compare real solver wall time across continuum.
Hardware Impact: Adds one `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp()` at schedule, one timestamp read at finalize, and one existing Vault-row scalar patch. It does not block main thread and prevents misleading microsecond reports on i3/MX350 or Quest-class hardware.
Problem: first timing patch still let `FastTick` return immediately while `_pipelineScheduled` was true, even if job had already completed before next fast phase. That delayed ready-only finalization until `LateFrameTick`, left one avoidable telemetry gap, and made naive fix risky because rescheduling before visual sync could overwrite shader payload before `H8BiomeTransitionPayload` was uploaded.
Solution: Added `TryFinalizeCompletedPipeline()` and `_pendingShaderPayloadUpload`. `FastTick` now finalizes only already-completed pipeline handles without blocking; if completed payload is waiting for LateFrame upload, it writes 64B reuse telemetry row and refuses to schedule new solver over same Vault shader payload. `LateFrameTick` performs CBuffer upload and clears pending flag. Shutdown and Vault rebinding clear pending flag.
Rejected Alternatives: Moving shader upload into `FastTick`; scheduling new pipeline over previous shader payload; writing telemetry while job is still running; calling `Complete()` to force timing proof.
Scalability potential: Low quality keeps 60Hz forensic coverage around 5Hz solver cadence; Middle/High/Ultra avoid visual-sync race while still allowing ready-only finalization as soon as worker jobs finish.
Hardware Impact: Adds one bool branch in `FastTick`/`LateFrameTick` and one 64B reuse telemetry write only when completed payload is waiting for visual sync. It avoids extra frame of stale forensic state without adding main-thread stall.

Decision 09: Binary Rig Parser With Endian Guard
Problem: `TryHydrateRigDefinitionsBinaryCold()` scanned for `leviathan_rig_definitions.h8bin` but always returned false, making binary route fake implementation.
Solution: Add bounded cold parser for 16-byte header and 16-byte aligned rig rows, with accepted `H8LR`/`LVRG` magic and `math.reversebytes` endian handling. Parsed data hydrates segment positions, previous positions, 64B matrices, and 16B constraints in Vault. Missing or invalid payloads still fall back to deterministic mock rig.
Rejected Alternatives: Hand-authoring binary asset was rejected because payload baker is not authoritative here. Throwing on absent payload was rejected because Task 01 requires isolated CI testing. Parsing strings or JSON was rejected because rig constraints are binary/CSV byte paths.
Scalability potential: Low through Ultra share same loaded skeleton truth. Continuous quality later controls how many rows are evaluated, not which binary file is selected.
Hardware Impact: Runtime hot-path gain is 0 us because this is boot/cold path. Stability gain is avoiding boot failure when binary is absent and avoiding divergent mock-vs-binary codepaths.
Decision 10: Exact Named IK Stage Jobs
Problem: Pass 1 folded multiple XML tasks into `LeviathanTerrainIkJob`, which made task reconciliation weak even though runtime behavior existed.

Rejected Alternatives: Renaming existing composite job was rejected because it would churn live runtime and increase merge risk. Adding interface arrays was rejected because IL2CPP virtual dispatch blocks Burst devirtualization.
Scalability potential: Low: one iteration, six-node/fake appendage motion, low shader payload. Middle: partial segment and iteration count. High/Ultra: full matrices, full FABRIK iterations, richer collider proxies and shader-fed motion.
Hardware Impact: named jobs do not add cost unless scheduled; they provide reusable split pipeline for later dispatcher integration. Expected future savings versus monolith scheduling: 20-60 us by skipping whole stages when quality/culling suppresses them.

Decision 16: Replace Telemetry Padding With Forensic Lanes
Problem: Task 16 required root AUP, evaluated bones, average FABRIK iterations, and Burst compute time. 96B terrain telemetry DTO only stored quality and iterations in anonymous padding, which made black-box dump weak evidence.
Solution: Preserve 96B ring-buffer ABI and replace unused padding lanes with named fields: `GlobalQualityWeight` at byte 60, `double3 RootAup` at byte 64, `AverageFabrikIterations` at byte 88, and `BurstSolveMicros` at byte 92. Runtime stamps root AUP from `AbsoluteUniversePosition.ToAbsoluteDouble3()` and patches latest telemetry entry after job completion with measured schedule-to-completion microseconds.

Solution: Keep same Vault bone source and assign colors per segment: green for standard spine, red for head/active IK target chain, blue for tail secondary spring overlay during tail-whip secondary motion.

Problem: Compile proof remains required after modulo-ring patch, but workstation still violates explicit build gate.
Solution: Rechecked CPU and compiler process state. CPU samples were `52.5`, `38.1`, `75.9`; no `dotnet`/`csc` process was active. No build was launched because sample window exceeded 50%.
Rejected Alternatives: Launch dotnet during >50% sample window, or report compile success from static scans.
Scalability potential: No runtime effect.
Hardware Impact: Prevents local compilation from competing with current parallel-agent workload.
2026-05-19 Ultra Polish Pass 8
Problem: first modulo shader patch rounded `_HectonFloraSwayFieldRingOffset` inside `SampleFloraSwayFieldCell`, so ultra trilinear sampling could repeat same global round for up to eight taps.
Solution: Compute integer ring offset once inside `ResolveFloraSwayFieldOffset` and pass it into every nearest/trilinear `SampleFloraSwayFieldCell` call.
Rejected Alternatives: Trust shader compiler common-subexpression elimination, or leave repeated ALU hidden behind visual feature.
Scalability potential: Low nearest mode saves small constant; High/Ultra trilinear mode avoids repeated ring-offset conversion across eight structured-buffer taps.
Hardware Impact: Not profiler-measured; removes redundant scalar/vector conversion work from vertex shader path.
Problem: scheduler treated `_floraSwayFieldActive == false` as center-change proxy, causing inactive but valid centered field to request reset even when wake simply started.
Solution: Split predicates. `centerChanged` now tracks AUP validity and integer cell shift only; `wakeStarted` schedules immediate response when valid inactive field receives active wakes without forcing full reset.
Rejected Alternatives: Preserve blunt inactive reset or delay first wake response until cadence timer expires.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid unnecessary reset churn after quiet periods; Ultra keeps immediate wake response without discarding valid toroidal field.
Hardware Impact: Prevents full active-range reset on wake start when center is valid; exact microseconds pending profiler proof.
Problem: Compile proof remains required after pass 8.
Solution: Rechecked build gate. CPU samples were `20.6`, `15`, `22.4`, but seven external `dotnet` processes were active, so no build was launched.
Rejected Alternatives: Start another dotnet build while other compiler/runtime processes are already active.
Scalability potential: No runtime effect.
Hardware Impact: Prevents compile contention with concurrent agents.
2026-05-19 Ultra Polish Pass 9
Problem: toroidal grid could be verified by source scan, but crash dump could not distinguish full reset from preserved wrapped recenter without reconstructing control flow from logs.
Solution: Add owner-local reset/wrapped-shift telemetry flags and mix current ring offset plus last center-shift cells into existing `FloraSwayFieldTelemetryEntry.StateHash`. DTO remains 64 bytes; no new Vault buffer or managed allocation is introduced.
Rejected Alternatives: Expand telemetry DTO beyond one cache line, add second telemetry buffer, or write managed text per frame.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all use same forensic route; quality changes field density/cadence, not dump ABI.
Hardware Impact: Adds seven integer FNV-style hash mixes only when black-box entry is recorded. No per-node or shader cost; exact microseconds pending profiler proof.
Problem: Compile proof remains required after pass 9.
Solution: Rechecked build gate. CPU samples were `82`, `91`, `92.9`, and seven external `dotnet` processes were active, so no build was launched.
Rejected Alternatives: Start another build while other agents still hold dotnet processes.
Scalability potential: No runtime effect.
Hardware Impact: Prevents local compile contention.
2026-05-19 Ultra Polish Pass 10
Problem: field scaled continuously, but resolution and cell-size were derived directly from current `GlobalQualityWeight`, so tiny thermal/profiler jitter could force repeated active-range resets and GPU upload shape changes.
Solution: Split runtime quality from layout quality. Cadence, source count, displacement gain, and shader interpolation still consume current `GlobalQualityWeight`, while `ResolveFloraSwayLayoutQualityWeight()` commits resolution/cell-size changes only after `0.035` quality delta using `math.step`.
Rejected Alternatives: Binary low/high tiers, per-frame cell-size rebuilds, or delayed coroutine/timer allocation path.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra still breathe continuously in cost and visual response; only expensive topology/layout changes get hysteresis to prevent visible reset churn.
Hardware Impact: Avoids repeated full field resets and 64^3 upload-shape churn during small quality oscillations. Adds one scalar field and constant-time math; exact microseconds pending profiler proof.
Problem: Compile proof remains required after pass 10.
Solution: Rechecked build gate. CPU samples were `100`, `100`, `100`; no `dotnet`/`csc` process was visible, but CPU alone blocks compilation.
Rejected Alternatives: Launch build on saturated machine because compiler processes were absent.
Scalability potential: No runtime effect.
Hardware Impact: Prevents compile contention during current system saturation.
2026-05-19 Ultra Polish Pass 11
Problem: flora sway Vault IDs `71580..71584` were not owner-local in current checkout. Static source scan found SHINOBU_155 physiology respawn already owns `71580..71589` in `Assets/_Project/Scripts/Physiology/ShinobuRespawnData.cs`, so SHINOBU_124 could alias respawn state, telemetry, tuning, or request buffers.
Solution: Move active flora sway Vault IDs to `71650..71654`: displacement field `71650`, metadata `71651`, 300-frame black box `71652`, stiffness rules `71653`, and CSV scratch `71654`. Focused source/doc scan found no `BufferID` owner for that range; incidental `7165xx` values in generated hash files are not Vault handles.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping old range and relying on boot order, adding IDs to shared `BufferID` enum during multi-agent batch, or sharing physiology buffers because they happen to have same numeric value. All three break one fact -> one owner -> one route.
Scalability potential: Runtime math does not change. Low/Middle/High/Ultra quality curves still control resolution, cadence, source budget, gain, and shader interpolation; fix prevents cross-domain memory aliasing at every tier.
Hardware Impact: Prevents undefined data corruption and false black-box evidence. Frame-time delta is 0 us by design; gain is correctness and avoiding catastrophic Vault alias stalls/crashes on i3/MX350 and ARM64 devices.
2026-05-19 Ultra Polish Pass 12
Problem: `ClearFloraSwayDisplacementField()` and `OnOriginShift()` could force-complete in-flight flora displacement job even when goal was only to disable or invalidate presentation data. That violates dependency-chain rule and can stall main thread during origin shifts.
Solution: Add `_floraSwayFieldDiscardScheduledUpload`. Clear/origin-shift now publishes inactive shader globals immediately; if field job is still running, its upload is skipped after natural completion. Metadata is zeroed only when no job is writing it or when scheduled job is already completed, avoiding main-thread write race with final metadata job.
Rejected Alternatives: Force `JobHandle.Complete()` during clear/origin shift, write metadata while `UploadDisplacementTextureJob` may still be running, or let stale completed data upload after field was explicitly disabled.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all keep same visual math. fix matters more on low hardware because 64^3 field job is more likely to collide with origin/clear event under frame pressure.
Hardware Impact: Removes potential main-thread wait from clear/origin-shift presentation invalidation. Exact microseconds are not profiler-measured; worst-case avoided cost is waiting for remaining Burst field chain plus stale GPU upload.
2026-05-19 Ultra Polish Pass 13
Problem: discard-only path avoided main-thread stall but could silently erase forensic difference between deliberately discarded stale upload and normal quiet frame.
Solution: Add `FloraSwayFieldDiscardedUploadFlag` and `RecordDiscardedFloraSwayFieldUpload()`. Completed-but-cleared and in-flight-discarded jobs now write one 64B black-box entry before pending wake count, ring offset, center-shift cells, and pending AUP are cleared. helper reads completed metadata only after job handle is done, validates finite `float4` metadata before using it, and falls back to `VaultMissing`/`NaN` flags instead of trusting corrupt values.
Rejected Alternatives: Treat discard as non-event, dump managed text on clear, expand `FloraSwayFieldTelemetryEntry`, or upload stale data just to preserve visible state sample.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all keep same 16B field and 64B telemetry ABI. Weak devices get same non-blocking discard behavior; high/ultra keep forensic proof when dense 64^3 updates are invalidated by origin shifts.
Hardware Impact: Adds one constant-size telemetry write only when scheduled upload is intentionally discarded. Frame-path savings from pass 12 remain; no new per-node work, no GPU upload, and no managed allocation are introduced.
