===== FILE: Rationale_SHINOBU_155__instant99.md =====
SHINOBU_155 Rationale - Player Death And Reconciliation Sequence
Status: PENDING_COMPILE_RUNTIME_PROOF_EXTERNAL_BRIDGE_ERRORS
Decision 0 - Establish Fresh Batch State
Problem: SHINOBU_155 had no current `Status_` or `Rationale_` files, and batch requires file-backed memory before code work.
Solution: Create fresh status/rationale files before gameplay edits. This preserves task boundaries under context compression and prevents undocumented work.
Rejected Alternatives: Chat-only tracking; modifying gameplay code before source archaeology; reading previous batch logs as authority.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged; this is process state, not runtime feature.
Hardware Impact: Runtime impact 0 us. Editor/process impact irrelevant to i3/MX350 frame time.
Decision 1 - Mandate Set
Problem: Death reconciliation crosses survival, AUP, Vault, SignalBus, shader presentation, and telemetry boundaries.
Solution: Use eight mandates: non-reload reset, zero-GC, ARM64 DTO layout, AUP precision, AUP determinism sync, SignalBus lane segregation, execution phases, post-mortem telemetry.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating death as UI/cutscene only; adding direct concrete dependencies on kinematics/base/AI; binary quality toggles.
Scalability potential: Low uses shortest fade and cheapest shader scalar; Middle keeps normal fade; High adds richer presentation; Ultra may add stronger post-process distortion in VISUAL_SYNC only.
Hardware Impact: Target is one-frame reconciliation under 0.1 ms suspicious threshold. Expected low-end gain is removal of scene reload, asset churn, and forced GC; exact microseconds pending profiler.
Decision 2 - Reconciliation Route
Problem: `HectonPlayerHealth.Die()` has no reload path to delete, but it also has no authoritative AUP/physiology reset and leaves death as managed event/TODO.
Solution: Keep player GameObject alive, emit blittable `PlayerRespawnSignal` through contract lane, restore local health scalar immediately to avoid stuck dead state, and let SHINOBU_155 reconcile Vault-backed physiology/AUP in dispatcher phases.
Rejected Alternatives: Directly referencing Physiology from Gameplay; moving Transform in `Die()`; building loading-screen substitute; waiting for Base Logistics before providing mock medical bay.
Scalability potential: Low uses single scalar blackout and fast decay; Middle adds moderate grain/chromatic scalar; High/Ultra retain longer Dear Lie cover and stronger shader distortion without CPU simulation.
Hardware Impact: Death path removes scene reload/asset churn. Expected low-end gain is frame-time continuity instead of 15 s stall; per-death CPU target is under 100 us and no managed allocation after boot.
Decision 3 - Vault Buffer IDs
Problem: SHINOBU_155 needs persistent buffers but core `BufferID` should not be churned for domain-owned feature.
Solution: Follow existing physiology pattern and define local constants cast to `BufferID` in SHINOBU_155 data file. Use 71604-71613 range after source audit showed 71580-71584 were already documented by SHINOBU_124 and 71592-71603 are owned by submarine autopilot lane.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing `H8Memory.cs`; declaring private persistent `NativeArray` fields; piggybacking respawn state into unrelated physiology DTO bits.
Scalability potential: One owner, one route: every tier reads same Vault state; quality only affects fade curve and shader complexity scalars.
Hardware Impact: Local `BufferID` constants have 0 runtime cost and avoid compile-wall edits in core memory headers.
Decision 4 - Cross-Domain Mesofauna Consumer
Problem: Task 12 explicitly requires Mesofauna to drop player aggro on `PlayerRespawnSignal`, but AI is sibling domain.
Solution: Add only contract-signal snapshot read in `PredatorCognitionDomain`'s existing signal/data stage and clear `TargetHashID`/state when signal marks requested or committed respawn. No direct Physiology type references are introduced.
Rejected Alternatives: managed callback from Physiology into AI; destroying predator targets; scheduling separate job that would need new dependency fence for small same-stage mutation; ignoring Task 12.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra identical data mutation; predator simulation cost decreases for at least one frame after death because hunt state is cleared.
Hardware Impact: Signal scan is bounded to same-frame snapshot and clear is O(active mesofauna). Expected cost is below 10 us for current slot counts; it removes repeated predator targeting after respawn.
Decision 5 - Vault Lock Semantics
Problem: first pass treated `GlobalDataVault.IsAllocationLocked` as hard runtime failure. That would prevent already-created respawn handles from being resolved after boot allocation window closes.
Solution: Split `EnsureVaultState()` into "handles already created" versus "need new handle requests." Allocation lock now blocks only first-time buffer requests; hot-path reads of existing Vault handles continue.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving runtime disabled after allocation lock; using private persistent arrays as fallback; force-unlocking Vault.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra share same preallocated memory. Throttled devices do not pay late allocation retry loop after boot.
Hardware Impact: Removes branch-to-failure path and prevents death reconciliation from falling back to managed component-only state. Estimated saved cost is failure recovery, not frame CPU; hot path remains one handle-created branch.
Decision 6 - Dear Lie Route
Problem: real camera teleport without visual cover is perceptually broken, but UI fade prefab or coroutine would allocate and reintroduce managed transition state.
Solution: Publish `_HectonRespawnDearLieParams` and `_HectonDeathFadeIntensity` through existing shader global Vault bridge, then let `Hecton8_UberNoir.hlsl` darken frame with quality-weighted grain/chromatic bias.
Rejected Alternatives: Canvas overlay; Timeline/coroutine fade; simulated camera travel; scene reload blackout.
Scalability potential: Low uses fast blackout and minimal shader math; Middle keeps grain; High/Ultra spend saved CPU on stronger chromatic/film response.
Hardware Impact: CPU cost is one `float4` publish. Shader work collapses continuously by quality scalar; expected CPU saving versus UI fade/controller is 20-60 us on low-end silicon and eliminates managed transition objects.
Decision 7 - Editor And CSV Human Control
Problem: Designers need to tune death fade and penalties without C# recompiles, but runtime string parsing and editor UI must not leak into gameplay path.
Solution: Keep UI Toolkit tuner under `#if UNITY_EDITOR`, write tuning directly into `RespawnTuningDTO`, use cold precomputed fade-readout LUT to avoid per-refresh string formatting, and parse `respawn_penalty_rules.csv` cold via byte spans into Vault-backed `InventoryDeathPenaltyRuleDTO` rows.
Rejected Alternatives: ScriptableObject-only settings requiring import/recompile; `string.Split`; direct inventory mutation from respawn job.
Scalability potential: Low-to-Ultra all consume same unmanaged tuning DTO. Quality controls fade rate and shader detail; penalty logic stays bounded.
Hardware Impact: Runtime hot path has 0 managed parsing allocation. Cold CSV read is editor/boot only; per-death inventory command emission is one NativeQueue write when enabled.
Decision 8 - Verification Boundary
Problem: full C# build is required for final compile proof, but AGENTS forbids running `dotnet build` while CPU load exceeds 50% or another compiler is active, and user explicitly said not to launch build until needed.
Solution: Run static source scans and CPU/compiler guard first. Current guard found no `dotnet`/`csc` process; CPU samples were `100`, `72.039`, and `29.782`, so compile was deferred because first two samples violated guard and static verification was lower-risk next step.
Rejected Alternatives: Launching build under transient high CPU load; claiming compile proof from static scans; waiting on unrelated system load without continuing docs/static verification.
Scalability potential: Process-only decision. Runtime tier behavior unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Prevents additional compile contention on saturated workstation. Runtime impact 0 us.
Decision 9 - Inventory Penalty Rule Contract Repair
Problem: first penalty route parsed CSV rows but inventory consumed only coarse `DropNonEquippedResources` command. It also hashed item tokens with lowercased byte FNV, while inventory item IDs use `LocHash` UTF-16 FNV over exact persistent IDs. Parsed rules could silently fail to match runtime items.
Solution: Move 16-byte rule row into `InventoryDeathPenaltyRuleDTO` under Core contracts, keep SHINOBU-owned Vault buffer ID, and pass buffer ID/rule count through spare fields in existing 32-byte `InventoryCommandSignal`. Inventory resolves Vault table through cached `IDataVault`, scans bounded rule rows, and applies `DropOnDeath`/`RetainIfEquipped` per item hash without polling `GlobalRegistry` from command consumption. If command claims Vault rule table and table cannot be resolved, Inventory fails closed instead of applying broad fallback drops. CSV parser now accepts raw numeric hashes or computes `LocHash.ComputeUtf8AsUtf16` from byte spans. XML's NativeHashMap wording is intentionally mapped to fixed Vault row table because GlobalDataVault exposes typed buffers, not owned hash containers, and 64-row cap keeps lookup deterministic and memcpy-safe.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct Physiology-to-Inventory calls; duplicating identical DTO in Inventory; managed dictionary/NativeHashMap field in runtime; case-folded hashes that do not match item persistent IDs.
Scalability potential: Low keeps same bounded table scan and can use small death penalty budget; Middle/High/Ultra can author richer per-item rules without code changes. Visual overkill remains bought by shader Dear Lie, not by heavier inventory logic.
Hardware Impact: Hot path adds only bounded rule scan on death frames, not per-frame work. Low-end i3/MX350 impact is expected below 0.1 ms suspicion threshold for current `64` rule capacity; avoids accidental broad item scans caused by mismatched rules.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Removes early survival-loop death loading screen blocker while preserving item-loss rules for first resource collection -> danger -> recovery loop.
Decision 10 - Physics Collision Suspend Consumer
Problem: first implementation set `PlayerRespawnSignalFlags.SuspendCollision`, but Physics did not actually consume it. That left Task 06 only half-proven.
Solution: Patch `HydrodynamicKccRuntime` to read only contract signal snapshot. request or committed respawn packet with `SuspendCollision` sets one-frame `_respawnCollisionBypassFrames` latch keyed by `SignalBus .SnapshotGeneration`; KCC skips `CapsulecastCommand.ScheduleBatch`, bypasses collision hit extraction, passes `CollisionBypass=1` into `KinematicResolutionJob`, and marks debug flags with `FlagRespawnCollisionBypass`. snapshot-generation latch prevents duplicate extension, so suspend remains exactly one snapshot generation.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct Physiology call into Physics; disabling CapsuleCollider; clearing Unity layers; allowing committed and requested signals to produce two collision-free frames.
Scalability potential: Low saves full capsulecast batch on death frame; Middle/High/Ultra keep same deterministic bypass and spend saved CPU on Dear Lie shader cover rather than extra collision work.
Hardware Impact: On respawn frame, one `CapsulecastCommand.ScheduleBatch` plus hit extraction is skipped. Expected saving depends on `entityCapacity * maxHits`, but for player lane it removes physics query and avoids contact correction against stale pre-teleport geometry.
Decision 11 - Deterministic Frame Stamp For Death Request
Problem: `PlayerDeathReconciliationBridge` originally stamped `PlayerRespawnSignal.Frame` with `Time.frameCount`, which is not deterministic dispatcher-facing frame source requested by rollback constraint.
Solution: Stamp request with `TimeSliceScheduler.CurrentFrameId`, which is advanced by master dispatcher pre-simulation route. authoritative reconciliation job still records `DispatcherJobContext.Frame`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `Time.frameCount`; adding direct SystemDispatcher API; storing managed clock singleton in Gameplay.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged; this removes nondeterministic metadata drift rather than changing visual cost.
Hardware Impact: Runtime impact is one static uint read instead of Unity time call. meaningful gain is rollback trace consistency, not frame time.
Decision 12 - Core Signal Lane Authority Repair
Problem: `PlayerRespawnSignal` existed as contract payload and local producers configured it, but Core did not yet own its direct flush/clear, finite guard, layout validation, or IL2CPP preservation entry. That left route dependent on local fallback registration instead of same explicit GlobalSignals authority used by other first-party lanes.
Solution: Added `PlayerRespawnSignal` to `GlobalSignals` direct pre-simulation flush and post-simulation clear, registered its central capacity through `InitializeCategorySignalLanes`, validated 96-byte payload size, added finite sanitizer for both `double3` AUPs plus phase/collision-frame bounds, added `HectonSignalLaneContract.PlayerRespawnSignal` with stable hash `0x5253504E`, and preserved closed generic lane in `SignalWardenRuntime`. payload now exposes its lane capacity constants so Gameplay and Physiology early-boot calls reuse same numbers instead of hardcoded duplicates.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving lane as fallback-only; adding direct Gameplay-to-Physiology callback; moving signal into sibling runtime assembly; accepting unguarded `double3` AUP payloads.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra consume same bounded lane: expected capacity 8, max frame signals 16, low-tier frame signals 4. quality-dependent cost remains in shader fade and KCC work avoided on respawn frame, not in extra broadcast traffic.
Hardware Impact: Prevents lost or wiped respawn snapshot without increasing steady-state frame work. On low-end silicon, bounded direct lane avoids fallback registry dispatch for this death route and rejects non-finite AUPs before AI/Physics consumers can ingest corrupted data.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Protects first death/recovery loop from signal-routing failure where health resets locally but AI/KCC/physiology consumers never see authoritative respawn packet.
Decision 13 - Visual Sync Phase Discipline
Problem: `PlayerDeathReconciliationBridge` emitted contract signal and also pushed `HectonShaderGlobalDataVaultBridge.PublishRespawnDearLie` immediately from Gameplay. That created second visual route outside `VISUAL_SYNC` and could allocate/initialize shader-global Vault storage from fatal-damage seam if graphics slot buffer was not prewarmed.
Solution: Remove Gameplay shader write. Gameplay now emits only `PlayerRespawnSignal`. first visual cover is authored by `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob` into `RespawnFadeDTO`, then `ShinobuRespawnReconciliationRuntime` publishes Dear Lie scalar during its VisualSync adapter.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping duplicate emergency shader write; adding Gameplay-to-Rendering direct dependency; using UI overlay fallback; forcing shader-global Vault allocation from fatal damage.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra still consume same continuous `GlobalQualityWeight` in fade job and shader. change removes non-authoritative route; it does not reduce visual overkill on high tier.
Hardware Impact: Death detection now performs one bounded signal enqueue and no shader-global DataVault lookup/write. shader scalar update remains in VisualSync, where graphics state belongs.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Prevents first death recovery from mutating rendering state before authoritative Vault reconciliation has accepted respawn request.
Decision 14 - Visual Sync Job Fence Repair
Problem: `VisualSyncTick` read `RespawnFadeDTO` after `PostSimulationTick` attempted non-blocking reclaim, but it did not re-check active job fence. If fade job was still running, VisualSync could read Vault row while Burst still owned writes.
Solution: Add non-blocking fence gate at start of VisualSync. If `_activeHandle` is not completed, VisualSync returns and keeps previous shader scalar. If it is completed, `CompleteActiveJobIfReady(false)` reclaims handle before reading fade row.
Rejected Alternatives: Calling `JobHandle.Complete()` unconditionally in VisualSync; allowing read/write race; duplicating fade state in managed field; publishing Gameplay-phase fallback shader scalar.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. only behavior difference is correctness under slow frame: weak hardware can skip VisualSync publish instead of stalling main thread.
Hardware Impact: Prevents main-thread block and native data race. In overloaded frames cost is one `IsCompleted` branch and no shader-global write until job fence is safe.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Protects death recovery visuals from stale or half-written fade values during early survival loop.
Decision 15 - Cross-Frame Writer Fence Repair
Problem: `ScheduleSimulation` could start new reset/fade job over same Vault pointers while previous frame's `_activeHandle` was still in flight. VisualSync was protected, but simulation producer could still stack two writers to `RespawnStateDTO`/`RespawnFadeDTO` rows.
Solution: Gate `ScheduleSimulation` on `_jobScheduled`. If prior handle is incomplete, return `JobHandle.CombineDependencies(dependsOn, _activeHandle)` and do not schedule another writer. If it is complete, reclaim it non-blockingly and then schedule next job.
Rejected Alternatives: Completing old job unconditionally in Simulation; allowing overlapping writers; copying state into second private buffer; adding managed queue of pending deaths.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged; overloaded devices naturally skip one respawn/fade update rather than blocking or racing.
Hardware Impact: Avoids false sharing/data races on Vault rows with one branch and one combined dependency in rare slow-job case. No new persistent memory is allocated.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Prevents repeated lethal events during early survival from corrupting active respawn row while previous reconciliation is still executing.
Decision 16 - Deterministic Frame Source Sweep
Problem: Static verification still found Unity `Time.frameCount` in health/survival signal payloads adjacent to lethal physiology traffic. `PlayerRespawnSignal` was already dispatcher-stamped, but `SurvivalVitalsChangedSignal` on death and physiology/vital warning freshness were still in Unity frame space.
Solution: Replace those frame stamps and freshness delta with `TimeSliceScheduler.CurrentFrameId`, dispatcher frame source already used by respawn bridge.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving Unity frame metadata around death route; adding new clock service; changing signal payload layouts; touching unrelated gameplay time users outside SHINOBU's health/survival files.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. value is deterministic trace coherence under rollback and black-box replay, not visual fidelity.
Hardware Impact: Static uint read cost is equivalent or cheaper than Unity frame access. important gain is removal of rollback drift source from lethal survival telemetry.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Keeps first death/recovery loop's vitals, physiology, and respawn signals in one frame domain for post-mortem correlation.
Decision 17 - Compile Wall Boundary
Problem: After CPU/process guard passed, `dotnet build Hecton8.Core.csproj --no-restore` failed before SHINOBU code on `CS2001` because `Assets/_Project/Scripts/Construction/LogisticsPipeEvents.cs` is deleted while still referenced by generated project.
Solution: Treat this as unrelated compile wall and do not create construction-domain stub or mutate generated project file. Continue static verification and record exact blocker for integrator.
Rejected Alternatives: Fabricating missing Construction file; editing `Hecton8.Core.csproj` by hand; rerunning build repeatedly against same missing source; reverting another agent's deletion.
Scalability potential: Runtime tier behavior unchanged. This is integration hygiene, not SHINOBU feature logic.
Hardware Impact: Prevents wasted compile loops. Runtime impact 0 us.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: respawn route cannot receive compile proof until construction source/project reference is reconciled.
Decision 18 - Cached Vault Authority Tightening
Problem: `ShinobuRespawnReconciliationRuntime.ResolveVault()` could be called from dispatcher phases and would fall back to `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` if `_dataVault` was null. That violates cold-discovery rule and hides missing boot wiring behind hot-path service polling.
Solution: Split route: dispatcher phases use cached `_dataVault` only and fail closed when absent; `ResolveVaultCold()` retains `GlobalRegistry`/latest-Vault fallback for Awake, Start, hot-swap/editor utilities, and gizmos.
Rejected Alternatives: Polling `GlobalRegistry` in PreSimulation/Simulation/VisualSync; storing private NativeArrays as fallback; direct construction of local Vault; throwing exceptions on missing Vault.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. Weak devices avoid possible cold service lookup branch in death/fade ticks.
Hardware Impact: Hot path removes service locator fallback. Estimated saving is tiny per tick, but real gain is architectural: no hidden global lookup in deterministic dispatcher phases.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Death recovery now either runs on boot-injected Vault or fails closed with no scene reload/object churn.
Decision 19 - Legacy Managed Death Event Ejection
Problem: Reconciled deaths still invoked legacy managed `OnDeath` listeners before local reset. `HectonSurvivalSystem.OnDeath` currently reaches PDA logbook code and can create UI/logbook side effects inside fatal frame, conflicting with zero-GC reconciliation mandate.
Solution: Reconciled deaths return immediately after signal emission and local scalar reset. Managed `OnDeath`, `PlayerDiedEvent`, and development log fallback remain only for unreconciled failure path.
Rejected Alternatives: Publishing `PlayerDiedEvent` for reconciled death; keeping PDA logbook side effects in fatal frame; adding direct PDA callback; allocating replacement managed event.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. Death truth is now signal/Vault black box; presentation is shader-driven.
Hardware Impact: Removes managed delegate fan-out and PDA/meta side effects from reconciled death frame. Exact GC delta requires Unity Profiler, but code path no longer calls known `OnDeath` subscriber on successful reconciliation.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first lethal survival event no longer risks dragging journal/meta systems into one-frame respawn path.
Decision 20 - Current-Frame Respawn Snapshot Repair
Problem: Gameplay can only publish lethal request immediately, so first `PlayerRespawnSignal` starts with `RespawnAUP = DeathAUP`. Physiology resolves actual med-bay AUP later in `PreSimulation`. If that resolved target is only stored in Vault or republished as queued signal, same-frame Physics/AI consumers can see stale death AUP or wait one frame.
Solution: Keep Physiology as sole med-bay resolver, then mutate current `SignalBus ` snapshot in-place with `SignalBus .TransformSnapshot`. transformer writes resolved `RespawnAUP`, `MedicalBayHashID`, `Requested`, `Committed`, `SuspendCollision`, translated med-bay flags, and clamps `SuspendCollisionFrames` to payload maximum. `HydrodynamicKccRuntime` now treats request or committed respawn packets as eligible, while snapshot-generation latch preserves one-frame collision bypass.
Rejected Alternatives: Queueing second committed signal for next frame; making Gameplay query med-bay Vault state; adding direct Physiology-to-Physics call; keeping KCC dependent on producer's original `Requested` bit only; leaving `math.max(byte, byte)` in transformer.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged for simulation truth. Same-frame correction prevents visual/physics pop on weak devices and lets high-tier Dear Lie shader spend more time on presentation instead of covering avoidable stale-collision frame.
Hardware Impact: Adds O(snapshotCount) unmanaged value-transform over lane capped at 16 events per frame; expected cost is below 1 us on i3/MX350 for normal 0-1 death packet traffic. Avoids one extra frame of stale capsule collision and queued duplicate signal.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death/recovery loop now gives KCC and mesofauna resolved med-bay AUP in same frame request is accepted, without loading screen or object churn.
Decision 21 - Kinematic Sector Denominator Guard
Problem: `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob.WriteKinematic()` divided target AUP by `HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble`. project contract expects that constant to be valid, but NaN mandate requires every division feeding physics truth to be guarded locally.
Solution: Clamp denominator with `math.max(HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble, 0.0001d)` before calculating sector. existing local-position math then subtracts guarded sector root and casts only local residual to `float3`.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting global contract constant without local guard; moving sector split to managed code; using `Transform.position`; adding exception checks in Burst path.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. This is correctness hardening, not visual cost. It prevents single bad constant or corrupted contract payload from poisoning KCC/rollback state.
Hardware Impact: One `math.max` in rare respawn job. Expected cost is below measurement noise on i3/MX350 and buys NaN containment for physics truth.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death recovery cannot poison player kinematic row through zero sector-size denominator.
Decision 22 - Local AUP Clamp Range Guard
Problem: After sector-division fix, `SafeLocal()` and runtime `AupDeltaToFloat3()` still used `HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble` directly as clamp range. It is not division, but if that constant were corrupted to zero or non-finite, local validation vectors could collapse or propagate invalid values before fallback path.
Solution: Add `SafeAupClampMeters()` in Burst job file and runtime file, each returning `math.max(HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble, 0.0001d)`. Local AUP residual conversion and medical-bay validation now use guarded range before casting to `float3`.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting contract constant in clamp helpers; duplicating raw `math.max` calls at each clamp site; moving validation into managed `Vector3` math; widening patch into unrelated AUP systems.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. This is deterministic containment; visual overkill budget stays in Dear Lie shader.
Hardware Impact: One double `math.max` per local conversion helper call on rare respawn/validation path. Expected cost is below measurement noise on i3/MX350; gain is preventing bad clamp range from poisoning target validation or rollback kinematic truth.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first lethal recovery route now protects both sector split and local validation clamp before med-bay AUP selection reaches Physics/Fauna consumers.
Decision 23 - Med-Bay Authority De-Duplication
Problem: `ShinobuRespawnReconciliationRuntime` already resolves med-bay target in `PreSimulation`, writes `RespawnStateDTO`, and transforms current `PlayerRespawnSignal` snapshot. `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob` then repeated same nearest-med-bay scan as its primary route, creating two target-selection authorities in one death frame.
Solution: Keep `PreSimulation` as owner of med-bay resolution. `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob` now consumes staged `RespawnStateDTO.TargetAUP` and `MedicalBayHashID` when staged state is pending, finite, and either has med-bay hash or explicit fallback flag. Staged route flags are applied only when staged target is accepted; fallback scan recomputes mock/invalid/fallback flags itself so stale state cannot leak into new death request. committed request row now preserves `MockMedicalBay` along with invalid/fallback/penalty flags for black-box correlation. job scans `MedicalBayRespawnPointDTO` rows only as fail-closed fallback when staged state is missing or invalid.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving duplicate med-bay scans as "harmless"; moving med-bay selection into Gameplay; expanding `RespawnRequestDTO` layout to carry another target copy; adding direct Base Logistics dependency to job; deleting fallback scan and making job brittle under boot/order failures.
Scalability potential: Low removes redundant Burst work from death frame while keeping deterministic fallback. Middle/High/Ultra keep same authoritative target and spend saved CPU budget on Dear Lie shader, not on second simulation truth lookup.
Hardware Impact: Normal death path removes one O(medBayCount) scan from `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob`; with current capacity this is up to 8 row reads and AUP local-distance evaluations avoided on i3/MX350. Fallback path remains bounded and only runs on missing/non-finite staged state.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death/recovery loop now has one med-bay owner in accepted frame, reducing chance of Physics/Fauna seeing target chosen by one path while Kinematic truth is chosen by another.
Decision 24 - Hot-Path Literal New Erasure
Problem: respawn path had no managed gameplay allocations, but `new` value-type/object-initializer syntax remained in Burst jobs, Simulation job scheduling, VisualSync shader payload publishing, cold DTO defaults, and helper return paths. That creates bad review evidence and can hide unnecessary struct construction/copy patterns in exact files that must be trivially memcpy/Burst-readable.
Solution: Rewrite SHINOBU job bodies and hot dispatcher code to `default` locals with explicit field assignment. `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob`, `UpdateRespawnFadeJob`, VisualSync `Vector4`, `RespawnFadeDTO`, `InventoryDeathPenaltyRuleDTO`, fallback `double3`, local `float3`, editor gizmo offsets, and telemetry/physiology DTO writes now avoid literal `new` syntax. Remaining `new` sites are cold and explicit: one runtime host GameObject, four dispatcher adapter objects, cold FileStream/BinaryWriter dump/CSV IO, stack-only `Span ` constructor, and teardown/service-replacement `JobHandle.Complete()` fences.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating value-type `new` as harmless and leaving noisy hot-path evidence; adding managed pools for structs; removing cold runtime host without proving another dispatcher owner exists; replacing teardown `Complete()` with unsafe native-buffer release while job may still own pointers.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged in behavior. low-tier benefit is tighter Burst/codegen hygiene and fewer false positives in allocation scans; high/ultra keep same VisualSync shader overkill route.
Hardware Impact: No measured microsecond saving is claimed from syntax alone. important i3/MX350 impact is risk removal: job scheduling, shader payload publish, and Burst DTO writes now have no literal `new` evidence, and static scans can distinguish hot path from cold boot/editor IO.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death/recovery loop now has cleaner zero-GC proof surface: lethal request -> Vault reconciliation -> shader Dear Lie publish uses explicit unmanaged value mutation, not initializer syntax that can be misread as allocation.
Decision 25 - Death-Vicinity Signal Initializer And Pack Purge
Problem: After SHINOBU respawn files were cleaned, adjacent health/survival code still published mutable GlobalSignals via object-initializer `new`, and `SurvivalDatabaseItemRecord` used `[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential, Pack = 1, Size = 20)]`. signal initializers are value-type syntax rather than heap allocation, but they weaken zero-GC evidence in fatal-damage vicinity. `Pack=1` is direct ARM64 alignment violation even if row is cold parsed.
Solution: Rewrite `VitalWarningSignal`, `PhysiologyStateSignal`, and `SurvivalVitalsChangedSignal` publishers to `default` plus field assignment in `HectonPlayerHealth`, `HectonSurvivalSystem`, and `ShinobuPhysiologyRuntime`. Replace `SurvivalDatabaseItemRecord` with explicit 24-byte layout: `StableHash` offset 0, `MassKilograms` 4, `VolumeLiters` 8, `EnergyDensityMegajoulesPerKilogram` 12, `BaseDurability` 16, `_pad0` 20.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving `Pack=1` because row is cold; broad-refactoring readonly `TraumaHudSignal` constructors in HUD event lane; changing survival database parser contract; adding new DTO type and forcing downstream copies.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. fix removes alignment risk and noisy signal construction evidence without changing visual quality or survival tuning.
Hardware Impact: `SurvivalDatabaseItemRecord` grows from 20 to 24 bytes, 20% cold staging-row increase for 256-row cap, but removes unaligned ARM64 row reads. Mutable signal publish cost remains equivalent and cleaner for Burst/IL2CPP inspection.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first lethal survival loop now has no mutable GlobalSignal object-initializer `new` in health/survival death-adjacent publishers and no `Pack=1` row in survival data parser used by same component.
Decision 26 - VisualSync Idle Publish And Registry-Poll Cull
Problem: `ShinobuRespawnReconciliationRuntime.VisualSyncTick()` published respawn Dear Lie shader payload every VisualSync frame once Vault row existed, even when `DeathFadeIntensity` was zero and effect was inactive. publish used bridge's no-argument method, whose slot resolution starts from `GlobalRegistry.DataVault`; that hid registry poll behind otherwise cached SHINOBU VisualSync route.
Solution: Add `_respawnDearLieVisualActive` as dirty latch. VisualSync now publishes while fade scalar or active flag is live, then publishes exactly one zero payload to clear shader state and returns on later idle frames. Add `HectonShaderGlobalDataVaultBridge.PublishRespawnDearLie(IDataVault, Vector4)` and route SHINOBU through its cached `_dataVault`. Core bridge now has `TryPrepareSlotsVault(IDataVault)` so caller-cached Vault routes reuse same slot validation without entering `GlobalRegistry.DataVault`. bridge now uses `default` field-assignment helpers for `float4` and `Vector4`, removing typed `new float4`/`new Vector4` from whole file.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving idle shader publishes in place; making Physiology write raw shader-global slot `19` directly; moving shader publication back into Gameplay; adding sibling Rendering dependency; globally refactoring every shader bridge publisher in this SHINOBU pass.
Scalability potential: Low skips all idle Dear Lie bridge work after final zero-clear and still exits visual cover fastest through `GlobalQualityWeight`. Middle/High/Ultra keep same active-frame chromatic/grain path, but only pay for it while effect is actually covering teleport.
Hardware Impact: Steady-state respawn VisualSync cost drops to branch and early return after zero-clear. Death-frame active cost remains one cached-Vault bridge write plus shader/global-dispatch handoff. No measured microseconds are claimed until profiler proof; static cost class removes one hidden hot registry lookup and idle shader slot write from normal gameplay.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death recovery still blacks out immediately, but post-recovery route no longer keeps touching shader-global state every frame during resource collection -> danger -> recovery loop.
Decision 27 - Hot Dispatcher Vault Allocation Gate
Problem: `PreSimulationTick`, `ScheduleSimulation`, `VisualSyncTick`, and fault-dump reads still called `EnsureVaultState(vault)`. That method is correct for cold boot because it requests Vault buffers, but using it as dispatcher-phase guard creates hidden allocation-capable route if boot order fails.
Solution: Add `HasHotVaultState(IDataVault)` as pure `vault != null && AreVaultHandlesCreated()` check. Dispatcher phases, default hydration after successful cold ensure, and telemetry dump reads now use this hot gate. Allocation-capable `EnsureVaultState(...)` remains restricted to Awake, Start, DataVault hot-swap rehydration, and editor/manual utilities.
Rejected Alternatives: Letting dispatcher ticks lazily allocate missing Vault buffers; throwing exceptions on missing handles; polling `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` from hot phases; adding private native fallback buffers.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged in visible behavior. Weak devices avoid surprise first-death allocation path; high/ultra still spend their budget on Dear Lie shader only while active.
Hardware Impact: Hot path removes cold allocation branch from every dispatcher phase. Expected steady-state saving is few branches, not measurable claim until profiler proof; material gain is deterministic H-PHI ownership and no runtime buffer request from death/fade ticks.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death/recovery loop now either runs on boot-created Vault handles or fails closed without allocating, reloading, or fabricating owner-local buffers.
Decision 28 - Reconciled Death Legacy Telemetry Ejection
Problem: `HectonPlayerHealth.Die()` published `GlobalTelemetryBus.PublishPlayerDeath()` before respawn bridge, and `HectonSurvivalSystem.CheckLethalConditions()` called `RecordDeathTelemetry()` before bridge. global telemetry bus can cold-initialize buffers and uses legacy frame source; survival recorder builds human-readable log. Neither belongs in zero-GC reconciled death frame because SHINOBU already owns Vault black-box telemetry.
Solution: Move `GlobalTelemetryBus.PublishPlayerDeath()`, `RecordDeathTelemetry()`, `OnDeath`, and `PlayerDiedEvent` to unreconciled fallback only. Add finite AUP gate to health death AUP resolution before emitting `PlayerRespawnSignal`; fallback runtime positions now use `default` field assignment instead of `new Vector3`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy telemetry before bridge; duplicating black-box death data into managed logs on successful reconciliation; emitting zero AUP from health when `CurrentAup` is non-finite; adding direct dependency on telemetry from SHINOBU jobs.
Scalability potential: Low avoids surprise legacy telemetry/log work on death frame. Middle/High/Ultra keep same Vault black-box and Dear Lie shader route; richer post-death presentation must remain shader-side, not managed logging.
Hardware Impact: Removes possible cold telemetry initialization and human-readable log construction from successful death reconciliation. Exact microseconds require profiler proof; static risk removed is managed/global side route before one-frame Vault reset.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Early oxygen/integrity death now either reconciles via SignalBus/Vault only or falls back to legacy death UX if bridge fails.

===== FILE: Rationale_SHINOBU_155__late1.md =====
SHINOBU_155 Rationale - Player Death And Reconciliation Sequence
Status: PENDING_COMPILE_RUNTIME_PROOF_EXTERNAL_BRIDGE_ERRORS
Decision 0 - Establish Fresh Batch State
Problem: SHINOBU_155 had no current `Status_` or `Rationale_` files, and batch requires file-backed memory before code work.
Solution: Create fresh status/rationale files before gameplay edits. This preserves task boundaries under context compression and prevents undocumented work.
Rejected Alternatives: Chat-only tracking; modifying gameplay code before source archaeology; reading previous batch logs as authority.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged; this is process state, not runtime feature.
Hardware Impact: Runtime impact 0 us. Editor/process impact irrelevant to i3/MX350 frame time.
Decision 1 - Mandate Set
Problem: Death reconciliation crosses survival, AUP, Vault, SignalBus, shader presentation, and telemetry boundaries.
Solution: Use eight mandates: non-reload reset, zero-GC, ARM64 DTO layout, AUP precision, AUP determinism sync, SignalBus lane segregation, execution phases, post-mortem telemetry.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating death as UI/cutscene only; adding direct concrete dependencies on kinematics/base/AI; binary quality toggles.
Scalability potential: Low uses shortest fade and cheapest shader scalar; Middle keeps normal fade; High adds richer presentation; Ultra may add stronger post-process distortion in VISUAL_SYNC only.
Hardware Impact: Target is one-frame reconciliation under 0.1 ms suspicious threshold. Expected low-end gain is removal of scene reload, asset churn, and forced GC; exact microseconds pending profiler.
Decision 2 - Reconciliation Route
Problem: `HectonPlayerHealth.Die()` has no reload path to delete, but it also has no authoritative AUP/physiology reset and leaves death as managed event/TODO.
Solution: Keep player GameObject alive, emit blittable `PlayerRespawnSignal` through contract lane, restore local health scalar immediately to avoid stuck dead state, and let SHINOBU_155 reconcile Vault-backed physiology/AUP in dispatcher phases.
Rejected Alternatives: Directly referencing Physiology from Gameplay; moving Transform in `Die()`; building loading-screen substitute; waiting for Base Logistics before providing mock medical bay.
Scalability potential: Low uses single scalar blackout and fast decay; Middle adds moderate grain/chromatic scalar; High/Ultra retain longer Dear Lie cover and stronger shader distortion without CPU simulation.
Hardware Impact: Death path removes scene reload/asset churn. Expected low-end gain is frame-time continuity instead of 15 s stall; per-death CPU target is under 100 us and no managed allocation after boot.
Decision 3 - Vault Buffer IDs
Problem: SHINOBU_155 needs persistent buffers but core `BufferID` should not be churned for domain-owned feature.
Solution: Follow existing physiology pattern and define local constants cast to `BufferID` in SHINOBU_155 data file. Use 71604-71613 range after source audit showed 71580-71584 were already documented by SHINOBU_124 and 71592-71603 are owned by submarine autopilot lane.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing `H8Memory.cs`; declaring private persistent `NativeArray` fields; piggybacking respawn state into unrelated physiology DTO bits.
Scalability potential: One owner, one route: every tier reads same Vault state; quality only affects fade curve and shader complexity scalars.
Hardware Impact: Local `BufferID` constants have 0 runtime cost and avoid compile-wall edits in core memory headers.
Decision 4 - Cross-Domain Mesofauna Consumer
Problem: Task 12 explicitly requires Mesofauna to drop player aggro on `PlayerRespawnSignal`, but AI is sibling domain.
Solution: Add only contract-signal snapshot read in `PredatorCognitionDomain`'s existing signal/data stage and clear `TargetHashID`/state when signal marks requested or committed respawn. No direct Physiology type references are introduced.
Rejected Alternatives: managed callback from Physiology into AI; destroying predator targets; scheduling separate job that would need new dependency fence for small same-stage mutation; ignoring Task 12.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra identical data mutation; predator simulation cost decreases for at least one frame after death because hunt state is cleared.
Hardware Impact: Signal scan is bounded to same-frame snapshot and clear is O(active mesofauna). Expected cost is below 10 us for current slot counts; it removes repeated predator targeting after respawn.
Decision 5 - Vault Lock Semantics
Problem: first pass treated `GlobalDataVault.IsAllocationLocked` as hard runtime failure. That would prevent already-created respawn handles from being resolved after boot allocation window closes.
Solution: Split `EnsureVaultState()` into "handles already created" versus "need new handle requests." Allocation lock now blocks only first-time buffer requests; hot-path reads of existing Vault handles continue.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving runtime disabled after allocation lock; using private persistent arrays as fallback; force-unlocking Vault.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra share same preallocated memory. Throttled devices do not pay late allocation retry loop after boot.
Hardware Impact: Removes branch-to-failure path and prevents death reconciliation from falling back to managed component-only state. Estimated saved cost is failure recovery, not frame CPU; hot path remains one handle-created branch.
Decision 6 - Dear Lie Route
Problem: real camera teleport without visual cover is perceptually broken, but UI fade prefab or coroutine would allocate and reintroduce managed transition state.
Solution: Publish `_HectonRespawnDearLieParams` and `_HectonDeathFadeIntensity` through existing shader global Vault bridge, then let `Hecton8_UberNoir.hlsl` darken frame with quality-weighted grain/chromatic bias.
Rejected Alternatives: Canvas overlay; Timeline/coroutine fade; simulated camera travel; scene reload blackout.
Scalability potential: Low uses fast blackout and minimal shader math; Middle keeps grain; High/Ultra spend saved CPU on stronger chromatic/film response.
Hardware Impact: CPU cost is one `float4` publish. Shader work collapses continuously by quality scalar; expected CPU saving versus UI fade/controller is 20-60 us on low-end silicon and eliminates managed transition objects.
Decision 7 - Editor And CSV Human Control
Problem: Designers need to tune death fade and penalties without C# recompiles, but runtime string parsing and editor UI must not leak into gameplay path.
Solution: Keep UI Toolkit tuner under `#if UNITY_EDITOR`, write tuning directly into `RespawnTuningDTO`, use cold precomputed fade-readout LUT to avoid per-refresh string formatting, and parse `respawn_penalty_rules.csv` cold via byte spans into Vault-backed `InventoryDeathPenaltyRuleDTO` rows.
Rejected Alternatives: ScriptableObject-only settings requiring import/recompile; `string.Split`; direct inventory mutation from respawn job.
Scalability potential: Low-to-Ultra all consume same unmanaged tuning DTO. Quality controls fade rate and shader detail; penalty logic stays bounded.
Hardware Impact: Runtime hot path has 0 managed parsing allocation. Cold CSV read is editor/boot only; per-death inventory command emission is one NativeQueue write when enabled.
Decision 8 - Verification Boundary
Problem: full C# build is required for final compile proof, but AGENTS forbids running `dotnet build` while CPU load exceeds 50% or another compiler is active, and user explicitly said not to launch build until needed.
Solution: Run static source scans and CPU/compiler guard first. Current guard found no `dotnet`/`csc` process; CPU samples were `100`, `72.039`, and `29.782`, so compile was deferred because first two samples violated guard and static verification was lower-risk next step.
Rejected Alternatives: Launching build under transient high CPU load; claiming compile proof from static scans; waiting on unrelated system load without continuing docs/static verification.
Scalability potential: Process-only decision. Runtime tier behavior unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Prevents additional compile contention on saturated workstation. Runtime impact 0 us.
Decision 9 - Inventory Penalty Rule Contract Repair
Problem: first penalty route parsed CSV rows but inventory consumed only coarse `DropNonEquippedResources` command. It also hashed item tokens with lowercased byte FNV, while inventory item IDs use `LocHash` UTF-16 FNV over exact persistent IDs. Parsed rules could silently fail to match runtime items.
Solution: Move 16-byte rule row into `InventoryDeathPenaltyRuleDTO` under Core contracts, keep SHINOBU-owned Vault buffer ID, and pass buffer ID/rule count through spare fields in existing 32-byte `InventoryCommandSignal`. Inventory resolves Vault table through cached `IDataVault`, scans bounded rule rows, and applies `DropOnDeath`/`RetainIfEquipped` per item hash without polling `GlobalRegistry` from command consumption. If command claims Vault rule table and table cannot be resolved, Inventory fails closed instead of applying broad fallback drops. CSV parser now accepts raw numeric hashes or computes `LocHash.ComputeUtf8AsUtf16` from byte spans. XML's NativeHashMap wording is intentionally mapped to fixed Vault row table because GlobalDataVault exposes typed buffers, not owned hash containers, and 64-row cap keeps lookup deterministic and memcpy-safe.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct Physiology-to-Inventory calls; duplicating identical DTO in Inventory; managed dictionary/NativeHashMap field in runtime; case-folded hashes that do not match item persistent IDs.
Scalability potential: Low keeps same bounded table scan and can use small death penalty budget; Middle/High/Ultra can author richer per-item rules without code changes. Visual overkill remains bought by shader Dear Lie, not by heavier inventory logic.
Hardware Impact: Hot path adds only bounded rule scan on death frames, not per-frame work. Low-end i3/MX350 impact is expected below 0.1 ms suspicion threshold for current `64` rule capacity; avoids accidental broad item scans caused by mismatched rules.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Removes early survival-loop death loading screen blocker while preserving item-loss rules for first resource collection -> danger -> recovery loop.
Decision 10 - Physics Collision Suspend Consumer
Problem: first implementation set `PlayerRespawnSignalFlags.SuspendCollision`, but Physics did not actually consume it. That left Task 06 only half-proven.
Solution: Patch `HydrodynamicKccRuntime` to read only contract signal snapshot. request or committed respawn packet with `SuspendCollision` sets one-frame `_respawnCollisionBypassFrames` latch keyed by `SignalBus .SnapshotGeneration`; KCC skips `CapsulecastCommand.ScheduleBatch`, bypasses collision hit extraction, passes `CollisionBypass=1` into `KinematicResolutionJob`, and marks debug flags with `FlagRespawnCollisionBypass`. snapshot-generation latch prevents duplicate extension, so suspend remains exactly one snapshot generation.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct Physiology call into Physics; disabling CapsuleCollider; clearing Unity layers; allowing committed and requested signals to produce two collision-free frames.
Scalability potential: Low saves full capsulecast batch on death frame; Middle/High/Ultra keep same deterministic bypass and spend saved CPU on Dear Lie shader cover rather than extra collision work.
Hardware Impact: On respawn frame, one `CapsulecastCommand.ScheduleBatch` plus hit extraction is skipped. Expected saving depends on `entityCapacity * maxHits`, but for player lane it removes physics query and avoids contact correction against stale pre-teleport geometry.
Decision 11 - Deterministic Frame Stamp For Death Request
Problem: `PlayerDeathReconciliationBridge` originally stamped `PlayerRespawnSignal.Frame` with `Time.frameCount`, which is not deterministic dispatcher-facing frame source requested by rollback constraint.
Solution: Stamp request with `TimeSliceScheduler.CurrentFrameId`, which is advanced by master dispatcher pre-simulation route. authoritative reconciliation job still records `DispatcherJobContext.Frame`.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping `Time.frameCount`; adding direct SystemDispatcher API; storing managed clock singleton in Gameplay.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged; this removes nondeterministic metadata drift rather than changing visual cost.
Hardware Impact: Runtime impact is one static uint read instead of Unity time call. meaningful gain is rollback trace consistency, not frame time.
Decision 12 - Core Signal Lane Authority Repair
Problem: `PlayerRespawnSignal` existed as contract payload and local producers configured it, but Core did not yet own its direct flush/clear, finite guard, layout validation, or IL2CPP preservation entry. That left route dependent on local fallback registration instead of same explicit GlobalSignals authority used by other first-party lanes.
Solution: Added `PlayerRespawnSignal` to `GlobalSignals` direct pre-simulation flush and post-simulation clear, registered its central capacity through `InitializeCategorySignalLanes`, validated 96-byte payload size, added finite sanitizer for both `double3` AUPs plus phase/collision-frame bounds, added `HectonSignalLaneContract.PlayerRespawnSignal` with stable hash `0x5253504E`, and preserved closed generic lane in `SignalWardenRuntime`. payload now exposes its lane capacity constants so Gameplay and Physiology early-boot calls reuse same numbers instead of hardcoded duplicates.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving lane as fallback-only; adding direct Gameplay-to-Physiology callback; moving signal into sibling runtime assembly; accepting unguarded `double3` AUP payloads.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra consume same bounded lane: expected capacity 8, max frame signals 16, low-tier frame signals 4. quality-dependent cost remains in shader fade and KCC work avoided on respawn frame, not in extra broadcast traffic.
Hardware Impact: Prevents lost or wiped respawn snapshot without increasing steady-state frame work. On low-end silicon, bounded direct lane avoids fallback registry dispatch for this death route and rejects non-finite AUPs before AI/Physics consumers can ingest corrupted data.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Protects first death/recovery loop from signal-routing failure where health resets locally but AI/KCC/physiology consumers never see authoritative respawn packet.
Decision 13 - Visual Sync Phase Discipline
Problem: `PlayerDeathReconciliationBridge` emitted contract signal and also pushed `HectonShaderGlobalDataVaultBridge.PublishRespawnDearLie` immediately from Gameplay. That created second visual route outside `VISUAL_SYNC` and could allocate/initialize shader-global Vault storage from fatal-damage seam if graphics slot buffer was not prewarmed.
Solution: Remove Gameplay shader write. Gameplay now emits only `PlayerRespawnSignal`. first visual cover is authored by `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob` into `RespawnFadeDTO`, then `ShinobuRespawnReconciliationRuntime` publishes Dear Lie scalar during its VisualSync adapter.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping duplicate emergency shader write; adding Gameplay-to-Rendering direct dependency; using UI overlay fallback; forcing shader-global Vault allocation from fatal damage.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra still consume same continuous `GlobalQualityWeight` in fade job and shader. change removes non-authoritative route; it does not reduce visual overkill on high tier.
Hardware Impact: Death detection now performs one bounded signal enqueue and no shader-global DataVault lookup/write. shader scalar update remains in VisualSync, where graphics state belongs.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Prevents first death recovery from mutating rendering state before authoritative Vault reconciliation has accepted respawn request.
Decision 14 - Visual Sync Job Fence Repair
Problem: `VisualSyncTick` read `RespawnFadeDTO` after `PostSimulationTick` attempted non-blocking reclaim, but it did not re-check active job fence. If fade job was still running, VisualSync could read Vault row while Burst still owned writes.
Solution: Add non-blocking fence gate at start of VisualSync. If `_activeHandle` is not completed, VisualSync returns and keeps previous shader scalar. If it is completed, `CompleteActiveJobIfReady(false)` reclaims handle before reading fade row.
Rejected Alternatives: Calling `JobHandle.Complete()` unconditionally in VisualSync; allowing read/write race; duplicating fade state in managed field; publishing Gameplay-phase fallback shader scalar.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. only behavior difference is correctness under slow frame: weak hardware can skip VisualSync publish instead of stalling main thread.
Hardware Impact: Prevents main-thread block and native data race. In overloaded frames cost is one `IsCompleted` branch and no shader-global write until job fence is safe.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Protects death recovery visuals from stale or half-written fade values during early survival loop.
Decision 15 - Cross-Frame Writer Fence Repair
Problem: `ScheduleSimulation` could start new reset/fade job over same Vault pointers while previous frame's `_activeHandle` was still in flight. VisualSync was protected, but simulation producer could still stack two writers to `RespawnStateDTO`/`RespawnFadeDTO` rows.
Solution: Gate `ScheduleSimulation` on `_jobScheduled`. If prior handle is incomplete, return `JobHandle.CombineDependencies(dependsOn, _activeHandle)` and do not schedule another writer. If it is complete, reclaim it non-blockingly and then schedule next job.
Rejected Alternatives: Completing old job unconditionally in Simulation; allowing overlapping writers; copying state into second private buffer; adding managed queue of pending deaths.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged; overloaded devices naturally skip one respawn/fade update rather than blocking or racing.
Hardware Impact: Avoids false sharing/data races on Vault rows with one branch and one combined dependency in rare slow-job case. No new persistent memory is allocated.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Prevents repeated lethal events during early survival from corrupting active respawn row while previous reconciliation is still executing.
Decision 16 - Deterministic Frame Source Sweep
Problem: Static verification still found Unity `Time.frameCount` in health/survival signal payloads adjacent to lethal physiology traffic. `PlayerRespawnSignal` was already dispatcher-stamped, but `SurvivalVitalsChangedSignal` on death and physiology/vital warning freshness were still in Unity frame space.
Solution: Replace those frame stamps and freshness delta with `TimeSliceScheduler.CurrentFrameId`, dispatcher frame source already used by respawn bridge.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving Unity frame metadata around death route; adding new clock service; changing signal payload layouts; touching unrelated gameplay time users outside SHINOBU's health/survival files.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. value is deterministic trace coherence under rollback and black-box replay, not visual fidelity.
Hardware Impact: Static uint read cost is equivalent or cheaper than Unity frame access. important gain is removal of rollback drift source from lethal survival telemetry.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Keeps first death/recovery loop's vitals, physiology, and respawn signals in one frame domain for post-mortem correlation.
Decision 17 - Compile Wall Boundary
Problem: After CPU/process guard passed, `dotnet build Hecton8.Core.csproj --no-restore` failed before SHINOBU code on `CS2001` because `Assets/_Project/Scripts/Construction/LogisticsPipeEvents.cs` is deleted while still referenced by generated project.
Solution: Treat this as unrelated compile wall and do not create construction-domain stub or mutate generated project file. Continue static verification and record exact blocker for integrator.
Rejected Alternatives: Fabricating missing Construction file; editing `Hecton8.Core.csproj` by hand; rerunning build repeatedly against same missing source; reverting another agent's deletion.
Scalability potential: Runtime tier behavior unchanged. This is integration hygiene, not SHINOBU feature logic.
Hardware Impact: Prevents wasted compile loops. Runtime impact 0 us.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: respawn route cannot receive compile proof until construction source/project reference is reconciled.
Decision 18 - Cached Vault Authority Tightening
Problem: `ShinobuRespawnReconciliationRuntime.ResolveVault()` could be called from dispatcher phases and would fall back to `GlobalRegistry.DataVault` if `_dataVault` was null. That violates cold-discovery rule and hides missing boot wiring behind hot-path service polling.
Solution: Split route: dispatcher phases use cached `_dataVault` only and fail closed when absent; `ResolveVaultCold()` retains `GlobalRegistry`/latest-Vault fallback for Awake, Start, hot-swap/editor utilities, and gizmos.
Rejected Alternatives: Polling `GlobalRegistry` in PreSimulation/Simulation/VisualSync; storing private NativeArrays as fallback; direct construction of local Vault; throwing exceptions on missing Vault.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. Weak devices avoid possible cold service lookup branch in death/fade ticks.
Hardware Impact: Hot path removes service locator fallback. Estimated saving is tiny per tick, but real gain is architectural: no hidden global lookup in deterministic dispatcher phases.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: Death recovery now either runs on boot-injected Vault or fails closed with no scene reload/object churn.
Decision 19 - Legacy Managed Death Event Ejection
Problem: Reconciled deaths still invoked legacy managed `OnDeath` listeners before local reset. `HectonSurvivalSystem.OnDeath` currently reaches PDA logbook code and can create UI/logbook side effects inside fatal frame, conflicting with zero-GC reconciliation mandate.
Solution: Reconciled deaths return immediately after signal emission and local scalar reset. Managed `OnDeath`, `PlayerDiedEvent`, and development log fallback remain only for unreconciled failure path.
Rejected Alternatives: Publishing `PlayerDiedEvent` for reconciled death; keeping PDA logbook side effects in fatal frame; adding direct PDA callback; allocating replacement managed event.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. Death truth is now signal/Vault black box; presentation is shader-driven.
Hardware Impact: Removes managed delegate fan-out and PDA/meta side effects from reconciled death frame. Exact GC delta requires Unity Profiler, but code path no longer calls known `OnDeath` subscriber on successful reconciliation.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first lethal survival event no longer risks dragging journal/meta systems into one-frame respawn path.
Decision 20 - Current-Frame Respawn Snapshot Repair
Problem: Gameplay can only publish lethal request immediately, so first `PlayerRespawnSignal` starts with `RespawnAUP = DeathAUP`. Physiology resolves actual med-bay AUP later in `PreSimulation`. If that resolved target is only stored in Vault or republished as queued signal, same-frame Physics/AI consumers can see stale death AUP or wait one frame.
Solution: Keep Physiology as sole med-bay resolver, then mutate current `SignalBus ` snapshot in-place with `SignalBus .TransformSnapshot`. transformer writes resolved `RespawnAUP`, `MedicalBayHashID`, `Requested`, `Committed`, `SuspendCollision`, translated med-bay flags, and clamps `SuspendCollisionFrames` to payload maximum. `HydrodynamicKccRuntime` now treats request or committed respawn packets as eligible, while snapshot-generation latch preserves one-frame collision bypass.
Rejected Alternatives: Queueing second committed signal for next frame; making Gameplay query med-bay Vault state; adding direct Physiology-to-Physics call; keeping KCC dependent on producer's original `Requested` bit only; leaving `math.max(byte, byte)` in transformer.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged for simulation truth. Same-frame correction prevents visual/physics pop on weak devices and lets high-tier Dear Lie shader spend more time on presentation instead of covering avoidable stale-collision frame.
Hardware Impact: Adds O(snapshotCount) unmanaged value-transform over lane capped at 16 events per frame; expected cost is below 1 us on i3/MX350 for normal 0-1 death packet traffic. Avoids one extra frame of stale capsule collision and queued duplicate signal.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death/recovery loop now gives KCC and mesofauna resolved med-bay AUP in same frame request is accepted, without loading screen or object churn.
Decision 21 - Kinematic Sector Denominator Guard
Problem: `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob.WriteKinematic()` divided target AUP by `HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble`. project contract expects that constant to be valid, but NaN mandate requires every division feeding physics truth to be guarded locally.
Solution: Clamp denominator with `math.max(HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble, 0.0001d)` before calculating sector. existing local-position math then subtracts guarded sector root and casts only local residual to `float3`.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting global contract constant without local guard; moving sector split to managed code; using `Transform.position`; adding exception checks in Burst path.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. This is correctness hardening, not visual cost. It prevents single bad constant or corrupted contract payload from poisoning KCC/rollback state.
Hardware Impact: One `math.max` in rare respawn job. Expected cost is below measurement noise on i3/MX350 and buys NaN containment for physics truth.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death recovery cannot poison player kinematic row through zero sector-size denominator.
Decision 22 - Local AUP Clamp Range Guard
Problem: After sector-division fix, `SafeLocal()` and runtime `AupDeltaToFloat3()` still used `HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble` directly as clamp range. It is not division, but if that constant were corrupted to zero or non-finite, local validation vectors could collapse or propagate invalid values before fallback path.
Solution: Add `SafeAupClampMeters()` in Burst job file and runtime file, each returning `math.max(HectonPhysicsContract.AupSectorSizeMetersDouble, 0.0001d)`. Local AUP residual conversion and medical-bay validation now use guarded range before casting to `float3`.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting contract constant in clamp helpers; duplicating raw `math.max` calls at each clamp site; moving validation into managed `Vector3` math; widening patch into unrelated AUP systems.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. This is deterministic containment; visual overkill budget stays in Dear Lie shader.
Hardware Impact: One double `math.max` per local conversion helper call on rare respawn/validation path. Expected cost is below measurement noise on i3/MX350; gain is preventing bad clamp range from poisoning target validation or rollback kinematic truth.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first lethal recovery route now protects both sector split and local validation clamp before med-bay AUP selection reaches Physics/Fauna consumers.
Decision 23 - Med-Bay Authority De-Duplication
Problem: `ShinobuRespawnReconciliationRuntime` already resolves med-bay target in `PreSimulation`, writes `RespawnStateDTO`, and transforms current `PlayerRespawnSignal` snapshot. `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob` then repeated same nearest-med-bay scan as its primary route, creating two target-selection authorities in one death frame.
Solution: Keep `PreSimulation` as owner of med-bay resolution. `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob` now consumes staged `RespawnStateDTO.TargetAUP` and `MedicalBayHashID` when staged state is pending, finite, and either has med-bay hash or explicit fallback flag. Staged route flags are applied only when staged target is accepted; fallback scan recomputes mock/invalid/fallback flags itself so stale state cannot leak into new death request. committed request row now preserves `MockMedicalBay` along with invalid/fallback/penalty flags for black-box correlation. job scans `MedicalBayRespawnPointDTO` rows only as fail-closed fallback when staged state is missing or invalid.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving duplicate med-bay scans as "harmless"; moving med-bay selection into Gameplay; expanding `RespawnRequestDTO` layout to carry another target copy; adding direct Base Logistics dependency to job; deleting fallback scan and making job brittle under boot/order failures.
Scalability potential: Low removes redundant Burst work from death frame while keeping deterministic fallback. Middle/High/Ultra keep same authoritative target and spend saved CPU budget on Dear Lie shader, not on second simulation truth lookup.
Hardware Impact: Normal death path removes one O(medBayCount) scan from `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob`; with current capacity this is up to 8 row reads and AUP local-distance evaluations avoided on i3/MX350. Fallback path remains bounded and only runs on missing/non-finite staged state.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death/recovery loop now has one med-bay owner in accepted frame, reducing chance of Physics/Fauna seeing target chosen by one path while Kinematic truth is chosen by another.
Decision 24 - Hot-Path Literal New Erasure
Problem: respawn path had no managed gameplay allocations, but `new` value-type/object-initializer syntax remained in Burst jobs, Simulation job scheduling, VisualSync shader payload publishing, cold DTO defaults, and helper return paths. That creates bad review evidence and can hide unnecessary struct construction/copy patterns in exact files that must be trivially memcpy/Burst-readable.
Solution: Rewrite SHINOBU job bodies and hot dispatcher code to `default` locals with explicit field assignment. `ResetPlayerPhysiologyJob`, `UpdateRespawnFadeJob`, VisualSync `Vector4`, `RespawnFadeDTO`, `InventoryDeathPenaltyRuleDTO`, fallback `double3`, local `float3`, editor gizmo offsets, and telemetry/physiology DTO writes now avoid literal `new` syntax. Remaining `new` sites are cold and explicit: one runtime host GameObject, four dispatcher adapter objects, cold FileStream/BinaryWriter dump/CSV IO, stack-only `Span ` constructor, and teardown/service-replacement `JobHandle.Complete()` fences.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating value-type `new` as harmless and leaving noisy hot-path evidence; adding managed pools for structs; removing cold runtime host without proving another dispatcher owner exists; replacing teardown `Complete()` with unsafe native-buffer release while job may still own pointers.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged in behavior. low-tier benefit is tighter Burst/codegen hygiene and fewer false positives in allocation scans; high/ultra keep same VisualSync shader overkill route.
Hardware Impact: No measured microsecond saving is claimed from syntax alone. important i3/MX350 impact is risk removal: job scheduling, shader payload publish, and Burst DTO writes now have no literal `new` evidence, and static scans can distinguish hot path from cold boot/editor IO.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first death/recovery loop now has cleaner zero-GC proof surface: lethal request -> Vault reconciliation -> shader Dear Lie publish uses explicit unmanaged value mutation, not initializer syntax that can be misread as allocation.
Decision 25 - Death-Vicinity Signal Initializer And Pack Purge
Problem: After SHINOBU respawn files were cleaned, adjacent health/survival code still published mutable GlobalSignals via object-initializer `new`, and `SurvivalDatabaseItemRecord` used `[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential, Pack = 1, Size = 20)]`. signal initializers are value-type syntax rather than heap allocation, but they weaken zero-GC evidence in fatal-damage vicinity. `Pack=1` is direct ARM64 alignment violation even if row is cold parsed.
Solution: Rewrite `VitalWarningSignal`, `PhysiologyStateSignal`, and `SurvivalVitalsChangedSignal` publishers to `default` plus field assignment in `HectonPlayerHealth`, `HectonSurvivalSystem`, and `ShinobuPhysiologyRuntime`. Replace `SurvivalDatabaseItemRecord` with explicit 24-byte layout: `StableHash` offset 0, `MassKilograms` 4, `VolumeLiters` 8, `EnergyDensityMegajoulesPerKilogram` 12, `BaseDurability` 16, `_pad0` 20.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving `Pack=1` because row is cold; broad-refactoring readonly `TraumaHudSignal` constructors in HUD event lane; changing survival database parser contract; adding new DTO type and forcing downstream copies.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra unchanged. fix removes alignment risk and noisy signal construction evidence without changing visual quality or survival tuning.
Hardware Impact: `SurvivalDatabaseItemRecord` grows from 20 to 24 bytes, 20% cold staging-row increase for 256-row cap, but removes unaligned ARM64 row reads. Mutable signal publish cost remains equivalent and cleaner for Burst/IL2CPP inspection.
First 20 Minutes Route Impact: first lethal survival loop now has no mutable GlobalSignal object-initializer `new` in health/survival death-adjacent publishers and no `Pack=1` row in survival data parser used by same component.
